Recognition of the alfa romeo code When the control unit receives the ignition 'ON' signal, it dialogues with the Body Computer through the Alfa Romeo CODE function to obtain starting enablement. Control of the fuel temperature With the temperature of the fuel at 80° C , measured by the sensor at the recirculation manifold, the control unit operates the pressure regulator in order to reduce the line pressure (it does not modify the injection times). Control of the engine coolant temperature With the temperature of the engine coolant greater than 105° C, the control unit: reduces the quantity of fuel injected (reduces the engine power); operates the cooling fans; lights up the coolant overheating warning light. Control of the quantity of fuel injected On the basis of the signals coming from the sensors and the values in the map, the control unit: it operates the pressure regulator; varies the 'pilot' injection time throughout the entire rev range; varies the 'main' injection time. Control of the idle speed The control unit processes the signals coming from the various sensors and regulates the quantity of fuel injected: it operates the pressure regulator; it varies the injector injection time. Within certain limits the speed takes the battery voltage into account. Fuel cut-off during overrunning When the accelerator pedal is released the following logics are implemented: it cuts off the supply to the fuel injectors; partial reactivation of the supply to the injectors before the idle speed is reached; it operates the fuel pressure regulator. Control of cylinder balance up to 3500 rpm On the basis of the signals received from the sensors, the control unit controls the precision of the torque up to 3500 rpm.: it varies the quantity of fuel injected in the individual injectors (injection time). Control of irregular operation The control unit processes the signals received from the various sensors and corrects the quantity of fuel to be injected in order to improve driveability, reducing jerks during driving through the injector opening time. Control of the exhaust fumes during acceleration In order to limit smoke during fast transitions, the control unit, on the basis of the signals received from the accelerator pedal potentiometer, flow meter and engine rpm, limits the quantity of fuel to be injected via: the pressure regulator the injection time of the fuel injectors. Control of the exhaust gas recirculation (e.g.r.) In accordance with EURO 3 anti-pollution regulations, the control unit, on the basis of the engine load and signal coming from the accelerator pedal potentiometer, limits the quantity of fresh air drawn in, implementing the partial intake of exhaust gases, via: regulating the opening of the electric E.G.R. valve. Control of the maximum torque restriction According to the number of revs, the control unit calculates the following from predefined maps: the torque limit; the permissible fumes (limit). It compares these minimum values and corrects them with other parameters: coolant temperature; engine rpm; vehicle speed; intake air temperature obtained from the built in air temperature/excess pressure sensor, and controls the quantity of fuel to be injected (pressure regulator - injectors). Control of the maximum speed limit When the engine reaches 5000 rpm, the control unit interrupts the operation of the injectors and consequently the supply pressure is reduced. Control of the heater plugs The control unit, during the following stages: starting; post-starting times the operation of the plug preheater control unit according to the engine temperature. Control of entry into operation of the air conditioning system The control unit operates the air conditioning compressor: switching it on/off when the relevant switch is pressed; switching it off momentarily (for around 6 s) if there is substantial acceleration or a request for maximum power. Control of the auxiliary electric fuel pump Irrespective of the engine speed, the control unit: supplies the auxiliary fuel pump with the ignition key in the ON position; excludes the auxiliary pump supply if the engine is not started up within a few seconds. Control of the position of the cylinders During each revolution of the engine, the control unit recognizes which cylinder is in the explosion stroke and operates the injection sequence at the appropriate cylinder. Control of the main injection and pilot injection advance On the basis of the signals coming from the various sensors, including the absolute pressure sensor in the actual control unit, the control unit determines the optimum injection point according to an internal map, not only in relation to driving comfort, but also in accordance with EURO 3 emission limits. Control of closed loop injection pressure On the basis of the engine load, determined by processing the signals coming from the various sensors, the control unit operates the regulator to obtain optimum line pressure. Control of the electrical balance According to the battery voltage, the control unit varies the idle speed: it increases the injector injection time; it regulates the line pressure. Control of vgt variable geometry turbine At the various engine operating speeds, the control unit processes the signal coming from the supercharging sensor and determines the quantity of fuel to be injected: it varies the injection time; it regulates the geometry of the turbine in order to optimise performance under all operating conditions. Control of the electric fans The control unit, in accordance with the coolant temperature and pressure of the refrigerant in the air conditioning system, controls: the switching on of the fans at the first or second speed. Control of butterfly closure on switching off In order to limit engine shake during switching off, the control unit controls the immediate closure of the butterfly at intake. Under all other operating conditions, the butterfly remains open. Control of cruise control system (where fitted) According to the position of the cruise control lever, the control unit directly controls the quantity of fuel injected to control and maintain the vehicle speed memorized. A warning light in the dashboard, activated by the control unit, indicates whether the system is operating or not. The cruise control is momentarily disabled: by operating the brake, by operating the clutch; the resume button restores the speed memorized. The cruise control is not disabled if there is an acceleration request (e.g. overtaking) and the vehicle automatically returns to the speed set as soon as the accelerator is released. The ASR function (anti-spin) has priority over the cruise control for safety reasons. Injectors They are fitted on the cylinder head and operated by the injection control unit. The injectors can be divided into two sections: actuator/nozzle consisting of a pressure rod (1), pin (2) and jet (3) solenoid valve consisting of a coil (4) and valve (5). Operation The operation of the injector can be divided into three stages: rest position The coil (4) is de-energized and the shutter (6) is in the closed position and does not allow the introduction of fuel into cylinder Fc > Fa (Fc: due to the line pressure acting on control area 7 of the rod 1; Fa: due to the line pressure acting in supply volume (8). "start of injection" The coil (4) is energized and causes the shutter (6) to be raised. The control volume (9) fuel flows towards the return manifold (10) causing a decrease in pressure in the control area (7). At the same time, the line pressure exerts a force Fa > Fc in the supply volume (8), via the supply duct (12), causing the raising of the pin (2) with the consequent introduction of fuel into the cylinders. "end of injection" The coil (4) is de-energized and returns the shutter (6) to the closed position which recreates an equilibrium with forces which return the pin (2) to the closed position and consequently end the injection. 1, Pressure rod 2, Pin 3, Jet 4, Coil 5, Pilot Valve 6, Spherical shutter 7, Control area 8, Supply volume 9, Control volume 10, Fuel return - low pressure 11, Control duct 12, Supply duct 13, Electrical connection 14, Fuel inlet connector - high pressure 15, Spring Supply manifold (Rail) The supply manifold is fitted on the inlet side cylinder head. With its volume of around 33 cc it dampens the fuel pressure oscillations due to: the operation of the pressure pump the opening of the injectors. The fuel pressure sensor (see 1060G) is fitted at the centre of the supply manifold. The (high pressure) hydraulic connections between the manifold-pump and manifold-injectors are made by means of steel pipes with an internal diameter of 2 mm and an external diameter of 6 mm. The injectors can be divided into two sections: actuator/nozzle consisting of a pressure rod (1), pin (2) and jet (3) solenoid valve consisting of a coil (4) and pilot valve (5). The operation of the injector can be divided into three stages. REST POSITION. The coil (4) is de-energized and the shutter (6) is in the closed position and does not allow the introduction of fuel into cylinder Fc > Fa (Fc: due to the line pressure acting on control area 7 of the rod 1; Fa: due to the line pressure acting in supply volume (8). START OF INJECTION, the coil (4) is energized and causes the shutter (6) to be raised. The control volume (9) fuel flows towards the return manifold (10) causing a decrease in pressure in the control area (7). At the same time, the line pressure exerts a force Fa > Fc in the supply volume (8), via the supply duct (12), causing the raising of the pin (2) with the consequent introduction of fuel into the cylinders. This pulley comprises a gap which enables the timing sensor to indicate the engine's timing position. The fuel injection control unit uses the timing sensor's signal to find out the TDC at the end of compression. Operation A semiconducting layer, through which current passes, immersed in a perpendicular magnetic field (force lines perpendicular to the current direction), generates at its ends a difference in potential known as Hall voltage. If the intensity of the current remains constant, the voltage generated only depends on the intensity of the magnetic field; the intensity of the field simply has to vary periodically to produce a modulated electrical signal, whose frequency is proportional to the speed with which it changes magnetic field. To obtain this change, a metal ring (the inside of the pulley) with a gap passes through the sensor. As it moves, the metal part of the ring covers the sensor, blocking the magnetic field, resulting in a low output signal; viceversa, level with the gap and so when the magnetic field is present, the sensor generate a high signal. This signal, together with the rpm and TDC signal, allows the control unit to recognize the cylinders and determine the injection point. 1, Pulley ring 2, Magnetic material Pressure relief sensor It is fitted at the centre of the inlet chamber and has the task of notifying the injection control unit to: regulating the injection pressure regulating the injection duration. Operation The operating principle is based on a heated diaphragm located in a measuring duct through which the intake air entering the engine flows. The hot film diaphragm is kept at a constant temperature (about 120° C above the incoming air temperature) by the heating resistor. The air mass passing through the measuring duct tends to draw heat from the diaphragm, so to keep the latter at a constant temperature, some current must flow through the resistor. This current is measured by a suitable Wheatstone bridge. The current is therefore proportional to the mass of flowing air. The flow meter directly measures the air mass (not volume), thus eliminating problems of temperature, altitude, pressure, etc. For operating checks, see test . An NTC thermistor sends the signal to the engine management control unit which sends the signal for the indicator and the warning light in the instrument panel. The sensor is based on semiconductor technology; so if the sensor temperature increases as the water temperature increases, the resistance decreases. as the variation in resistance is not linear, for the same temperature increment, it is higher for low temperatures than for high temperatures. AIR FLOW METER WITH AIR TEMPERATURE SENSOR INTEGRATED Specifcations Type The flow meter is located on the air inlet duct and is of the 'hot film' type. The intake air temperature sensor is built into the flow meter. The air flow meter cannot be dismantled. Operation The operating principle is based on a heated diaphragm located in a measuring duct through which the intake air entering the engine flows. The hot film diaphragm is kept at a constant temperature (about 120° C above the incoming air temperature) by the heating resistor. The air mass passing through the measuring duct tends to draw heat from the diaphragm, so to keep the latter at a constant temperature, some current must flow through the resistor. This current is measured by a suitable Wheatstone bridge. The current is therefore proportional to the mass of flowing air. The flow meter directly measures the air mass (not volume), thus eliminating problems of temperature, altitude, pressure, etc. Fuel temperature sensor Specifications It is built into the fuel heater and measures the temperature of the coolant by means of an NTC thermistor which has a negative resistance coefficient. The sensor is based on semiconductor technology; so if the sensor temperature increases as the fuel temperature increases, the resistance decreases. As the variation in resistance is not linear, for the same temperature increment, it is higher for low temperatures than for high temperatures. The engine control unit implements the following recovery strategies: if there is a fault with one of the two potentiometers, a throttle opening of up to 40° is allowed for a long period if both of the potentiometers fail completely, the throttle opening is excluded. Operation Introduction The sensor consists of a casing, fixed to the pedals by bolts, which contains a shaft, in an axial position, connected to the two potentiometers. There is a coil spring on the shaft which guarantees the correct resistance to the pressure whilst a second spring ensure the return on release. Operating range from 0° to 70°; mechanical stop at 88°. if one of the two potentiometers or both of them are broken, the accelerator pedal should be replaced in one piece because it cannot be dismantled.

COMPONENT DESCRIPTION TURBOCHARGER (GARRET A/R.53) Specifcations It has variable geometry and is connected to the exhaust manifold; its purpose is to increase the volumetric output of the engine. This variable geometry turbocharger consists of: a centrifugal compressor a turbine a series of moving vanes a pneumatic actuator for operating the moving vanes. The operation of the turbocharger's variable geometry is managed by the control unit via the control of the VGT solenoid. 1. Engine management control unit 2. VGT solenoid 3. Vacuum reservoir 4. Moving vane actuator 5. Turbocharger This variable geometry turbocharger makes it possible to: increase the speed of the exhaust gases in the turbine at low engine speeds; slow down the speed of the exhaust gases in the turbine at high speeds. Controlling the speed (kinetic energy) of the exhaust gases makes it possible to produce: greater engine torque at low speeds; greater maximum power at high speeds. Operation at high rotation speeds If the engine rotation speed increases, the kinetic energy of the exhaust gases also gradually increases. As a result the speed of the turbine (1) increases and consequently the supercharging pressure which also acts on the actuator (3). The actuator (3), controlled by the solenoid, operates the opening of the moving vanes (2) via a rod, until the fully open position is reached. There is therefore an increase in the sections and consequently a slowing down in the flow of the exhaust gases passing through the turbine (1) at speeds which are the same as or lower than those for the low speed conditions. The speed of the turbine (1) decreases and settles down at a suitable rate for the correct operation of the engine at high speeds. 1. Turbine 2. Moving vanes 3. Pneumatic actuator 4. Rotary ring Operation at low rotation speeds When the engine rotation speed is low, the exhaust gases possess little kinetic energy: under these circumstances, a conventional turbine would rotate slowly, supplying a limited supercharging pressure. In a variable geometry turbine (1), on the other hand, the moving vanes (2) are in the maximum closure position and the small sections between the vanes increase the speed (C) of the intake gases. Increased intake speeds result in greater peripheral speeds (U) for the turbine and consequently the compressor. The speed of the gases inside the impeller is shown by the vector (W). 1. Turbine 2. Moving vanes 3. Pneumatic actuator 4. Rotary ring

MODULAR INTAKE MANIFOLD It is an inlet manifold of modular length managed by the engine management control unit; it allows the volumetric efficiency to be increased, and so: improving the torque supply at low-medium speeds increasing the power at high speeds. The manifold consists of: two nylon half shells an internal oscillating pipe a vacuum accumulator inside the manifold an actuator controlling the modular intake device, with a built-in three-way solenoid. Operation The fuel injection control unit controls the three-way solenoid (1) which places the vacuum accumulator (2) in communication with the pneumatic actuator (3), which in turn, via a linkage, allows the oscillating pipe (4) to move. The rotation of the oscillating pipe allows the pipes to assume the configurations of short power pipes with rpm up to 2800 rpm and over 5200 rpm long torque pipes with rpm from 2800 to 5200 rpm. SWITCHING DEVICE CONTROL ACTUATOR ENABLEMENT SOLENOID This is a three-way solenoid valve integrated in the pneumatic inlet manifold actuator and is operated by the injection control unit. Its function is to allow the vacuum present in the vacuum tank (inside the modular intake manifold) to act on the pneumatic actuator which controls the oscillating pipe. 1 - Enablement solenoid for changeover device actuator 2 - Modular intake control actuator 3 - Vaccum intake pipe 4 - Atmospheric presure air intake

Lambda sensor It is mounted on the front section of the exhaust pipe, and it informs the control unit about the combustion trend (stoichiometric ratio). To obtain an optimum mixture, the quantity of air drawn in by the engine is the same as the theoretical quantity that would be needed to burn all the injected fuel. In this case the Lambda factor (?), the ratio between the quantity of air drawn in and the theoretical quantity of air (needed to burn all the injected fuel), is 1. Thus: ? = 1 ideal mixture ? > 1 lean mixture ? < 1 rich mixture a, Rich mixture (too little air) b, Lean mixture (too much air) The Lambda probe, placed in contact with the exhaust gases, generates an electrical signal whose voltage depends on the concentration of oxygen present in the gases. This voltage undergoes a sudden variation when the composition of the mixture moves away from ? = 1. 1, Ceramic body 2, Protective tube 3, Metal body 4, Electrical resistor A, Ceramic inner part B, Ceramic outer part For operating checks. See Test 1080B Checking Lambda sensor Catalytic converter The three-way catalytic converter simultaneously reduces the three polluting gases present in the exhaust gases: unburnt hydrocarbons (HC); carbon monoxide (CO); nitrogen oxides (NOx). Two types of chemical reactions take place in the converter: oxidation of the CO and HC, converted into carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O) reduction of the NOx converted into nitrogen (N2). The converter consists of a monolith, a metal mesh support for damping impacts and vibrations and an outer stainless steel housing resistent to high temperatures and atmospheric agents. The monolith consists of a honeycomb structure comprising a ceramic material coated with a very thin layer of catalytically active substances, platinum or rodium. These accelerate the chemical decomposition of the harmful substances contained in the exhaust gases which, passing through the core cells at temperatures of over 300°-350° C, activate the catalyzers, thus starting the oxidoreduction reactions. To optimze the efficiency and duration of the catalyzer, a perforated plate metal cone improves the diffusion of the exhaust gases in the cells of the ceramic core. 1, Ceramic monolith 2, Metal support 3, Outer casing 4, Perforated plate metal cone The noble metals contained in the catalytic converter, because of the high temperature, are chemically attacked if lead is present. For this reason the use of petrols containing lead should be avoided, otherwise the converter will be quickly and irreversibly damaged. Never use petrol containing lead, not even in an emergency or for a very short time. CONSTRUCTION FEATURES Lambda probe Of the 'planar' type, it is mounted on the front section of the exhaust pipe, and it informs the control unit about the combustion trend (stoichiometric ratio). On the exhaust system, there are two Lambda probes upstream of the catalytic converter (fitted on the catalytic preconverter) and one Lambda probe downstream of the catalytic converter (fitted on the converter). For the logic of management of the signals coming from the Lambda probes Characteristic of working principle 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The electronic control unit identifies the composition of the mixture (rich or lean) from the Lambda sensor output voltage. It adjusts the quantity of fuel injected to ensure the optimum composition of the mixture (l = 1) to create the ideal conditions for the treatment of the exhaust gases in the catalytic converter. If the mixture is too rich (lambda less than 1), then the quantity of fuel should be reduced and, if the mixture is too lean (lambda greater than 1), then the quantity of fuel should be increased. a, Rich mixture (lack of air) b, Weak mixture (too much air) The Lambda sensor, placed in contact with the exhaust gases, generates an electrical signal whose voltage depends on the concentration of oxygen present in the gases. This voltage is characterized by a sudden change when the composition of the mixture moves away from Lambda = 1. The heating of the Lambda sensor is managed by the fuel injection control unit in relation to the exhaust gas temperature. This avoids thermal shocks on the ceramic casing due to the contact with condensed water, present in the exhaust gases when the engine is cold. The measuring cell and heater are built into the 'planar' (stratified) ceramic element, with the advantage of obtaining quick heating of the cell, thus permitting a closed loop' check (Lambda = 1) within 10 seconds of engine start-up. 1, Connecting cable 2, Protective sleeve 3, Planar sensor element 4, Ceramic tube casing 5, Probe seating 6, Ceramic seal 7, Protective tube The operation of the Lambda sensor is based on the principle of an oxygen concentration cell with solid electrolyte. The system is equipped with an E.G.R. valve (1) in order to reduce the NOx (nitrogen oxide) emissions still further. The E.G.R. (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) valve carries out the function of taking some of the exhaust gases and returning them to the inlet chamber (2). The E.G.R. valve is operated by the vaccum modulated by the solenoid valve (3) controlled by the injection control unit. Vacuum modulator solenoid Operation The vacuum arrives at chamber E from duct F (case I) because the force of the spring (6) acts on the moving element (4) and the deviation valve (5) allows it to pass. The vacuum then reaches chamber B and the surface of the shutter (3), via the compensation port D. When the forces acting on the disc (3) are balanced, the atmospheric pressure in duct A enters chamber B, moving the moving element downwards (case II) therefore the valve (5) shutter closes duct F and places chamber E in contact with chamber C, which is at atmospheric pressure, decreasing the value of the vacuum in duct E. The decreased vacuum value or the increased absolute pressure in chamber E raises the moving element (4) again (case I), closing port C and placing the valve (5) in the ideal condition (E in contact with F) and the cycle is repeated. For operating checks see test . See Test 1080C Check on operation of E.G.R valve modulator. OPERATION The system is equipped with an E.G.R. valve (1) in order to reduce the NOx (nitrogen oxide) emissions still further. The E.G.R. valve is controlled by the fuel injection control unit, and carries out the function of re-injecting into the engine intake some of the exhaust gases drawn from the exhaust manifold. A heat exchanger (3) permit partial cooling of the exhaust gases, increasing the volumetric output of the engine. 1 - E.G.R. valve 2 - Engine control unit 3 - Heat exchanger 4 - Exhaust manifold 5 - Throttle body CONSTRUCTION FEATURES This system directs a proportion of exhaust gases (5 - 15%) to the intake under certain service conditions. This lowers the temperature peak in the combustion chamber to reduce the formation of nitrogen oxides (NOx). The E.G.R. valve (1) is controlled by the fuel injection control unit (2), and carries out the function of re-injecting into the engine intake some of the exhaust gases drawn from the exhaust manifold (4). A heat exchanger (3) allows the partial cooling of the exhaust gases, further lowering the temperature in the combustion chamber. 1 - E.G.R. valve 2 - Fuel injection control unit 3 - Heat exchanger 4 - Exhaust manifold 5 - Throttle body OPERATION The fuel injection control unit, with coolant temperature > 20° C and engine speed of between 800 and 3000 rpm, drives the E.G.R. solenoid with a square-wave signal. The change in this signal allows the EGR coil to move a plunger and thus adjust the flow of burnt gases from the exhaust manifold to the intake manifold; two results are thus obtained: less air is introduced; combustion temperature is reduced (due to the presence of inert gases) to reduce NOx (nitrogen oxide) production. The engine control unit is kept constantly informed of recirculated gas quantity by information from the flow meter. If the intake of a certain amount of air (Qam) rpm is required at a certain rpm and the amount sent by the flow meter (Qar) is less, the difference (Qgr) is the recirculated gas quantity. The vapours coming from the tank through the two multi-purpose valves (1) are sent to the separator (2). The condensed vapours in the separator fall back into the tank. Uncondensed vapours are sent through the pipe (3) to the canister (4), where they are absorbed and stored by the activated charcoal. The vapours pass to the inlet box through the solenoid (5) controlled by the fuel injection unit. Multi-function valves The functions of the two multi-purpose valves are: pressurization of the tank retaining seal in the event of roll-over Pressurizing the tank The tank is maintained at a pressure of 30-45 mbar by means of a fluorosilicone rubber valve, which rests on a sealing edge. The valve is supported by a stainless steel plate and counteracted by a spring. When the pressure in the tank exceeds the specified value, it overcomes the resistance of the spring and the valve is able to rise, allowing vapours to flow to the canister. When the pressure returns to the correct limits, the valve closes again. Retaining Under particular driving conditions, a vacuum could be created in the tank because of: temperature changes fuel consumption. In this case, the valve's function is to restore the pressure of the tank by allowing air in. A fault in this function could cause the engine to miss or stall, because of difficulties in supplying the fuel pump. This function is carried out by the "goose beak" valve formed directly out of the fluorosilicone rubber. Seal in the event of roll-over The roll-over function prevents fuel from leaking from the tank if the vehicle overturns or is on a very steep slope. During normal driving of the vehicle (bends, acceleration, braking, etc.), the fuel is shaken up and may spill into the canister. The high sensitivity of the roll-over prevents this spillage. The roll-over closure angle is less than 33°. Canister Mounted in the front right wheelarch, this consists of an activated-charcoal filter element which absorbs the fuel vapours coming from the separator. Multi-function valves The functions of the two multi-purpose valves are: pressurizing the tank ventilating the tank retention seal in the event of roll-over The multifunction valve can be removed from the separator and a Viton gasket ensures an effective seal. Pressurizing the tank The tank is maintained at a pressure of 30-45 mbar by means of a fluorosilicone rubber valve, which rests on a sealing edge. The valve is supported by a stainless steel plate and counteracted by a spring. When the pressure in the tank exceeds the specified value, it overcomes the resistance of the spring and the valve is able to rise, allowing vapours to flow to the canister. When the pressure returns to the correct limits, the valve closes again. In this case, the valve's function is to restore the pressure of the tank by allowing air in. A fault in this function could cause the engine to miss or stall, because of difficulties in supplying the fuel pump. This function is carried out by a goose beak valve located on the multi-purpose valves. Seal in the event of roll-over The roll-over function prevents fuel from leaking from the tank if the vehicle overturns or is on a very steep slope. During normal driving of the vehicle (bends, acceleration, braking, etc.), the fuel is shaken up and may spill into the canister. The car's high roll-over sensitivity prevents this spillage. A conventional manual transmission (single dry clutch plate and synchronised C.510.5 gearbox) is connected to an electronically-controlled hydraulic device that manages the clutch and gear shifts. 1, Hydraulic unit 2, Electric pump 3, Fluid reservoir 4, Gear selector lever 5, Speed selection buttons 6, Electronic control unit (CFC 202F) This use of this system does not impose any changes to the clutch and internal gearbox mechanism. The clutch pedal has been eliminated and car take-off is achieved by means of the accelerator pedal alone. The gearbox can work in two operating modes: semiautomatic, manual, when the driver requests gear changes by operating a lever on the central console or buttons on the steering wheel; automatic, known as 'CITY' where the system decides when to shift gear. The advantages of this type of system are as follows: the driver no longer needs to operate the clutch pedal and gear lever but can still enjoy all the driving satisfaction that comes from direct control of the transmission; driving safety is increased because the control system prevents driver error and improper use of the transmission system; improved performance by conventional manual transmission components (reduced clutch wear). Once the warning light has gone out, it is ready to accept gear changes made using the gear selection lever. Operation with engine off For safety reasons, the gear can be changed using the selection lever only with the brake pedal pressed. When you need to leave the car parked on a gradient and engage a gear to hold it in place, it is essential to check on the display that the new gear has engaged and then wait 1 to 2 seconds before releasing the brake pedal to allow the clutch to engage fully. After changing gear, release the gear selection lever immediately. A prolonged manoeuvre (more than 10 seconds) will cause the transmission warning light to come on. The system will switch automatically to CITY mode and a buzzer will sound. All this can be reversed by releasing the gear selection lever Engine starting The engine may be started with a gear engaged or with the gearbox in neutral. Keep the brake pedal depressed during start-up. After start-up, the transmission switches automatically to neutral (indicated by the letter N on the display) and the system selects semiautomatic operation mode (manual). If the engine fails to start with a speed engaged, the driver is informed of a situation of potential danger due to the fact that the transmission has automatically switched to neutral by a buzzer and a message on the display. The car can be push-started as follows: Turn the ignition key to the ON position Check the warning light has gone off (after 10 seconds); with the car running at a certain speed and the gearbox in neutral, shift up a gear (+) using the selection lever. This operation cannot be carried out if the battery is completely flat. Take-off Take-off is possible in 1 st , 2 nd and reverse according to specific clutch closure maps in the control unit. For safety reasons, the above gears can be selected using the selection lever (steering wheel controls are not active until the car is running at 10 km/h) only with the brake pedal depressed or with the car at a standstill in the case of reverse. When the driver depresses the accelerator pedal, the car takes off and the system closes the clutch progressively to move the car. The driver may adjust the transmitted torque by operating the accelerator pedal. When the accelerator pedal is released, the clutch opens and the car slows. When engine rpm and clutch rpm are the same, the clutch is fully closed. During take-off, the driver may request a gear change (it is advisable to release the accelerator pedal to avoid rapid interruption of the torque transmitted by the clutch). Engine brake on descents With the car on a descent, gear engaged, accelerator pedal released and car speed increasing over a set level, the clutch is automatically reclosed to provide the necessary engine braking effect. If the driver operates the accelerator pedal during this stage, clutch closure obeys a map stored in the transmission control unit. Automatic clutch closure is suspended if the car moves in the opposite direction to that of the speed engaged. Slowing down When the car is slowing down, e.g. after releasing the accelerator pedal, the system automatically re-opens the clutch to prevent the engine stalling. The clutch re-opens at an engine speed computed on the basis of: engine rpm deceleration level (based on engine rpm) brake pedal pressed/not pressed. When slowing down, if the speed is higher than 3 rd , the transmission automatically shifts down. When the car stops, 1 st gear is engaged automatically. Manual gear shifts - semiautomatic operation Semiautomatic mode is set: automatically whenever the car is started; when the driver operates the gear lever or buttons while in CITY mode; when the driver presses the CITY button again while in CITY mode. The system will accept an shift up or shift down request with the car in motion and clutch fully closed only if it is compatible with the current rpm range. Normally a gear lever or button command (with car speed more than 10 km/h) will trigger only one upward or downward shift. It is advisable to wait for the end of a gear shift before requesting another, in order to avoid multiple requests in fast succession. Once a gear shift request has been accepted, the shift is carried out according to an automatic sequence that reflects actual driver behaviour. engine torque reduction (by reducing advance/closing throttle) and simultaneous clutch opening; current gear disengaged, new gear selected and engaged. The engine (CUT OFF) is controlled in parallel, to increase engine rpm to the same level as clutch rpm following engagement of the new gear; modulated clutch closure and simultaneous gradual return to maximum possible torque delivery by the engine. When engine rpm and clutch rpm are the same, the clutch is fully closed. Gear changes become faster with the accelerator pedal pressed through at least 60% of its travel and car speed greater than 5000 rpm. A current gear shift request may be interrupted at any time by a new request by the driver, provided it is compatible with the current engine rpm range. If the gear shift is not successful, it is repeated a second time from neutral. The gear above the one originally requested is then engaged. City mode - automatic shifting The speed is selected on the basis of a single control unit map on the basis of: accelerator pedal position vehicle speed. optimal gear (based on accelerator pedal position) brake pedal position. If the accelerator pedal is released, the system does not shift up a speed in order to maintain an engine braking effect. Gears are shifted in exactly the same way as during semiautomatic operation. The same transmission and engine control parameters are used. Request to shift to neutral This request takes precedence over all other gear shift requests. With the engine off, hold down the brake pedal to engage neutral. With the car in motion, neutral cannot be engaged when the car is travelling at more than a given speed (40 km/h) Turning off the engine and deactivating the system When the ignition key is turned off, the engine goes off but the Selespeed system stays active until the car comes to a complete standstill. The hydraulic section is deactivated 2-4 seconds after the ignition is turned off and the gear display goes off immediately after. Only at this point is the Selespeed system deactivated. The speed selected before the engine is turned off remains engaged. When the engine is turned off with the gearbox in neutral, the buzzer attracts the driver's attention so that the car can be made safe by engaging 1 st gear or reverse. In this case, turn the ignition key to MAR and engage 1 st or reverse with the brake pedal depressed. Never leave the car in neutral. Never remove the ignition key when the car is in motion because the Selespeed system would work anomalously until the car was stopped and the steering wheel would lock automatically the first time it was steered. It is vital to switch off the engine and deactivate the Selespeed system, keeping the brake pedal pressed; only release the pedal when the gear display is switched off. When the buzzer sounds For safety reasons, the system activates the buzzer when: reverse is engaged; the car is parked in neutral (the buzzer goes off when the ignition key is turned off). the clutch overheats during start-up; the car moves in the opposite direction to that of the gear engaged. For safety reasons, with the car at a standstill, engine running and 1 st , 2 nd or reverse engaged, the system: activates the buzzer; automatically switches to neutral when: the accelerator pedal and/or brake pedal is not operated for at least 50 seconds; the brake is depressed for longer than 10 minutes; the driver's door is opened and the accelerator pedal and brake pedal have not been operated for at least 1 second. Recovery Making the system safe The control unit is able to identify potentially dangerous situations and make the system safe as a precautionary measure. The system makes the system safe as follows: temporary suspension of current gear shifts in the case of: incorrect range selection (gear selection plan) clutch not sufficiently open gearbox input rpm too high; immediate engine stop command (via CAN line) with gear engaged, car taking-off/waiting to take off and detection of hydraulic clutch fault giving rise to fast clutch re-closure; control unit fault leading to: maintenance of pre-existing traction status until the car is about to stop; clutch opening command whe car is about to pull up. Faulty operation When the system detects faults in its components, its operating strategies are reconfigured. The system adopts the following operating restrictions according to where the fault lies: gear lever faulty, the system switches to automatic CITY mode so the car can be driven to the first Authorised Service Outlet; clutch solenoid faulty, clutch operation locked with the car at a standstill; clutch sensor faulty, clutch control locked with the car at a standstill; shift solenoids faulty, gear shift acceptance locked selection solenoids faulty, gear shift acceptance blocked; shift and selection sensors faulty, gear change times extended and acceptance only of 1 st , 2 nd and reverse. engine, gearbox input and gearbox output rpm sensor faulty, and acceptance only of 1 st , 2 nd and reverse. oil pressure sensor faulty, open loop pump control gear selection lever switches faulty, switch to automatic mode. Faults in the Selespeed system are indicated by a warning light (1) on the rev counter. When the system comes on, the warning light should come with a fixed light for 4 seconds. If the warning light continues to flash, a fault has been detected in the transmission. At the same time, the buzzer sounds intermittently for 4 seconds. The CITY control is located on the tunnel, near the gear lever and allows the activation of the automatic gear change function. The lever control takes priority if simultaneous requests are made using both the steering wheel lever and the lever on the tunnel. A gear change request is NOT accepted with the car in motion if the request leads to rpm levels that are too high or too low. Horn A buzzer warns the driver of the following: system faults improper use (e.g. clutch overheating) car safety (e.g. doors open) Incorrect or inconsistent driver operation The Selespeed system prevents incorrect driver operation that could cause dangerous situations or be detrimental to the system. The strategies are: the lever control takes priority if simultaneous requests are made using both the steering wheel lever and the tunnel lever; reverse gear cannot be engaged with the vehicle moving; a gear change request is not accepted with the car in motion if the request leads to rpm levels that are too high or too low; only 1st gear, 2nd gear and Reverse gear can be engaged with the vehicle stationary and the engine running. The system has been designed taking into account the possibility that incorrect manoeuvres that could create dangerous situations could be requested allowing: the engine can only be started with a gear engaged if the vehicle is stationary, the accelerator pedal released and the brake pedal pressed (the system initially places the gearbox in automatic neutral and then enables the starting of the engine); with the car at a standstill (or virtually still), gear change requests are accepted only if the brake pedal is pressed (applies also to neutral). This prevents dangerous situations in case the lever/buttons on the steering wheel are accidentally operated by someone else or even by the driver; disabling of the steering wheel buttons at vehicle speeds of less than 15 km/h, thereby preventing possible driver error during parking manoeuvres; inhibition of the 'neutral' control above a preset speed, thereby preventing incorrect operation in critical situations, for example, downhill; CITY mode cancellation when the driver selects the gear directly using the lever/buttons, the driver's selection takes priority in this situation. automatic engagement of neutral and buzzer warning the driver for a limited period in the following cases: insufficient oil pressure for the management of the clutch, engine started and door open (starting with the door open is, however permissible because the driver's action on the brake or the accelerator is detected), engine started with gear engaged and no sign of operation of accelerator or brake for more than 5 secs., gear engaged and accelerator released and brake pedal pressed for at least 30 secs.; independent gear change if the driver insists outside of the rev range without changing gear. SYSTEM OPERATION Turning on the system This takes place by turning the ignition key. The system informs the driver, through the instrument display, of the gear engaged and, after 1 - 2 secs., the system is capable of accepting new gear changes from the lever only. With the engine switched off Any gear whatsover can be engaged (including Reverse) and neutral can be engaged; these operations can only be carried out with the brake pedal depressed. Engine starting The system only enables the starting enablement relay if the gearbox is in neutral which the system automatically does when the brake pedal is pressed at the time of starting. Vehicle take off / acceleration Only 1st gear, 2nd gear or Reverse can be engaged for take off after starting. For safety reasons 1st and 2nd gears can only be engaged with the brake pedal pressed, whilst for Reverse gear in addition to this condition the vehicle must also be at a complete standstill. When the brake pedal is released and the accelerator pedal operated, the system gradually closes the clutch and allows the vehicle to take off. Modulating the position of the accelerator pedal allows the system to meter the torque transmitted by the clutch and consequently the acceleration of the vehicle. When the system detects synchronism between the engine and clutch speeds, it closes the clutch completely Vehicle slowing down When the accelerator is released the system recognizes the intention to slow the vehicle down and automatically reopens the clutch to prevent the engine from stalling. This reopening takes place at an engine speed that depends on the deceleration and the controls implemented by the driver (brake pressed or not). When slowing down, if the speed engaged is higher than 3rd, the system automtically shifts down. When the vehicle stops, 1st gear is engaged automatically. Vehicle downhill When the vehicle is driving downhill, a gear is engaged and the accelerator pedal is released, the speed increases, but as the preset speed in the control unit is reached, the clutch is automatically closed again to provide an engine braking effect; if the accelerator is pressed again, the driver resumes control of the vehicle. Gear shift With the vehicle moving and the clutch completely closed, the system is capable of accepting gear shift commandsif they are compatible with the rpm range. Gear shifts can be implemented, as described previously, using the controls on the steering wheel or the joystick on the tunnel (if the lever and the steering wheel lever are operated simultaneously, the lever takes priority). Once a gear shift request has been accepted, the shift is carried out according to an automatic sequence that reflects actual driver behaviour: engine torque reduction through a command from the Selespeed control system to the engine control system with the simultaneous opening of the clutch; release, selection and engagement of the new gear (parallel to this stage the engine is controlled so that the speed for the clutch after the engagement of the new gear can be reached); modulated clutch closure and simultaneous gradual return to maximum possible torque delivery by the engine. When the system detects synchronism between the engine and clutch speeds, the clutch is completely closed; a gear shift in progress may be interrupted at any time by a new request provided that it is compatible with the engine rpm range; the actuator control sequences during a gear shift are accompanied by waiting, allowing the repetition of the control if the outcome is not correct the first time, engaging a higher gear than requested. Automatic gear shift (city mode) The Selespeed system has an automatic operating mode, similar to the one on conventional automatic transmissions. The selection of the speed to engage is made using a (single) map that correlates the position of the accelerator pedal, the vehicle speed and the optimum gear. If the accelerator pedal is released, the system keeps the clutch as closed as possible to allow maximum engine braking. Gears are shifted in exactly the same way as during semiautomatic operation. The same transmission and engine control parameters are used. Request to shift to neutral With the engine off the brake pedal must be pressed, as described previously. With the vehicle moving, this request is not accepted above a preset vehicle speed. Switching off the engine and the system With the ignition key in the OFF position, the engine switches off and the Selespeed system keeps the gear selected engaged. The Selespeed system is only completely deactivated after having received a 'nil speed' input from the engine, gearbox input, gearbox output and after having saved the functional and diagnostic data in the control unit stable memory (all of this takes place in less than 2 seconds). Information for the driver The information for the driver concerning the operation of the Selespeed system is transmitted through a display located in the centre of the instrument that indicates the gear engaged or the CITY mode or the failure of the system; a buzzer signals the improper use of the vehicle, or an unsafe situation or the failure of the system (e.g. improper use may be starting with the clutch overheating, an unsafe situation could be leaving the vehicle not in gear). Push-starting The car can be push-started as follows: turn the ignition key to the ON position check the warning light has gone off (after 10 seconds); with the car running at a certain speed and the gearbox in neutral, shift up a gear (+) using the selection lever. This operation cannot be carried out if the battery is completely flat. This automatic transmission allows the driver to shift gears manually by moving the selector lever into a special sector, Q-System. The CAE electronic control unit manages automatic transmission operation by connection to: sensors/actuators fitted to the transmission for receiving information on operating conditions and operating the clutch and brakes; the injection/ignition control unit for the exchange of information on the engine; control panel for displaying operating conditions. DIAGRAM OF INPUT/OUTPUT INFORMATION FROM THE CONTROL UNIT . 1, SPORT/CITY programme button 2, ICE programme button 3, Gear selection lever position switch 4, Selector lever position sensor 5, Mainshaft rpm sensor 6, Driver's door switch 7, Layshaft rpm sensor 8, Transmission fluid temperature sensor 9, Brake light switch 10, Injection-ignition control unit / CAN line 11, Thottle body integral with D.V.E. 12, Engine coolant temperature sensor 13, Transmission fluid cooling fan 14, Control panel 15, Buzzer control 16, Speed shift solenoids (S1 and S2) 17, Lock-up clutch solenoid (SL) 18, Pressure control solenoid (STH) 19, Ignition key lock release control 20, Tester connection OPERATING STRATEGIES Shifting gears Gear shifts depend on: accelerator pedal position vehicle speed typical engine parameters (throttle opening angle and engine rpm); speed strategy selected by the driver (SPORT/CITY or ICE). The CAE control unit sends a duty-cycle signal to speed shift solenoids S1 and S2. This controls fluid flow to the brakes and clutch in order to achieve the various transmission ratios. Shifting from 3 rd to 4 th is prevented at engine coolant temperatures lower than a threshold stored in the control unit. Torque converter lock-up Lock-up clutch engagement to lock the torque converter depends on: the gear engaged; accelerator pedal position; vehicle speed; speed strategy selected by the driver (SPORT/CITY or ICE). The CAE control unit sends a duty-cycle signal to the SL lock-up clutch solenoid, which cuts off fluid flow to the rear end of the clutch and triggers release. The CAE control unit contains special torque converter lock programs for SPORT and CITY gear strategies, while the torque converter cannot be locked while in ICE mode. The torque converter is not locked under the following conditions: system in recovery mode (fault signal from one component); with brake pedal pressed and gear input speed below a given threshold; with throttle closed (accelerator pedal not pressed), car speed lower than 125 km/h and selection lever in D position; with engine coolant temperature lower than a threshold value stored in the control unit. To improve gear shift quality while shifting between 3 rd and 4 th speeds with the lock-up clutch engaged, the CAE control unit sends a duty-cycle signal to the SL solenoid in order to release the lock-up clutch temporarily. Implementing gear strategies The CAE control unit can instruct the automatic transmission to adopt three strategies: CITY, for the greatest driving comfort and optimal fuel consumption; SPORT, for top performance; ICE, to increase driving safety when grip is poor. The control unit also uses an automatic WARM-UP program to help the engine warm up. The system sets itself to CITY mode whenever the car is started. When the SPORT/CITY button is pressed, the system switches from CITY to SPORT mode and vice versa. When the ICE button is operated, the system uses the IICE strategy and cuts out the other two strategies. When the ICE button is pressed again, the system returns to the strategy selected previously. The system can switch between one strategy and another at any time while driving. The selected strategy is displayed beside the selector ever position on an instrument panel display. Typical curves governing transition between the four lock-up clutch ratios (while changing up or down) are then expressed on the basis of percentage throttle opening and car speed. Operation in city mode The CAE control unit selects CITY mode whenever the engine is started. This mode ensures a very smooth drive designed for comfort and running economy. Operation in sport mode The CAE control unit engages SPORT mode when the relevant button is operated. This operating strategy exploits available power to the full to achieve maximum car performance. Throttle opening remains the same, but upward gear shifts automatically take place at a higher rpm. SPORT mode is shut off: by pressing the ICE button again; by pressing the ICE button; when the car is in recovery mode. Operation in ice mode The CAE control unit switches to ICE mode when the ICE button is operated with the gear selection lever set to D. This strategy increases driving safety on roads with low grip and makes it easier to take off following start-up. When ICE strategy is selected, the lock-up clutch is not locked. ICE strategy is shut off: by pressing the ICE button again; when gear selection lever is set to a position other than D; by turning off the engine; when speed exceeds 45 km/h; when transmission fluid temperature exceeds a threshold; when the car is in recovery mode. Operation in automatic warm-up program This program is activated automatically by the CAE control unit. It helps the car warm up faster by raising gear shift points. It is activated after start-up if engine coolant temperature is below a threshold stored in the control unit and remains activated up to 55° ?. Hydraulic pressure changes Hydraulic system pressure is regulated by the CAE control unit to achieve the following functions: line pressure increase when cold; line pressure reduction during transition from N - R; control pressure modulation. Line pressure increase when cold With: gears selection lever in N position; transmission fluid temperature lower than 10 ° C; car speed lower than 7 km/h, The CAE control unit sends a 5 second signal to the STH solenoid to increase line presure and thus reduce time required to engage 1 st speed or reverse. Line pressure reduction during transition N-R When the gear selection lever is shifted from N to R position, the CAE control unit sends a signal to the STH solenoid to reduce line pressure in order to reduce jerkiness due to engagement of reverse. Control pressure modulation The CAE control unit increases solenoid control pressure according to throttle opening and car speed. Controlling gear shift times The CAE control unit compares the ratios between input and output speeds (supplied by mainshaft and layshaft rpm sensors respectively) with stored transmission ratios for the various speeds in order to assess gear shift times. Controlling gear shifts Automatic transmission speed engagement gives rise to jerks due to the sudden transmission ratio changes. This effect is more marked during engagement of 1 st gear and reverse because higher transmission ratios are possible. To reduce this stress and improve driving comfort, the automatic transmission adopts the following strategies: 1 st speed and reverse are engaged at reduced drive torque (garage function); squat controlled during transition betwen N - D; line pressure reduced during transition between N - R. 1 st speed or reverse engagement (garage function) When the gear selection lever is shifted as follows: from N (or P or R) to D from any position to R The CAE control unit instructs the injection - ignition control unit to reduce drive torque and thus reduce the jerkiness experienced while shifting to 1 st speed or reverse. Transition from n - d with control of squat When the gear selection lever is shifted from N to D position, the CAE control unit simultaneously engages 3 rd gear before moving on to 1 st gear. In this way, the jerkiness due to engagement of 1 st gear is reduced together with consequent squat. This function cuts in only when the following conditions occur simultaneously: brake pedal pressed; throttle closed; car speed lower than 7 km/h; CITY or SPORT mode in use. Transition from n - r with reduction in line pressure When the gear selection lever is shifted from N to R position, the CAE control unit instructs the STH solenoid to reduce line pressure in order to reduce the jerkiness experienced during engagement of reverse. Safety functions Protection against excess rpm The CAE control unit prevents the engagement of lower ratios (even when the gear selection lever is moved by hand) until car speed has dropped below a given threshold in order to prevent dangerous engine racing. Shift-lock The speed selection lever can be moved from position P, with the ignition key turned on, only with the brake pedal depressed (Shift-lock safety function). In case of emergencies (faults, flat battery etc.), teh lever can only be moved from P position by pressing a manual button beneath the gear lever boot and simultaneously shifting the lever from P to the required position. Key-lock When turned off, the ignition key may be removed only if the gear selection lever is in P position (Key-lock). In case of emergency ( faults, flat battery etc.), the ignition key may be removed even when the gear selection lever is not set to P. To do this, press the release device located in the trim near the ignition by hand and simultaneously remove the key. Buzzer This is built into the control panel and comes on for 18 seconds when: the driver's door is open and/or engine status and gear selection lever position is other than P R is engaged. Fault indication Fault warning light Automatic transmission faults are indicated by warning light (1) on the control panel as follows: fixed light, maximum automatic transmission fluid temperature; flashing light, automatic transmission failure. When the ignition key is turned to MAR position, the warning light should come on and then go off after about 4 seconds. If the warning light stays on or comes on while the car is in motion, the automatic transmission is faulty. Warning light comes on with fixed light If the warning light comes on with a fixed light during motion, the transmission fluid has reached maximum temperature. The control unit runs an emergency program under these circumstances. Warning light flashing If the warning light flashes during motion, the automatic transmission is faulty. The control unit runs an emergency program under these circumstances. In this situation, it is advisable to stop the car and turn off the engine. Next time the car is started, the automatic test system could eliminate the fault, though it will remain stored in the control unit. If the fault persists (warning light flashing), select the gear manually as if driving a manual car and remember that the only two speeds available are 2 nd and 4 th . This means that the gear will always change to 2 nd whether 1 st or 2 nd is selected; 4 th will always be selected whther 3 rd or 4 th is selected. Reverse may be engaged. The reverse lock may not be active when the car is driven with a faulty transmission. Never move the lever to R with the car in motion. TORQUE CONVERTER It is fitted between the engine and the gearbox in place of the conventional disc clutch. The torque converter is designed to ensure a smooth (hydraulic) connection between the engine and the gearbox. The torque converter consists of: a casing (1) containing the oil and the various components a pump impeller (2) connected to the crankshaft and to the oil pump a turbine impeller (3) connected to the gearbox input shaft a stator (4), fitted on the free wheel, which has the task of directing the flow of oil to the pump impeller a torque converter lock-up device (5) operated by the CAE control unit via a solenoid valve and a regulation valve. a clutch cover (6). The converter operates in two stages: converter stage, where it multiplies the torque coupler stage, where it transmits the torque with an efficiency of 98% or 100% according to whether or not the lock-up is activated. Torque converter operation As soon as the engine is started up, the pump impeller behaves like a centrifugal pump and the oil is thrust by the centrifugal force into the radial ducts. The oil comes out of the pump impeller vanes, is directed to the turbine impeller where it flows through the ducts from the edges towards the centre. If the oil were to flow directly to the pump impeller it would meet the impeller vanes in the opposite direction to the direction of rotation. 1, Pump impeller 2, Turbine impeller To avoid this, there is a "stator" between the two impellers. The stator has the task of directing the flow of oil to the pump impeller in the direction of rotation of the impeller. 1, Pump impeller 2, Turbine impeller 3, Stator In this way, the energy of the oil on entering the pump impeller is added to the kinetic energy of the pump impeller possessed at that moment. The greater the difference in speed between the pump and the turbine, the greater the torque multiplication (max. with the turbine stationary). When the turbine starts to assume speed, the multiplication of the torque gradually decreases. A, During starting B, Intermediate speed C, Coupling stage 1, Pump impeller 2, Turbine impeller 3, Stator Lock-up clutch In 1 st gear, 2 nd gear and reverse, drive torque is transmitted from the torque converter. In 3 rd and 4 th gear, torque is firstly transmitted hydraulically via the converter and then mechanically via the lock-up clutch. The clutch connects the converter pump and turbine to eliminate internal converter slide as speed picks up and form a mechanical coupling between engine and gearbox mainshaft. The torque converter can be locked to increase transmission performance at high speeds and reduce fuel consumption on long motorway journeys. 1, Engine flywheel attachments 2, Case integral with pump 3, Lock-up clutch 4, Turbine 5, Pump 6, Stator 7, Mainshaft The lock-up clutch is engaged by the CAE control unit by solenoid SL in 3 rd and 4 th gear when the drive torque need no longer be multiplied by the torque converter. Solenoid SL cuts off oil flow to the rear clutch surface to reduce pressure, while pressure inside the converter continues to act on the front surface. The clutch fitted to the turbine hub is then pressed against the case integral with the converter pump to lock the converter. Oil pump This gear pump is fitted between the torque converter and the gearbox casing and is controlled by the converter pump impeller (6). The oil, under pressure, engages the gears and lubricates the various gears. The pump is made up of two eccentric gears: drive gear (7) with outer teeth driven gear (8) with inner teeth. The two gears are housed in a pump casing (3) which contains an asymmetrical separator which creates two different chambers: an inlet chamber (1) and a supply chamber (2). 1, Inlet 2, Supply 3, Pump casing 4, Washer 5, Gasket 6, Drive gear (operated by the torque converter pump impeller) 7, Driven gear 8, Centering pin Drive transmission We will now examine drive transmission under different driving conditions and describe the control procedures required to achieve different transmission ratios. Belt brake B4 locks differential gear S3 of train P3 and prevents it from turning. The parking lock is disengaged and planet gears ST3 are free to turn around differential S3; the car will move if it is on a gradient. In position N or P, brake B4 is activated to reduce stress caused by the simultaneous engagement of several brakes and clutches when the lever is moved to position D or R. Because brake D4 must be activated in both 1 st and reverse gears, simultaneous engagement will be reduced by also activating it in N and P. Epicyclic gear train This automatic transmission uses three epicyclic gear trains to produce five transmission ratios (4 forward speeds and reverse). Rear gear train P1 is a single epicyclic gear train consisting of a pinion or differential S1 (1), three long planet gears ST1 (3) integral with gear carrier (5) and a ring gear K1 (2). Front gear train P2 consists of a double epicyclic train made up of pinion or differential S1 91), three long internal planet gears ST1 (3), six short external planet gears (4) integral with gear carrier (5) and ring gear (K2) (6). Long planet gears (ST1) and ring gear S1 (1) are common to gear trains P1 and P2, which are located on the mainshaft. 1, Shared differential S1 2, Ring gear K1 of gear train P1 3, Shared long planet gears ST1 4, Short planet gears ST2 of gear train P2 5, Gear carrier 6, Ring gear K2 of gear train P2 Gear train P3 is a single epicyclic gear train made up of a pinion or differential S3 (1), three planet gears ST3 (2) integral with gear carrier (3) and ring gear K3 (4). This gear train is located on the layshaft. 1, Differential S3 2, Planet gears ST3 3, Gear carrier 4, Ring gear Clutches There are three, multplate oil bath clutches comprising, alternately: driven plates (2) lined with material with a high friction coefficient steel drive plates (2) The clutches are activated by the automatic transmission hydraulic control system solenoid unit. Clutch C1 prevents mainshaft and ring gear K1 of gear train P1 from turning in relation to one another. Clutch C2 prevents mainshaft and differential S1 common to gear trains P1 and P2 from turning in relation to one another. Clutch C3 prevents differential S3 and the gear carrier of gear train P3 on the layshaft from turning in relation to one another. Brakes There are four: three multidisc oil-bath type and one band brake. The brakes are activated by the automatic transmission hydraulic control system solenoid unit. Brake B1 locks the rotation of differential S1 common to gear trains P1 and P2. Brake B2 locks the rotation of the outer race of freewheel F1 to prevent differential S1 common to gear trains P1 and P2 from turning anticlockwise. Brake B3 locks the rotation of ring gear K2 of gear train P2. Band brake B4 prevents differential S3 of gear train P3 from turning. Freewheels These consist of two concentric races and a cage enclosing a set of asymmetrical dowels. The dowels allow both races to turn freely in one direction only. If they are turned the other way, they bind to form a reaction couple. Freewheel F1 prevents anticlockwise rotation of differential S1 common to gear trains P1 and P2, when brake B2 is engaged. Freewheel F2 prevents anticlockwise rotation of ring gear K2 of gear train P2. Freewheel F3 prevents clockwise rotation of differential S3 of gear train P3. Solenoids for engagement of speeds s1 and s2 These are located in the front part of the automatic transmission, where they implement gear changes. When the normally closed (N.C.) solenoids receive a signal from the CAE control unit, they change position to engage the different transmission ratios. Lock-up clutch solenoid sl This is located in the front part of the automatic transmission, where it locks the torque converter. The solenoid is controlled by a duty-cycle signal from the CAE control unit. It cuts off the oil flow to modulate the outlet pressure acting on the rear clutch surface. The clutch is fitted to the turbine hub. It is pushed by pressure acting against the front inner surface of the converter, against the case interal with the converter pump to lock the converter. Pressure control solenoid sth This is located in the front part of the gearbox. It controls hydraulic pressure changes. The solenoid is controlled by a duty-cycle signal emitted by the CAE control unit. It regulates the hydraulic pressure acting on the brakes and clutches in order to: reduce gear engagement times when cold reduce jerkiness when reverse is engaged. The solenoid regulates control pressure according to throttle opening and car speed.

GEAR SELECTOR LEVER The gear selector lever can assume the following positions in automatic mode: P, park R, reverse N, neutral D, drive and the following positions in manual mode: 1 st speed 2 nd speed 3 rd speed 4 th speed. Lift the ring beneath the selection lever knob for the following shifts: from P to R and viceversa from N to R. Information on gear selector lever position (P - R - N - D) is supplied to the CAE control unit by a sensor fitted externally on the gear casing and connected to the lever mechanically (bowden cable) and electrically. The CAE control unit sends the control panel a coded signal via a dedicated serial line in order to display corresponding lever position and operating mode (SPORT, CITY or ICE). The lever may be shifted from position D to manual mode by moving it to the left in the selection gate. Special switches allow the CAE control unit to identify: changeover from automatic to manual mode changeover from one speed to another while in manual mode lever position. GEAR LEVER POSITION SENSOR This is located on the front part of the gear casing. It detects gear selection lever position (it is mechanically connected to the lever) and informs the CAE control unit by means of an electrical signal. The CAE control unit turns on the relevant warning light on the control panel. The sensor also: turns on the reversing lights when reverse is engaged enables engine start-up with the speed selection lever set to N or P .

Mainshaft rpm sensor This magnetic induction sensor is located on the gear casing. It measures mainshaft rpm via a 12-toothed phonic wheel on the outer surface of clutch cylinder C1. The sensor sends control unit CAE a pulse signal (12 pulses per mainshaft revolution) proportional to gearbox input rpm. LAYSHAFT rpm sensor This magnetic induction sensor is located on the gear casing. It measures layshaft rpm via an 18-toothed phonic wheel formed from the parking lock gear. The sensor sends the CAE control unit a pulse signal (18 pulses per layshaft revolution) proportional to gearbox output rpm, i.e. vehicle speed. This signal is used to implement gear shifts.
The driveshafts, the constant velocity joints and the intermediate shaft which make up the "transmission" assembly transmit the movement of the gearbox to the drive wheels.

The driveshafts (1), made from high resistance steel, have splined ends to allow matching with the constant velocity joints (2). The constant velocity joints are composed of an innerl "drive" core (3) fitted on the input shaft and an outer "driven" shell (4), which is part of the coupling output. The inner core has six spherical splines on the outer surface which contain six balls (5), kept in place by a chamber (6). The balls are the true drive transmission element, because they are simultaneously housed in the same number of grooves on the inner surface of the shell. The intermediate shaft (1), made from high resistance steel, connects the flange and the differential with the right driveshaft by means of the splined end. To limit the projection between the mounting points, the intermediate shaft is supported by a seat on the gear casing.

CONSTRUCTION FEATURES All versions are equipped with Bosch 5.3 A.B.S. anti-lock brakes with four active sensors and four channels. The system control unit controls the EBD (Electronic Brake force Distribution) function to distribute the brake force between the front and rear axles. Disc brakes on all four wheels (self-ventilated on the high range). LUCAS floating aluminium caliper with automatic play take-up BOSCH 8' brake servo with additional chamber and 7/8' pump Mechanical type handbrake with twin cable. DESCRIPTION General characteristics The A.B.S. system consists of: an electronic control unit integrated in the electro-hydraulic control unit an electro-hydraulic control unit which modulates the braking pressure via eight solenoid valves, two for each wheel four 'active' type sensors which detect the angular rotation speed of the wheels. Function check Operating principle The electronic control unit processes the signals coming from the active sensors and the brake light switch and implements the modulation of the brake fluid pressure in the following conditions: pressure increase stage pressure maintenance stage pressure reduction stage. Braking is therefore intermittent with a succession of stages governed by braked wheel rolling status. The device works so quickly that the driver cannot feel the repetitive operation cycle. Pressure increase stage With the brake pedal pressure, the electronic control unit (1): does not supply the pressurizing solenoid valve (N.A.) (2) does not supply the discharge solenoid valve (N.C.) (3). Therefore, the pressure produced by the brake pump (4) reaches the brake calipers (5) without undergoing variations. Pressure maintenance stages The electronic control unit (1): supplies the exhaust solenoid (N.O.) (2) does not supply the discharge solenoid valve (N.C.) (3). Therefore, the hydraulic connection between the brake pump (4) and the brake caliper (5) is interrupted. The pressure in the brake caliper (5) remains constant even if the pressure on the brake pedal increases. Pressure reduction stage The electronic control unit (1): supplies the pressurizing solenoid valve (N.A.) (2) supplies the discharge solenoid valve (N.C.) (3). The hydraulic connection between the brake pump (4) and the brake caliper (5) is interrupted and the pressurizing solenoid valve (3) opens and places the brake caliper (5) in contact with the low pressure accumulator (6) and the recovery pump (7). The electronic control unit (1) also supplies the recovery pump (7) drive motor (8) to reintroduce the fluid removed from the brake caliper (5) back into the main circuit. The fluid passes through the high pressure accumulator (9) and the restricter (10) which have a damping effect. The system is equipped with a single-acting valve (11) fitted in parallel to the pressurizing valve (2) which allows a rapid reduction in the pressure at the brake caliper (5) when the brake pedal is released. Ebd function (electronic brake force distribution) The EBD function controls the distribution of the brake force and therefore replaces the conventional mechanical load proportioning valve making it possible to: acts independently on the rear brake calipers improve the distribution of the brake forces intervene in an optimum manner in all load conditions (static or dynamic), driving conditions (in a straight line or round bends) and condition of the vehicle (tyres, brakes and suspension worn) implement a strategy which follows the ideal distribution curve. Fa, front axle brake force Fp, rear axle brake force A, Distribution curve implemented by the braking system B, Ideal distribution curve C, Distribution curve implemented by the conventional hydraulic load proportioning valve D, Distribution curve implemented by the EDB function A failure in the EBD function is signalled by the following warning lights coming on simultaneously: A.B.S. warning light insufficient brake fluid and/or handbrake applied warning light It is therefore necessary: to avoid violent braking because the rear wheels may lock early to drive the vehicle extremely carefully to the nearest authorized workshop to have the system checked. Recovery The electronic control unit is equipped with a safety circuit which has the task of safeguarding the efficiency of the system. With the ignition key inserted, the safety circuit checks the following for 4 seconds: the operation of the electronic control unit it activates the solenoid valves to check their operation it operates the recovery pump to check its operation it checks the active sensor signals. Each time the vehicle sets off from a stationary position, the safety circuit checks the presence of the active sensor signals. With the vehicle driving, the safety circuit behaves in the following way: it continuously compares the angular speed of the wheels with the reference speed calculated it checks the memory conditions govern operation of both relays it constantly checks the battery voltage If the safety circuit has detected one or more irregularities with the system components during the checking stage it behaves in the following way: it switches off the A.B.S. system guaranteeing, however, the operation of the conventional braking system and EBD function. it signals the irregular condition to the driver by the warning light in the instrument panel coming on.
