CONSTRUCTION FEATURES On account of its operating specifications, in the following conditions, the engine on the 2.0 JTS version: after cold starting; whilst warming up; with the climate control working, produces a minimal vacuum in the brake servo caused by the increased opening of the throttle. DESCRIPTION The brake servo vacuum circuit is equipped with a by-pass with two built-in one way valves (5) and (7) which operate through the differences in pressure (P1) and (P2) upstream and downstream of the throttle casing. There is a restricter (6) for the pipe near the valve (5) to take advantage of the Venturi effect. A servo brake minimum vacuum pressure sensor (8) is fitted on the brake servo (9) which notifies the engine management control unit of the vacuum in the brake servo. OPERATING With the engine cold or additional loads applied, the air passes through the by-pass and is in contact with the brake servo by means of the one-way valve (5) and the restricter increases the vacuum at which the air is removed from the brake servo. With the engine warm and without additional loads, the vacuum in the intake manifold is equal to or more than -600 mb (ideal value) and the air in the brake servo is removed via valve (7). If the brake pedal is pressed repeatedly and, in particular, if the throttle is open on account of other consumers, the vacuum in the brake servo may go down to below the level of -290 mb. At this point, the brake servo minimum vacuum sensor (8) intervenes, sending an electrical signal to the engine management control unit. Having received the signal (1.5 - 5 Volt), the control unit processes it and transforms it into a physical vacuum value and intervenes by decativating: the air conditioning, the stratified engine operating mode, therefore the vacuum in the brake servo increases guaranteeing assistance for at least three repeated presses of the brake pedal. FAULT DIAGNOSIS When the engine management control unit receives the signal it carries out the electrical fault diagnosis. If an occasional error is detected, it intervenes by temporarily deactivating the air conditioning and the stratified engine operating mode. If a validated error is detected (i.e. verified at least three times), caused by an open circuit or a battery/earth short circuit, it is switched OFF, i.e. the air conditioning and the stratified engine operating mode are definitively deactivated until the fault is repaired. 1 - Modular intake manifold 2 - Throttle casing 3 - Air flow meter 4 - Air cleaner 5 - One-way valve 6 - Restricter 7 - One-way valve 8 - Brake servo minimum vacuum sensor 9 - Brake servo 10 - Vacuum signal transformation graph

ELECTRO-HYDRAULIC UNIT It consists of an electronic control unit (1) and an electro-hydraulic control unit (2). Electronic control unit The electronic control unit is responsible for: acquiring the data coming from the 'active' wheel rpm sensors storing control parameters defined during the preparation of the vehicle storing the control software processes downloaded data controls the braking process detecting failures at the braking system components stores the fault codes and activates the A.B.S. warning lights. transmitting and receiving data via the diagnostic connector. Hydraulic control unit The electro-hydraulic control unit consists of: eight two-way solenoid valves a dual circuit electric recovery pump a low pressure accumulator a high pressure accumulator Responsible for modulating the pressure of the fluid at the brake calipers via two solenoid valves with the following stages: brake fluid pressure increase brake fluid pressure maintenance brake fluid pressure discharge. The letters indicating to which caliper and to which brake pump outlet they should be connected at stamped on the control unit at each outlet. RR = to the right rear brake (pipe marked with a light blue coloured band) LR = to the left rear brake (pipe marked with a green coloured band) RF = to the right front caliper (pipe marked with a yellow coloured band) LF = to the left front caliper (pipe marked with a white coloured band) MC1 = from the main circuit/flange side pump (pipe marked with a black or pink coloured band when the pipe polyammide resin is black) MC2 = from the secondary circuit/front pump (pipe marked with a brown coloured band). Active sensors They consist of two basic elements: a magnetic multi-polar codifier (1) integrated in the 'instrument' wheel hub bearing a Hall-effect receiver (2) opposite the codifier. The adoption of active sensors offers the following advantages: it reduces sensitivity to electro-magnetic interference resists interference generated by road surface heating it saves weight and size it simplifies the transmission couplings through the elimination of the phonic wheels. CONSTRUCTION FEATURES INTRODUCTION In addition to the normal functions carried out by the ABS 5.3 all the versions are equipped with A.S.R. (Antislip regulation). Characteristic of working principle 3340 A(B.S. ANTI-LOCK BRAKING SYSTEM .) This function intervenes when the A.B.S. control unit detects, via the signals received from the active sensors, that the speed of one or both drive wheels is different from that of the driven wheels (slipping). The A.B.S. control unit notifies the engine management control unit, via the CAN line, of the existence of slipping and requests a reduction in torque. Control system According to the vehicle driving conditions, two different control systems are activated without the driver operating the brake pedal in any way: In the case of excessive power with both drive wheels slipping the following takes place: an instant reduction in the ignition advances (petrol versions); a reduction in the butterfly opening angle (petrol versions); intervention with the injection times (JTD versions); a modulating action of the braking system at the drive wheels. In the case of only one drive wheel slipping, the following takes place: an instant reduction in the ignition advances (petrol versions); a reduction in the butterfly opening angle (petrol versions); intervention with the injection times (JTD versions); a braking action at the wheel which is slipping, producing a resistant torque. As a result, the differential transmits the same torque to the wheel with better grip. With the brake pedal depressed, the A.S.R. antislip function acts exclusively on the engine (reduction in torque) to guarantee the maximum efficiency of the A.B.S. braking system. Whilst driving on a snow-covered surface, with snow chains fitted, it may be useful to switch the A.S.R. function off: under these circumstances the slipping of the drive wheels during take off actually allows improved traction. Any failures which involve the exclusion of the A.S.R. system are only signalled by the warning light in the instrument panel coming on. Button/warning light A button allows the A.S.R. antislip function to be excluded; this is signalled by the LED in the button lighting up. Each time the vehicle is started up the A.S.R. antislip function is activated. Operation Intervention during braking With the brake pedal depressed, the electronic control unit: does not supply the solenoid valve (N.C.) (8); does not supply the solenoid valve (N.A.) (9). In this way, the system operates during the following stages: pressure increase, pressure maintenance, pressure reduction, as described in the Bosch 5.3 A.B.S.. 1 - Master cylinder 2 - High pressure accumulator 3 - Pump 4 - Low pressure accumulator 5 - Pressurizing solenoid valve 6 - Discharge solenoid valve 7- Brake calipers 8 - Inlet solenoid valve 9 - Operating solenoid valve A.s.r. intervention If one/both of the drive wheels is/are slipping, then the electronic control unit: supplies the hydraulic pump (1); supplies the (N.C.) solenoid valve (2); supplies the (N.A.) solenoid valve (3). Therefore the pressure produced by the pump (1) arrives at the brake caliper passing through the solenoid valve (6). The operating pressure for the brake caliper is modulated by the solenoid valves (5) and (6). In addition, the A.B.S./A.S.R. control unit notifies the engine management control unit (CAN line) of the presence of slipping. The latter, decreases the torque supplied by the engine with: a reduction in the ignition advances (petrol versions); a reduction in the butterfly valve opening (petrol versions); intervention on the injection times (JTD versions). 1 - Pump 2 - Inlet solenoid valve 3 - Pilot solenoid 4 - Brake calipers 5 - Pressurizing solenoid valve 6 - Discharge solenoid valve Warning light operation In the case of problems, the ASR system switches off automatically and the ASR warning light in the instrument panel and the ASR warning light on the button come on constantly. SPECIFCATIONS General characteristics The V.D.C. system (Vehicle Dynamic Control System) controls the vehicle during dynamic manoeuvres on the road and intervenes in emergency conditions. In any type of grip conditions this system increases the safety margin for the vehicle in the case of sudden manoeuvres or initial losses of grip (passing through puddles, icy sections, etc.). Whilst the anti-lock braking system (ABS) maintains the stability of the vehicle during rapid deceleration and the traction control systems (ASR/TCS) work during rapid acceleration, the V.D.C. system has been designed to keep the vehicle stable in the case of sudden manoeuvres in order to improve the vehicle's road holding, especially over slippery surfaces. In effect the V.D.C. system reacts to both vehicle oversteer and understeer and is equipped to return it to a stable condition to allow the driver to maintain full control of the vehicle. The VDC comes on automatically when the vehicle is started up and cannot be switched off. 1 - Steering angle sensor 2 - Yaw/side acceleration sensor (integrated within a single component) 3 - VDC warning light in instrument panel PERFORMANCE The V.D.C.: recognizes the wheels' longitudinal or lateral loss of grip; controls all the vehicle's driving conditions, from braking to acceleration to ensure the direction and stability of the geometry; assists the driver, even if they are not particularly experienced, to control critical situations within certain limits. SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS Devices adopted The V.D.C. system is managed by the ABS control unit with the restriction that only vehicles equipped with ABS/ASR can be fitted with this new function. The control unit processes the signals from the following sensors: steering angle sensor, side acceleration sensor and slewing sensor, engine operating conditions; wheel rpm sensor, and uses special algorhythms in the software to obtain the values for dynamic control: sliding of the wheels, drifting of the axles, wheel geometry angles, etc. From these figures the system correctly interprets any mistakes made by the driver and returns the vehicle to a stable condition. In addition to the above mentioned sensors, the minimum interface requirements for the vehicle to fit the system are: high speed CAN line, power unit with specific brake pump, specific ABS unit, instrument panel with special active type warning lights. OPERATING Operating principle The basic idea behind the V.D.C. consists of comparing the nominal parameters (processed by the control unit on the basis of the speed of the 4 wheels, steering angle, slewing speed, lateral acceleration, braking torque and engine torque) with the actual parameters in a given driving situation. In effect, on the basis of the input parameters it is possible to calculate, using a very complex mathematical model, whether the vehicle is taking a bend within the grip limits or whether it is about to skid (oversteer/understeer). Controlling the dynamics of the vehicle in extreme conditions is certainly second nature for a professional driver, but can be complicated for a 'normal' driver who may find themselves in emergency conditions. The V.D.C. system intervenes in such cases, acting to restore driving conditions which are compatible with the current grip conditions. The V.D.C. system uses two sensors, one of which 'reads' the slewing speed, or the rotation around the vertical axis of the vehicle. The sensor sensor, on the other hand, detects lateral acceleration. On the basis of this data, the V.D.C. understands whether the vehicle is about to skid at the front or the back (oversteer/understeer). In order to make it possible to control these critical situations, the system is capable of varying the injection parameters to manage the engine power and decelerate each of the four wheels individually thereby producing a slewing moment which is opposed to the one causing the instability in relation to the normal trajectory. If the vehicle loses grip at the rear, this movement is recovered by deceleration aimed at the outer wheels thereby restoring the necessary side grip to the rear wheels. If the loss in grip involves the front carriage, the system implements a reduction in power through choking. Button/warning light When the key is turned to the ON position, the VDC warning light in the instrument panel should come on and go off after about 4 seconds. If the warning light does not go out, or remains on whilst driving, this indicates a failure in the system. If the warning light flashes during driving, this means that the VDC system has intervened. The Infocenter, in turn, signals the fault by the warning light, together with the message, coming on. 1 - ASR warning light in button 2 - EBD warning light in instrument panel 3 - ASR warning light in instrument panel 4 - VDC warning light in instrument panel In the case of problems the VDC and ASR systems switch off automatically and the VDC warning light in the instrument panel and the ASR warning light on the button come on constantly. If the fault only involves the VDC system, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on whilst the warning light on the ASR button remains off and the operation of the ASR system is still enabled. If, on the other hand, the fault only affects the ASR, both systems are disabled and the VDC warning light in the instrument panel and the warning light on the ASR button come on constantly. If the VDC or ASR systems are not working properly, the vehicle behaves like a version on which these systems are not fitted. COMPONENT DESCRIPTION Steering sensor Specifications Operation The steering angle sensor detects steering wheel angle and turning speed and makes the data available to the C-CAN network (steered angle sensor node). Components Location The sensor is incorporated in the steering column switch unit and cannot be dismantled on its own. If removal and refitting operations are carried out on the steering wheel, steering column and power steering/alignment adjustment, the sensor must be electronically calibrated using a Tester. Pin out the sensor comes with a four pin connector, two pins are used to supply the sensor and two for the C-CAN line Pin 1, Earth Pin 2, +15 positive Pin 3, C-CAN H Line Pin 4, C-CAN H Line Operation The sensor measures the following using its internal electronic system: the steering column angular position the steering column rotation speed. This information is processed directly by the sensor and made available to the brake node via the C-CAN network The sensor has a measurement range of 1560° and a resolution of 0.1 °. The sensor must be set to the steering wheel position in order to work properly. This setting is carried out using a Tester (see instructions provided with the EXAMINER device). The sensor comes with an automatic diagnosis function and is able to check the plausibility of information processed. Lateral yaw/acceleration sensor Specifications Operation The lateral yaw/acceleration sensor detects rotations about the vehicle vertical axis (yaw) and measures side accelerations. It is connected directly to the ABS control unit. Sensor operational specifications are as follows: Supply voltage: Minimum value 8.2 V Maximum value 16V Rated value 12V Operating temperature: Minimum value -40° C Maximum value +85° C Current uptake at 12 V: Rated value 70mA Yaw sensor: Measurement range +/-100 °/s Resolution +/-0.2 °/s Side acceleration sensor Measurement range +/-1.8 g Components The sensor consists of a plastic case that encloses the sensitive parts that detect lateral yaw and acceleration and also an electronic control system. The sensor comes with a six pin connector - all pins are connected. Pin1 - Yaw sensor reference signal Pin2 - ABS control unit yaw sensor test signal Pin3 - 12V sensor supply Pin4 - Yaw signal in °/Sec Pin5 - Side acceleration signal in G Pin6 - Earth Location The sensor is located at the centre of gravity beneath the central console near the Air Bag control unit Operation The sensor is supplied directly by the ABS control unti and supplies a yaw and acceleration signal simultaneously via its sensitive elements. The yaw sensor is processed directly by the sensor and sent to the ABS control unit with a superimposed reference signal. Yaw signal range is between: lower limit 0.65V upper limit 4.35V reference signal 2.5V. 1 - Upper limit 2 - Reference signal 3 - Lower limit The ABS control unit supplies an alternating signal to the sensor for testing and safety functions.

All versions are equipped with power steering. This steering system guarantees: steering safety and precision at high speeds good handling limited effort during parking manoeuvres and at low speeds. DESCRIPTION The steering column consists of: a lower collapsible section (1) which allows the position of the steering wheel (4) to remain fixed in the case of a frontal impact an upper section (2) supported by a steel bracket and a magnesium support (3) which prevent vibrations of the steering wheel (4). With the advantage of: increasing the passive safety of the vehicle improving driving comfort. The steering column slides for the axial adjustment and moves in a rocking motion for the vertical adjustment. The steering lock is the 'friction' type in accordance with the regulations governing the prevention of break-in attempts. The system consists of bush (5) and a spring (6) fitted on the upper steering column (2). The spring has a 'smooth part' on the outside and a 'toothed part' on the inside. The toothed part is a press fit on the upper shaft bearing down slightly on the surface and preventing sliding in relation to the shaft. The smooth part is a press fit on the inner diameter of the bush (5) and can slide in relation to the bush with a controlled torque (between 10 and 24 daNm). The function of the friction system limits the maximum force which can be transmitted and guarantees the following in the case of a theft attempt: the security of the steering column impossibility of lock mechanism breakage with the advantage of ensuring: the anti-theft function driving safety. Quadrilateral front suspension, i.e. consisting of two superimposed triangles. In this configuration the shock absorber and the spring are flexible, damping elements which have no structural function. The rear suspension is the MacPherson type, indepedent with longitudinal track control arms. This type of suspension has the advantage of reduced dimensions allowing the adoption of a particularly low load carrying area. The combination of the two suspensions allows the following strong points: precision and gradual steering and steering wheel force prompt responsiveness high degree of stability and ease of control even in poor grip conditions very smooth and balanced movements very good comfort for a sports car. Front and rear wheel hubs with integrated bearing for A.B.S. system active sensors (ref. group 33) which replace the flywheel on previous systems.

DESCRIPTION Introduction The superimposed suspension "track control arm" triangles are hinged at the top to the wheel hub . At the base, the lower am is connected to the suspension crossmember and the upper arm to a press-fitted shell. The advantage of this type of suspension comes from the relative freedom of position for the tops of the two track control arms where the suspension steering axis passes. Specifications: The springs and shock absorbers play a very important role in the vehicle's driving safety and comfort, ensuring tyre grip on the road surface at all times and at the same time absorbing impact on rough ground. When a heavy load is transported or a trailer or caravan is towed, both these circumstances may cause the vehicle to suffer from the load on the rear axle. A solution to this problem is the adoption of a self-levelling suspension system, which keeps a constant distance between the rear axle and the bodywork, irrespective of the load applied to the rear axle. As may be observed in Fig. A, the position of the rear suspension is lowered, reducing the useful travel of the suspension and consequently confort when negotiating road surface roughness. In addition the frequency of the springs, the effective damping of the shock absorbers and the suspension geometry vary significantly, deviating from optimum conditions. A, Vehicles with conventional suspension B, Vehicles with self-levelling suspension For the Alfa 156 Sport Wagon, the BOGE Nivomat self-levelling suspension system has been adopted: it consists of two compact and independent units which are fitted instead of the conventional shock absorbers. These units maintain the correct distance between the rear axle and the bodywork and their damping force is dependent on the load. Nivomat suspension thus eliminates the well-known problem of conventional suspension which tends to be too hard when the vehicle is empty, and too "spongy" when travelling fully laden. The Alfa 156 Sport Wagon fitted with Nivomat units travels comfortably even with a light load, but remains dynamically stable and safe when fully laden. The BOGE Nivomat self-levelling suspension operates without requiring an external energy source. The Nivomat suspension is a unit which has its own internal pumping action. The energy required for this purpose is obtained entirely from the vertical movements of the vehicle's bodywork. As soon as the vehicle, by moving, makes the suspension work, the Nivomat units' internal pump starts to operate. It draws hydraulic fluid from an internal reservoir and sends it to a high-pressure chamber in which a compressed gas acts. In this way, the Nivomat units bring the vehicle's bodywork to the predetermined height for optimum driving when the vehicle starts to move, compensating the downward movement of the bodywork caused by a heavy load or a trailer. There is no separate device for controlling the height which requires adjustment: the height sensors are built into the shock absorber struts. The initial procedure for adjusting the bodywork height is completed after the vehicle has travelled a distance of around 2000 metres, depending on the road surface. When the load is removed or passengers leave the vehicle, the optimum height is restored while the vehicle is at a standstill. The Nivomat units carry out the simultaneous functions of a load-dependent hydropneumatic spring and a hydropneumatic shock absorber and replace conventional shock absorbers, offering the advantages of hydropneumatic self-levelling suspension for every type and class of vehicle, with load-dependent damping. This system may be installed in the factory on new vehicles or relatively easily on vehicles already in circulation, without too much adaptation and at low cost. COMPOSITION The BOGE Nivomat self-levelling units used on the Alfa 156 Sport Wagon consist of an outer shell containing two chambers: the low-pressure chamber (1), located at the bottom, acts as the fluid reservoir and is partially filled with gas under pressure; the high-pressure chamber (2), located at the top of the unit, is divided in two by a membrane (2); the external part contains the pressurized gas, while the inner part is filled with fluid. Unladen, the pressure inside the two chambers is identical, about 25 bar; fully laden, the low-pressure chamber is at about 8 bar, while the high-pressure chamber reaches about 80 bar. The outer casing contains the actual cylinder of the shock absorber (4), to the stem (5) of which is connected the piston (6) with the damping valves. A perforated pumping stem (7), connected to the base of the unit, runs along the inside of the hollow piston, forming the fluid pump (8). On the outer surface of the stem (7) there is a hole (9), which acts as a height sensor. Hydraulic diagram of the Nivomat unit. Cross-section of the Nivomat unit. OPERATION After loading the vehicle (passengers, luggage), the Nivomat units will yield (condition A) to an extent in relation to the stiffness of the springs. Following the vertical movements of the wheels, caused by the more or less severe irregularities in the road surface, the fluid present in the low-pressure chamber (1) is drawn by the fluid pump (8) via the perforated stem (7) and the inlet valve (11). From the pump, the fluid is sent, via the outlet valve (12) and the duct (13) to the bottom chamber of the shock absorber (4); from here, through the channel (14), the fluid reaches the high-pressure chamber (2) and compresses the gas contained by the membrane (3). The greater pressure created also acts in the bottom chamber of the shock absorber (4), causing the stem (5) to extend and the vehicle to be raised. When the groove (10) begins to emerge from the piston (6), this means that the optimum driving height has been reached (condition B) and the pressurized fluid can flow through the hole (9) and perforated stem (7) into the low-pressure chamber (1). A, Non-levelled condition B, Levelled condition The levelled condition is reached after travelling a distance of about 2000 m, depending on the road surface. Generally a loaded vehicle maintains its levelled height from one day to the next, counteracting the interruptions that occur during a journey (stops for refuelling, meals, overnight, etc.). When the vehicle is unloaded, the bodywork is raised as with a conventional spring system, and is then lowered immediately, as the fluid is transferred from the high-pressure chamber to the low-pressure chamber, up to the nominal level at which it remains. Characteristic curve of the Nivomat suspension The graph below compares the characteristic curves of a conventional shock absorber and a BOGE Nivomat self-levelling unit. The horizontal axis shows the downward movement(s) of the bodywork, while the vertical axis shows the loads (N) applied to the vehicle. The conventional shock absorber has a spring with constant stiffness, so the downward movement of the bodywork is directly proportional to the applied load (N) and its characteristic curve is linear (dashed line). With the unladen weight defined Pv and fully laden weight defined Pc, the respective operating points A* and B* are obtained on the characteristic linear curve and the relative downward movement S*. The Nivomat unit has springs which are less stiff, plus the elastic effect which varies depending on the applied load and the effect of the end-of-travel flexible buffer (dashed and dotted line). The three characteristic curves may thus be defined: characteristic curve (linear) of the mechanical spring by itself, less steep than the curve relating to the conventional shock absorber, being less stiff; characteristic curve of the Nivomat unit without load, which combines the elastic effects of the mechanical spring, the compressed gas (about 25 bar) and the end-of-travel buffer; characteristic curve of the Nivomat unit fully laden, which differs from the above because a larger proportion is taken up by the compressed gas (pressure increased to about 80 bar). Note that in the Nivomat unit, the stiffness increases as the applied load increases. The curve (2) gives the operating points A and B in the unladen and fully laden conditions, and the downward movement "S" with the vehicle at a standstill. When the vehicle sets off, in the Nivomat units the fluid is transferred from the low-pressure chamber to the high-pressure chamber, because of roughness on the road surface. When the gas pressure increases, the operating point is gradually shifted towards the left on curves with increasing stiffness, causing the vehicle to be raised. After travelling a distance of about 2000 metres, the operating point C is reached, which corresponds to a predetermined levelling condition.  Scrapping self-levelling units Before sending Nivomat self-levelling units to be scrapped, it is necessary and a duty to de-pressurize them. Under normal conditions, the internal pressure in the Nivomat units is 25 bar. If they are scrapped without being depressurized, the units could explode and could cause serious injury to people and damage to objects nearby. To depressurize Nivomat self-levelling units, two small holes must be drilled in the areas shown in the figure, corresponding to the high-pressure (1) and low-pressure (2) chambers. The holes must have a diameter of 1 mm and depth of at least 8 mm. Because of the high internal pressure, a mixture of fluid and gas will be sprayed from the holes, so it is advisable to carry out the drilling operation behind a protective shield. The self-levelling unit is depressurized when the stem can be pushed with one hand.

The radiator is a heat exchanger connected to the engine cooling circuit by means of a pipe which takes hot water from the engine to heat the air which is sent to the passenger compartment. The rotation of the outside air inlet flap is controlled by means of the recirculation actuator. This operates the flap in two extreme positions - "dynamic air" and "recirculation" without any intermediate positions. A motor controls the rotary movement of a drive pin which acts directly on the flap.

When the engine is cold, the heater unit cannnot heat the interior properly. This is particularly true of Diesel engines, which heat up more slowly. These engines may optionally be fitted with a supplementary heater system. This remains active from the moment when the engine is turned on until a certain temperature is reached. The system takes the form of an additional heater device, located on the heater unit motor coolant delivery line. This device contains three heater plugs (similar to those used to preheat the combustion chamber). OPERATION STRATEGY Heater plug operation is controlled by a special electronic control unit. This controls one, two or three plugs to provide a heating power of 200W, 400W or 600W. This control logic depends on: engine coolant outlet temperature; available electrical power level; of engine rpm Coolant outlet temperature is provided by a temperature sensor located on the line carrying coolant to the heater, immediately upstream of the additional heater device. The control system deactivates the heater plugs when engine coolant outlet temperature exceeds 70° C. The control unit also considers air temperature in the engine bay. This is not recorded by a sensor, but assumed to be the same as coolant temperature upon start-up: deactivation temperature drops from 70° C to 65° C if the assumed air temperature is higher. The second parameter - available electrical power level - is obtained from battery voltage: if the voltage exceeds 12.8 V, heater plug operation is enabled. One, two or all three heater plugs are activated below this temperature. This parameter is re-read every 10 seconds to monitor power uptake so that the battery does not go flat. Engine rpm information is used to prevent the heater plugs operating with the engine off: the enablement level is 660 rpm. for the 4 cylinder engine, it is 530 rpm. for the 5 cylinder engine. The supply of one, two or three heater plugs is controlled by two relays: 1. level: activated by the first relay; 2. level: activated by the second relay; 3. level: activated by both relays. A third relay/safety switch cuts off the power supply to the heater plugs if they are not effectively earthed. The metal device containing the spark plugs is connected to the engine earth by a braid. If this connection is cut, the relay cuts off the power supply to the heater plugs. COMPONENT LOCATION - 1, Additional heater device 2, Earth braid for additional heater 3, Additional heater relays 4, Temperature sensor for additional heater 5, Additional heater control unit 6, Additional heater coils (plugs) The additional heater device containing the three heater plugs is located on the pipe carrying coolant to the heater unit. It is secured to the engine bulkhead by a bracket. The coolant temperature sensor is fitted to the same pipe immediately upstream, i.e. in the direction of the engine thermostat. The three relays are located near the diesel filter on a special bracket fastened to the engine bulkhead. The system control unit is located beneath the facia, on the conveyer/distributor unit in both air conditioned and heated versions (next to the existing relay in this case).

AIR CONDITIONER COOLING CIRCUIT The air conditioning system is designed to cool and dehumidify the air to be introduced into the passenger compartment. The cooling circuit operates according to a common refrigerant cycle with R134a fluid where all the changes of state (from liquid to gas and viceversa) are exploited to absorb and give off heat. The operation of the system takes place at two pressure levels: the high pressure is maintained by the compressor, the low pressure by the expansion valve. The refrigerant fluid comes out of the compressor in the form of gas at a high pressure and high temperature. It then enters the condenser, undergoes refrigeration and comes out liquified. The fluid then passes through the drier filter, which absorbs any particles of water, because the water present in the pipes could, on freezing, block the expansion valve, reducing the efficiency of the cycle. In effect, in the next expansion valve, the pressure of the fluid is lowered and as a result so too is its temperature. The fluid, still in a liquid state, enters the evaporator: evaporation removes heat from the air which enters the passenger compartment. In addition, when this air comes into contact with the cold walls of the evaporator it loses a high percentage of humidity and therefore enters the vehicle colder and less humid. Lastly, the fluid returns to the compressor and the cycle begins again. 1, Compressor 2, Condenser 3, Fan motor 4, Expansion valve 5, Evaporator unit 6, Passenger compartment fan 7, Drier filter 8, 4 stage pressure switch Location of system components - 1, Air conditioning compressor 2, Pulley with compressor electro-magnet coupling 3, Air conditioning condenser 4, Drier filter 5, 4 stage pressure switch 6, Expansion valve 7, Evaporator unit Air conditioner compressor The compressor fitted on these versions is the variable capacity SANDEN SD7V16 type. According to variations in the system load conditions - changing external temperature and/or humidity or sharp variations in the engine load - the compressor processes the fluid through a capacity which starting from the maximum value of 161.3 cm 3 /rev, is gradually reduced to 10.4 cm 3 /rev: this solution is defined 'unlimited variable displacement'; it protects the evaporator against freezing so effectively that a frost sensor is not necessary. The compressor is the alternating piston type: the variation in the capacity is achieved by titling the connecting rod holder plate with a consequent variation in the piston stroke: the movement of the plate is activated by an internal adjustment valve according to the balance of pressure upstream and downstream of the compressor. In particular, a low inlet pressure involves the shuttering of the compressor (reduced capacity), whilst a high pressure involves operation at maximum power (maximum capacity). Air conditioner compressor Specifications The compressor fitted on this version is the DENSO 7SB16 variable capacity swash plate type. The compressor capacity varies between a maximum value (161.5 cc/rev) and a minimum value (8 cc/rev) according to the thermal load in the climate control system: this feature makes it possible to reduce the capacity (and therefore the compressor power) according to the refrigerant power needed. The alternating piston type compressor produces the variation in the capacity by tilting the rotary plate (swash plate) which defines the piston stroke. The way the pistons are connected to the plate, which identifies the technology, makes it possible to have a single plate which rotates and guides the pistons with the advantage of reducing vibrations, noise and torque fluctuations. The variation in the capacity is achieved by means of a regulation valve which balances the pressure inside the compressor casing according to the compressor inlet and outlet pressure. The balance of the forces due to the pressures makes it possible to adjust the inclination of the plate and, consequently, the capacity. The maximum capacity is achieved with the plate at the maximum angle, whilst with the plate almost vertical, the capacity is minimum. The compressor is started at minimum capacity thanks to a special spring. 1, Shaft 2, Plate 3, Pad 4, Piston 5, Inlet muffler 6, Valve 7, Swash plate mechanism 8, Minimum capacity spring 9, Electro-clutch pulley + Operation The drive is transmitted by the auxiliary belt to the pulley (9) and, consequently, when the electro-clutch is activated, to the shaft (1). The rotary motion is transformed into th rectilinear motion of the pistons (4) via the plate (2) which is on the shaft and slides on the piston (3) pads. The regulation valve (6) controls the capacity so that the inlet pressure is always as desired. The spring (8) keeps the plate in the minimum capacity position when the compressor is deactivated. The muffler (5) reduces the inlet gas impulses and consequently the noise and vibrations. Other system components Compressor pulley with electromagnetic coupling The compressor is engine-driven via a belt and a pulley fitted to an electromagnetic coupling. An electrical signal (12V) from the system control unit engages the coupling when the control system permits. (see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: Unit 10) Air conditioner condenser The condenser is a heat exchanger located in front of the engine cooling radiator. The structure is parallel flow type with U pipes that connect both manifolds located on the right hand side of the condenser. Each individual pipe contains up to 14 fluid ducts. The coolant, in a gaseous state, passes through the condenser pipes and liquefies (at an average temperature of 60° C). The outside of the condenser comes into contact with the air produced by the vehicle moving forwards. When the vehicle is stationary or in a traffic jam, the air is produced by the same fan used by the engine radiator (for greater detail, see wiring diagrams: 'Engine cooling'). An insufficient heat exchange in the condenser increases the pressure in the system and causes the incomplete condensation of the fluid with a considerable reduction in the efficiency of the system. Drier filter The drier filter is connected by a pipe to the evaporator inlet duct and filters the refrigerant fluid mainly in a gaseous state but partly also in a liquid state, plus the lubricant oil/anti-freeze. Any small impurities which could obstruct the expansion valve are retained by two filter layers whilst the (dehydration) water is retained by molecular sieves or a chemical compound (SILICAGEL) to prevent any particles of moisture contained in the system from freezing in the expansion valve and stopping it from working. For this reason all the system components must be stored in a dry place with the connectors sealed until the time of fitting. In the lower part of the shaped pipe, which is positioned inside the accumulator and is contact with the outlet connector, there is an opening to ensure the return of the lubricant oil to the compressor. There is a metal gauze filter seal on the above mentioned shaped pipe, by the opening for the oil. 1, Filtering layer 2, Filtering layer 3 Silicagel 4-stage pressure switch A four stage pressure switch controls the safe and correct operation of the circuit. The four pressure stages allow the compressor and the cooling fan to be switched on/off as follows: 1st level (below 2.5 bar approx): minimum pressure allowing the compressor to be switched on 2nd level (15 bar approx): pressure that requires the cooling fan to be switched on at the first speed 3rd level (20 bar approx): pressure that requires the cooling fan to be switched on at the second speed 4th level (beyond 28 bar approx): pressure too high and therefore dangerous for the entire system Expansion valve The thermostatic expansion valve fitted on the evaporator inlet and outlet ducts has the task of regulating the flow and expansion of the R134a fluid, causing it to change from the liquid state to the gaseous state before it enters the evaporator. The automatic regulation of the passage section for the refrigerant fluid inside the expansion valve is carried out by a sensitive bulb which, according to the temperature of the fluid, suitably adjusts the size of the opening by acting on a special spring which moves a shutter and determines the extent of the expansion. The increase in temperature at the evaporator outlet, measured by the bulb, causes the opening of the valve with a consequent increase in the flow rate of the fluid to the evaporator. Conversely, at low temperatures, the flow rate is decreased. The valve adjustment screw is calibrated in production and should not be tampered with: this would involve a decrease in the efficiency of the system. 1, Sensitive bulb 2, Passage 3, Spring 4, Shutter 5, Adjustment screw Evaporator The evaporator is the second heat exchanger in the system and consists of an aluminium structure with fins which increase the heat exchange surface. It is located in the duct/distributor unit. The evaporator inlet and outlet ducts are fixed to the assembly plates which constitute the heat exchange area. The evaporator is chemically treated to make it corrosion resistant. It represents the system cooling element and can have (recirculation) air coming from the passenger compartment or air from the outside passing through it for the necessary exchange of air inside the passenger compartment. The outside or recirculation air which passes through the evaporator is at a higher temperature than that of the refrigerant fluid, in a liquid state at a low pressure and temperature, which it contains and this causes evaporation (always at low pressure). At the same time, the air which comes into contact with the evaporator fins is cooled and dehumidified. The humidity which condenses on the evaporator fins is collected and discharged outside the vehicle. GLOSSARY Climate control Fully automatic system for adjusting ventilation, heating and air conditioning. The system uses an extremely sophisticated system to maintain a preset temperature inside the car, regardless of outside weather conditions. Led The LED code (Light Emitting Diode) is used for particular diodes capable of emitting light at a certain wavelength when a low voltage electric current passes through. Recirculation This is a function of the ventilation system which makes it possible to circulate the same air in the passenger compartment, excluding the intake of outside air. It is a very useful function because it makes it possible to exclude the intake of undesired outside air into the passenger compartment (fumes, air polluted by driving in traffic, etc.). Heat exchanger This device is designed (with a relatively small volume compared with the heat exchange surfaces) to allow the flow of heat from the fluid at a higher temperature to another fluid at ambient temperature. NTC sensor Negative temperature coefficient resistance. Sensor resistance alters as the temperature changes. More specifically, it drops as temperature increases. Diagnosis The control unit uses sensor monitoring and adjustment software with actuator self-adaption to record and store a series of anomalies and faults that could affect the system. These stored errors may be read using an Examiner and connecting to the diagnostic socket. Controls and functions Air flow rate/control unit off knob Rotating the air flow rate control knob in an anti-clockwise direction beyond the minimum flow rate (decrease below 0 bars and fan off) causes the climate control unit to be switched off (OFF). With the compressor enabled, the minimum air flow rate is one bar, therefore it is not possible to decrease the air flow rate below this value because the control unit would switch off. Turning the air flow rate knob, in a clockwise direction, or pressing any button whatsoever (except the heated rear windscreen and recirculation) switches the system back on, implements the requested function, if there was none previously (otherwise it confirms it) and restores all the other operating conditions that the system had memorized previously, forcing the automatic control of the flow rate if the AUTO button was used to switch it on. In OFF the recirculation button has a dual function (ON/OFF). Auto button Pressing this button cancels any previous manual intervention and restores the automatic check on the following functions: Air distribution Fan speed Compressor Driver/passenger temperature setting check The three LEDs, Compressor and AUTO, when on, indicate that all the above functions are automatically controlled. When the right LED is off this means that a Distribution or Ventilation manoeuvre has been carried out manually. The left LED also goes out (mainly when the compressor is disabled manually) if the control system does not manage to reach or maintain the desired temperature. The button (A) which disables the Compressor does not necessarily switch off the right AUTO LED. Compressor enabling/disabling button (led on - compressor enabled) Pressing the button (A) switches off the LED, the compressor is disabled and the outside air recirculation function is enabled to prevent misting. Once the button is pressed the function remains stored for an indefinite period even after the vehicle has stopped in the same way as the other manual controls. The button is dual purpose and therefore pressing it a second time re-enables the compressor and the LED comes on. If the compressor enabled LED goes out, then the right LED in the AUTO button switches off automatically. Temperature setting flashing logic With the compressor disabled the system checks whether the outside temperature is higher or lower or the same as the temperature set. Under these circumstances the passenger compartment temperature cannot be lower than the outside temperature. If the outside temperature is lower than that set, the system works normally and is capable of fulfiling the request without switching on the compressor. If the outside temperature is the same as or higher than the temperature set, then the system is not capable of supplying the temperature request by the user and signals this showing the temperature set, flashing in the display. At the same time as this flashing, the Automatic LEDs go out until the Compressor enabling command is renewed. If the outside temperature conditions higher than or the same as that set or with the button (A) on remain in the memory. The outside temperature reading flashing is repeated each time the engine is started up. Mono button Pressing the mono button has the following effect: the temperature set by the passenger button becomes the same as that set by the driver and the LED comes on. From this moment the system behaves like a single zone system. Pressing the MONO button again or changing the passenger temperature setting causes the following to happen: the MONO button LED goes out and the dual zone temperture control is restored. These functional states are maintained even after the ignition is switched on and off several times. Passenger compartment temperature setting knobs The passenger compartment temperature is set by the control unit each time the battery is connected at 24 ° C. The users can alter the temperature setting using the appropriate knobs. Turning the knobs in a clockwise direction increases the temperature set, whilst turning them in an anti-clockwise direction decreases the temperature set. The increases/decreases are in 0.5 ° C steps and one complete revolution of the knob produces 24 steps. The maximum permissible difference between the driver's selection and the passenger's selection of 7° C. Turning a knob until the above mentioned difference is reached, the system attaches the current adjustment (setting) of the knob which is still to the adjustment of the knob which is moving (neither knob takes precedence). The temperature setting range, in MONO, is 16.5 to 32.5 ° C; below 16.5 ° C the value set becomes 'LO' whilst above 32.5 ° C the value set becomes 'HI', The range goes from 16 ° C to 33° C in DUAL-ZONE operation. When the control unit is switched off, the value of the temperature set, shown in the display, is stored in the memory and restored at the next key-on. If the user selects a temperature setting lower than the outside temperature with button (B) switched off (i.e. with the compressor disabled), the impossibility of achieving the temperature requested is signalled by the flashing of the temperature setting. HIGH CONDITION (Hi) The HI or maximum heating condition is achieved by the user setting a temperature above 32.5 ° C. This request by the user switches off the Auto LED and forces the system into MONO and involves the following actions: Mixture flaps in fully hot position. Distribution flap at FLOOR Air flow rate at maximum value (seasonal) Compressor according to user request Recirculation remains as requested by user. In the HI condition, manual settings are allowed and the exit from the MONO condition, through the button, determines the exit from the HI function and the temperature setting of 32.5° C for both zones. Pressing the AUTO button causes the exit from the HI condition and the setting of 32.5° C If the driver turns the temperature setting this affects the passenger setting taking out of HI at 32.5 ° C. If the passenger turns the temperature setting then this also alters the driver's setting, taking it out of HI (at 32.5 ° C) and then they can only alter their own setting when the system is in the DuaI Zone setting. LOW CONDITION (LO) The LO condition or maximum cooling is reached by the user setting a temperature below 16.5° C. This request by the user switches off the AUTO LEDs and forces the system into MONO and involves the following actions: Mixture flaps in fully cold position. Distribution flap in VENT Air flow rate at maximum value (seasonal) Compressor enabled Recirculation remains as requested by user. If the request is Automatic, the flap is forced shut when the passenger compartment Temp. <T ext. It returns to the normal Automatic logic on exit from LO. In the LO condition, manual settings are allowed and the exit from the MONO condition determines the exit from the LO function and the setting of the temperature for both zones at 16.5° C. Pressing the AUTO button causes the exit from the LO condition and a setting of 16.5° C. If the driver rotates the temperature setting it moves the passenger adjustment (setting) outside of LO, to 16.5 ° C. If the passenger changes the temperature setting the driver's setting also moves outside of LO (at 16.5 ° C) and then the setting can only be changed with the system in the DuaI Zone setting. Air distribution control The MODE button for managing the Distribution is the rocker type and therefore operates with a clockwise or anti-clockwise ROLLING logic. There are 5 air distribution positions (VENTI, BI-LVEL, HEAT, FLOOR and DEF). With Automatic Distribution the system controls the distribution direction and displays the choice with the appropriate arrows in the centre display coming on. Automatic control can, in the presence of fairly strong sunshine, force the distribution to search for the maximum possible comfort level (FLOOR ->BI-LEVEL and BI-LEVEL -> VENT). MANUAL DISTRIBUTION SETTING One of the 5 positions can be selected manually by operating the MODE button repeatedly (rolling clockwise or anti-clockwise) and producing the following distributions: clockwise direction: DEF, HEAT, FLOOR, BI-LIVEL, VENT. anti-clockwise direction: DEF, VENT, BI-LEVEL, FLOOR, HEAT. Each distrbution will be shown by the arrows in the centre display which light up individually or in combination according to the configuration described above. Recirculation button Pressing the recirculation button determines three possible types of operation, in order, according to the following logic: 1. automatic recirculation (amber LED on) 2. forced recirculation closed or on (passenger compartment inside air, orange LED on). 3. forced recirculation open or off (passenger compartment outside air, orange LED off - amber LED off). AUTOMATIC OPERATION The recirculation is managed automatically (opening/closing) depending on both the quality of the intake air and the thermal adjustment changes. The 'Intake air quality' sensor determines the requests for closing the recirculation flap when the concentration of harmful gases exceeds dangerous levels. In particular, it is capable of distinguishing the following levels: Clean air 1st level pollution Sensor broken These requests are monitored by the control unit and, as planned, the flap is opened/closed depending on the level of pollution detected. In any case, if a safety procedure is in progress (e.g. MAX-DEF) the flap remains in the DYNAMIC position. In Automatic mode the right LED remains on to signal the automatic operation whilst the left LED comes on during closed recirculation and switches off during open recirculation. FORCED RECIRCULATION CLOSED OR ON (PASSENGER COMPARTMENT INSIDE AIR) In this type of manual operation, signalled by the right LED being off, the left LED coming on signals the closing of the recirculation flap. FORCED RECIRCULATION OPEN OR OFF (PASSENGER COMPARTMENT OUTSIDE AIR) In this type of manual operation, signalled by the right LED being off, the left LED going out signals the forced opening of the outside air flap. FORCED RECIRCULATION CLOSED OR ON (PASSENGER COMPARTMENT INSIDE AIR) WITH VEHICLE STATIONARY In Automatic mode, to prevent the intake of air into the passenger compartment which is polluted by the exhaust gases when the vehicle is stationary, when the speed of the vehicle is approaching zero (6 km/h), the system controls the closing of the recirculation. When the speed of the vehicle increases again to above 12 km/h, the system restores the pre-existing automatic mode conditions. This logic does not apply with the Compressor disabled. Fan speed control knob The air flow rate can be manually adjusted in steps, with one bar on the display representing 3 steps, up to a maximum of 6 bars and then it switches off. If there have been no manual interventions, the fan speed is continuously controlled in automatic mode and the appropriate number of bars light up on the display depending on the flow rate. The control unit is capable of regulating the air flow rate according to the outside temperature. The temperature bands are: outside temperature < 15° C; from 15° C to 25° C and > 25° C. Manual intervention on the fan control results in the exit from the AUTO condition. In particular, to increase or decrease the fan speed, turn the centre knob in a clockwise or anti-clockwise direction, respectively. With the ignition key in the ON position, if the control unit is controlling the air flow rate in Automatic mode, then this air flow rate is at 1 bar (minimum flow rate) until the engine is started up. If the compressor is disabled, the ventilation control can be adjusted manually until the display shows 0 bars. If the compressor is enabled and the engine is started up, the manual ventilation cannot go below 1 bar shown on the display, because, with the compressor enabled, there must be a minimum air flow rate to prevent the evaporator from freezing. Max def button The MAX DEF procedure manages the flow rate and the distribution of the air with the aim of demisting the windows as quickly as possible. When the MAX DEF button is pressed, the system carries out the following operations: MAX DEF LED comes on Memorizing the functional state and MAX DEF previous displays Switching off of right LED, AUTO button and automatic recirculation (if on) Switching on of the DEF distribution, compressor enabling, MONO, HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN Temperature display on fully hot (HI) on both side displays Ventilation on centre display. In addition, the activation of the following commands: Air flow rate with 4 bars displayed Distribution flap in Def position (before Mix implementation) Mixture flaps in Max Heat position (after implementation of Def) Forced air intake flap open (dynamic) Compressor function enabled Rear windscreen defrosting During the operation of the MAX-DEF it is possible to: alter the air flow rate (increase/decrease) at will deactivate the heated rear windscreen Deactivating the MAX-DEF control only causes the heated rear windscreen to switch off if it was already on and the command to switch on was given by MAX-DEF; in all other cases, the heated rear windscreen remains on. It is not possible to: Alter the temperature setting (driver/passenger) Alter the distribution setting. It is possible to interrupt the MAX-DEF function by operating any of the climate control buttons (Recirculation, Compressor Enabling, Auto, Mono, MAX-DEF) implementing the return to the previous condition MAX DEF condition and implementing the command for the button pressed. The management of the MAX-DEF procedure takes precedence over the management of the following procedures: LO (maximum cold) HI (maximum heat) Their execution, if in progress, is interrupted if the MAX-DEF procedure is activated. The MAX DEF lasts for 3 minutes. Heated rear windscreen The rear defrosting is implemented both through the special button and through the MAX DEF procedure. The display of the function state is shown by the LED coming on/going off. The function requesting the activation of the heated rear windscreen is only subordinate to the key on. The HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN function is not memorized with the ignition switched OFF. Climate control sensors Outside air temperature sensor The NTC sensor is fitted on the door mirror and has an operating range of between -40° C and 80° C The system checks the sensor and updates the value in the following conditions: temperature measured higher than that memorized: the update only takes place if the speed of the vehicle is equal to or above 30 km/h and the increase in temperature is measured for more than a minute temperature measured equal to or below that memorized: the system updates the value of the outside temperature Treated air temperature sensors There are four treated air temperature sensors. They are positioned in the duct which directs the air to the lower (floor) vents and near the centre vents (vent). They are NTC sensors (where the resistance decreases as the temperature increases) with an operating range of -40° C to 100° C, accuracy 0.5 ° C, Resistance at 25° C: 10Kohm ± 5%. 1 - Left vent treated air sensor 2 - Right vent treated air sensor 3 - Left floor treated air sensor 4 - Right floor treated air sensor Passenger compartment inside air temperature sensor This is an NTC sensor incorporated in the climate control unit, resistance at 25° C: 10Kohm ± 5%, operating range -40° C +100° C. The sensor is ventilated; in effect, it incorporates a small, brushless type fan with 6 vanes with a rotation speed of 3600 ± 600 rpm and an air supply > 2.0 m/s. The latter is always supplied so that the temperature reading is not affected by the hot air inside the dashboard. Solar sensor The solar radiation sensor is positioned on the facia near the windscreen. It is the DUAL ZONE type for the optimum control of the dual climate control system temperatures. The task of this sensor is to convert light signals (lux or kcal/m2h) into a proportional electrical linear signal. The sensor is a specific type of diode (photodiode) that can alter its rate of conduction according to the amount of light that strikes it; in practice, the light that strikes the lens of the photodiodes releases electrons from the crystal grating. A superabundance of electrons and gaps therefore appear. The electrons flow toward the photodiode spatial charge or junction area (NP) and increase junction current (photoelectric current) in proportion with light intensity. In order to achieve a very high response rate, the photodiode is fitted with a lens designed to focus light more effectively on the photodiode semiconductor junction (N-P). Using this signal, the control unit (NCL) varies the temperature parameters decreasing it, acting on the air distribution at the same time. Pollution sensor (a.q.s.) The pollution sensor is an electronic device which is designed to supply an enabling signal for the recirculation flap when the air pollution index exceeds the pre-set level, to prevent the introduction of polluted air into the passenger compartment. On return to normal conditions, the NCL restores the recirculation to the position prior to the activation of the function. It is fitted in the dynamic air intake compartment under the windscreen. The AQS sensor is an integrated system complete with sensitive element, processor and output interface. By using a special sensitive element it is possible to detect the presence, in the air around the vehicle, of harmful oxidizing particles (e.g. CO) or reducing particles (e.g. NOx). The sensitive element is heated and regulated at a constant temperature of 300° C to provide the same performance in an ambient temperature range of between -25° C and 85° C. It is not affected by the speed and the temperature of the air passing through. Misting sensor The misting sensor is a device which operates without contact, using electronic and optic technology to detect the presence of droplets of water (misting) on the inner surface of the windscreen or the rearscreen of a vehicle. The information coming from the misting sensor is sent to the vehicle's climate control system to provide the demisting strategy. 1 - Misting sensor The sensor casing is made from high resistance polypropylene; since it works without contact it is fitted on the mounting bracket for the rear view mirror in such a position that it does not affect the driver's vision, not only for aesthetic reasons, but also so that it is not exposed to direct sunlight as the UV rays could damage it. The only part of the sensor that is visible is the frame (a rapid attachment cover which acts as an optic lens and an aesthetic cover for the sensor) which conducts the infrared rays to the measuring surface and collect the energy reflected. This frame is usually dark red and looks almost black. In practice, this sensor (equipped with photodiodes) is capable of transforming the light signals into a proportional electrical signal which is sent to the control unit (NCL). Using this signal, the control unit varies the parameters of the output air temperature, increasing it and altering the distribution and the speed of the actual air. SENSOR SPECIFICATIONS Sensor specifications are as follows: The sensor is activated at operating voltages between 10 and 16V. The operating temperature is between -20° C and 70° C. The sensor is capable of working in an ambient where the humidity is 95%. It is able to withstand a high level of vibrations without its performance being affected thanks to the type of fastening with a special algorhythm in its software. It can normally work up to an altitude of 3500 m and can withstand falls from a height of 1 m from the ground without suffering damage and with its performance unaffected and has been designed to prevent the entry of dust. Removing a layer of dust does not alter the calibration or adversely affect performance. MAINTENANCE The sensor does not require any maintenance except for the regular cleaning of the lens cover (or frame). It may be necessary to clean the lens cover when there is a large build up of dirt or impurities on the lens which prevent the reception and transmission of an acceptable quantity of light. The lens should be cleaned using a weak solution of soap and water. Actuators Stepping motors The rotor which includes a certain number of pairs of permanent polymagnets, is in a rest position (minimum magnetic energy) due to the polar configuration imposed by the outside of the electro-magnetically energized stator. 1 - Rotor 2 - Stator A casing 3 - Stator B casing 4 - Winding A 5 - Winding B If the reversal of polarity of the energizing windings is carried out correctly by the digitally controlled orders, the rotor turns exactly one step in the direction selected and moves into a new rest position. In this case the energizing current is independent from the load and if it is applied with a rapid sequence of pulses (frequency) the stepping movement is transformed into a practically continuous movement. As with direct current geared motors, the polarity of the stator windings is correctly reversed by means of switches which are formed by electronic power stages in the control unit. The number of steps for each rotation results from the number of polar pairs (P) of the rotor and the number of phases (m) for the stator. The typical positioning accuracty for these geared motors is about ± 5% of the stepping angle and is mainly not connected to the total of positioning steps i.e. the positioning angle. The angular increments (usually > 1.8°) can vary according to the task that the geared motor has to perform. These types of geared motor are widely used in new systems. Air mixture flap actuators The actuators rotate the mixture flaps according to the control unit command. A motor with a 12 volt supply controls the rotary movement of a drive pin which acts directly on the mixture flaps. SPECIFICATIONS: nominal voltage 12V nominal operating frequency 200 Hz nominal speed 1.67 RPM steps per revolution 7200 (7200 impulses for 1 revolution) reduction ratio 300 coil resistance 84 ohm Air distribution actuator The actuator moves via a rack slide, with guiding splines which contain the bearings and two levers; there are 5 possible positions for the distribution flaps: Main: DEF, VENT, FLOOR Combined: BILEVEL, HEAT. SPECIFICATIONS: nominal voltage 12V nominal operating frequency 200 Hz nominal speed 5 RPM steps per revolution 2400 (2400 impulses per rev) reduction ratio 100 coil resistance 70 ohm Recirulation actuator The recirculation actuator rotates the flap in the two dynamic air and recirculation extreme positions wihout intermediate positions. A motor with a 12 V supply controls the rotary movement of a drive pin which acts directly on the flap. Reversing the polarity produces movement in the opposite direction SPECIFICATIONS: nominal voltage 12V nominal operating frequency 200 Hz nominal speed 5 RPM steps per revolution 2400 reduction ratio 100 coil resistance 70 ohm The closing of the flap takes place in < 2.5 secs The feedback control on all the mixture, distribution and recirculation motors is carried out by measuring the difference in the current absorbed by the coils supplied to identify a loss in steps corresponding to a mechanical failure or sticking. Each time a new actuator is fitted the learning test has to be carried out using the diagnostic equipment. Evaporator The evaporator is a heat exchanger fitted inside the blower/distributor unit. It consists of an aluminium structure with fins which increase the heat exchange surface. The evaporator is smaller than the condenser. The refrigerant in the evaporator changes from a liquid state to vapour which is slightly overheated. This change in state is produced by directing the hot, humid air which needs to be treated onto the evaporator using fan. As the temperature of the air is higher than that of the refrigerant, it gives off some of its heat; on cooling, the humidity contained condenses on the evaporator fins in the form of droplets. They are collected in a chamber and discharged. This produces cool, dehumidified air. The effective cooling is due to the change in state of the coolant fluid from a liquid to a gas. This change takes place with a great deal of heat absorption. The process takes place extremely quickly because the liquid is introduced into the coil atomized and at low pressure through the expansion valve jet. It can therefore evaporate very rapidly along the coil, absorbing a considerable amount of heat. If the evaporator coils are not supplied with sufficient refrigerant, the evaporation is limited; in this case, operation would be poor with an insufficient heat exchange. In the opposite case, if the supply to the evaporator coils is too large, the evaporation of the coolant in the coils would be incomplete. In this case, the coolant might return to the compressor, in a liquid state, which would damage the compressor pistons and the valves. In addition, under these circumstances, operation would be poor with insufficient heat exchange. Too high a pressure reading on the inlet pressure gauge or excessive oozing from the evaporator coils and the intake pipes, accompanied by poor evaporator cooling, indicate that the coil is receiving excessive refrigerant. The evaporator can receive air from inside the vehicle (recirculation air) or from the outside, thereby producing an exchange of air inside the passenger compartment. The evaporator is chemically treated to be resistant to corrosion. Heater This is a heat exchanger connected to the engine cooling circuit by means of special pipes: one draws hot water from the engine and allows the heating of the air introduced into the passenger compartment, the other allows the return of the coolant to the engine. Additional heater p.t.c. (diesel versions) The additional PTC heater, available as an optional extra on the JTD versions, is designed to heat the passenger compartment more quickly wih the engine running (rpm > 700 rpm) in the case of adverse weather conditions (for example, particularly cold climate). It is a resistance located near the radiant mass with a maximum power of 750 W and a voltage of 13.5 V. The voltate at connector A determines 30% of the heater power. The voltage at connectors B-C determines 70% of the heater power. The PTC is deactivated with the air flow rate at 0. Interior fan The fan that sends outside or recirculation air to the evaporator battery is controlled by a permanent magnet electric motor. It is located inside the casing, near the evaporator; it receives a 12 V supply and is operated at different speeds by an electronic governor located nearby. 1 - Fan speed electronic governor 2 - Electric fan Electronic governor The different fan rotation speeds are controlled by an electronic governor fixed to the actual duct. The governor controls the voltage and therefore the motor supply current consequently controlling the fan speed and air cubic metres/hour. In addition, the governor processes a feedback signal with a frequency proportional to the fan rotation speed. It is used as a control signal for the rotation speed of the motor to diagnose increases in temperature due to current absorption or excessive mechanical resistance; in practice, any malfunctions. Pollen filter There is a combined type air filter (PARTICLES + ACTIVE CHARCOAL) for the passenger compartment to improve comfort. The former makes it possible to prevent the intake of pollen and pollutant particles into the passenger compartment; the latter reduces the tiresome sensation produced by unpleasant smelling substances due to dampness forming on the surfaces. 1 - Filter 2 - Cover The main specifications of the filter element are: high filtering capacity: the filter retains more than 55% of particles with dimensions between 3 and 5 microns and more than 90% between 5 and 10 microns. easy to replace. CONSTRUCTION FEATURES TWIN LEVEL AUTOMATICALLY CONTROLLED CLIMATE CONTROL SYSTEM The automatic climate control is managed by a control unit which, thanks to an extremely sophisticated operating logic, is capable of controlling the temperature in two areas of the passenger compartment, heating or cooling the incoming air so that it reaches the desired temperature. It is also capable of demisting the windscreen surface and the side windows relatively quickly which improves safety. This performance is achieved thanks to the excellent software logic and the air distribution.
