Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Check that the battery voltage is over 9 V Continue to Step 1 Battery voltage below 9 V: in these conditions the door locks are not supplied by the control unit Restore the correct battery voltage 1 CHECK OPERATION OF INDIVIDUAL DOORS All OK Problems met Operation Check that, when the door lock/unlock is operated, none of the locks is activated Continue to Step 2 Fault in one of the front locks Check and if necessary replace the front door lock motors Op. 7005N21 Fault in one of the rear locks Check and if necessary replace the rear door lock motors Op. 7010N21 Faulty connection between services control unit and one of the locks door lock motors See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING 2 CENTRAL LOCKING ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check, in order: central locking fuse, located in junction unit connection between junction unit and services unit services control unit supply correct operation of services control unit See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING Continue to Step 3 Connections not correct Restore connections Component defective Replace the component involved (if a fuse is involved, search for the cause of the problem) Control unit not working Replace the services control unit Op. 5505A18 3 CORRECT OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom' When the central door locking is operated with the key (or remote control) the doors do not open / close at all. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Check that the battery voltage is over 9 V Continue to Step 1 Battery voltage below 9 V (in this case the locks are not supplied by the control unit). Restore the correct battery voltage 1 DOOR OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check that the doors lock/unlock properly using the key. Continue to Step 2 Fault in the front locks Check and if necessary replace the front door lock motors ( Op. ) 7005N21 Fault in the rear locks Check and if necessary replace the rear door lock motors ( Op. ) 7005N21 Lack of continuity between control unit and door lock geared motors Restore the continuity between the control unit and the door lock geared motor, if necessary, replacing the wiring. 2 CENTRAL LOCKING ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check, in order: central locking fuse located in services control unit connection between services control unit and junction unit ( See ) E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING Continue to Step 3 Component defective Replace the component involved (if a fuse is involved, search for the cause of the problem) Connection damaged Restore connections 3 INTEGRATED ELECTRIC WINDOWS CENTRAL LOCKING ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNIT All OK Problems met Operation Check that the integrated electric windows central locking is working properly Continue to Step 4 Control unit not working Replace the integrated electric windows central locking control unit ( Op. ) 5505A18 4 CORRECT OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

When the central locking is operated using the remote control the doors do not open / close at all. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Check the charge of the remote control incorporated in the key Check that the central locking is working properly using the key Continue to Step 1 Remote control battery run down Replace battery Central locking mechanical fault See table P10 CENTRAL LOCKING 1 REMOTE CONTROL RECEIVER CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the supply, earth and connections with the integrated electric windows central locking control unit Continue to Step 2 Connections damaged Restore the correct connections Component defective Replace the alarm remote control receiver 2 CENTRAL LOCKING ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check, in order: central locking fuse, located in service control unit connection between service control unit and junction unit control unit supply ( See ) E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING Continue to Step 3 Component defective Replace the component involved (if a fuse is involved, search for the cause of the problem) Connection damaged Restore connections 3 INTEGRATED ELECTRIC WINDOWS CENTRAL LOCKING ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNIT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check that the integrated electric windows central locking control unit is working properly Continue to Step 4 Control unit not working Replace integrated electric windows central locking control unit ( Op. ) 5505A18 4 CORRECT OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

The sunroof does not move at all when its control is operated Results of the tests 1 CHECK SUNROOF SUPPLY CIRCUIT All OK Problems met Operation Check, in order: sunroof supply fuse sunroof supply fuse sunroof electronic control unit connections between relay, fuse and sunroof electronic control unit See E3060 SUN ROOF Continue to Step 2 Connections not correct Restore the connections Component defective Replace the component involved (if a fuse is involved, search for the cause of the problem) Electronic control unit not working Replace control unit Op. 7030B66 2 CHECK SUNROOF MOTOR All OK Problems met Operation Check the operation of the sunroof motor In particular, ascertain: condition of motor pinion state of control rack Continue to Step 3 Faults in motor components Replace the motor Op. 7030B70 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

When the control is operated, the sun-roof opens/closes in irregular manner. It sticks at some points or remains locked at an angle Results of the tests 1 CHECKING SUN-ROOF All OK Problems met Operation Remove the glass Op. 7030B18 Check the sun-roof operating devices are working properly. Check in particular: control cable condition slide and guide condition presence of end travel blocks Continue to Step 2 Dirty guides Clean the guides and repair the slide mechanism End stop screws missing Replace the screws and the entire slide mechanism Guides disconnected Repair the slide mechanism Op. 7030B50 2 CHECKING SUN-ROOF CONTROL DEVICES All OK Problems met Operation Remove the motor. Op. 7030B70 Check that sun-roof opening devices are working properly. Check in particular: condition of motor pinion control cable condition Continue to Step 3 faults in sun-roof operating devices Replace the components involved 3 CHECKING SUN-ROOF CONTROL DEVICE ALIGNMENT All OK Problems met Operation Check installation of the sun-roof assembly In particular, ascertain: slides are properly aligned with timing points flexible racks are properly secured and undamaged Continue to Step 4 Faulty fitting of the sunroof Refit the sunroof correctly Op. 7030B54 4 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

When the control is operated, the sun roof opens/closes normally, but does not stop correctly in the opening, hinged opening or closing positions Results of the tests 1 CONTROL DEVICE ALIGNMENT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Remove the glass Op. and check that the slides and the guides are correctly aligned 7030B18 Continue to Step 2 Faulty fitting of the sunroof Refit the sunroof correctly Op. 7030B54 2 SUN ROOF END OF TRAVEL DEVICE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition of the end of travel switch and the control cam, located on the motor Continue to Step 3 End of travel device faulty Renew the connections or replace the motor Op. 7030B70 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

When the key is turned to the ON position, the AIR BAG warning light remains on after 5 secs. The AIR BAG warning light remains on after a fairly severe impact. Check whether the AIR BAG control unit has intervened and, if it has, replace it. The engine is making a cyclical noise, noticeable when the engine is hot during brisk acceleration and using long ratios Preliminarily check: the type of fuel that there is no water or dirt in the tank Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Check the type of fuel Preliminarily check that there is no water or other fluids in the fuel tank Continue to Step 1 Presence of dirt in the fuel tank Clean the fuel tank Op. 1040A10 Fuel unsuitable Clean the fuel tank Op. and fill with suitable fuel 1040A10 1 TYPE OF NOISE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Carry out a road test and check whether the noise sounds metallic during brisk acceleration and using long ratios Metallic sound: Continue to Step 2 Duller sound: probably knocking Overhaul the engine: check the condition of the main bearings and replace them: Op. 1024A10 2 CHECK WITH DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems met Operation Connect the diagnostic equipment (Examiner or other instruments) to the diagnostic socket Check: that there are no faults in the engine management control unit plausibility of all the parameters Continue to Step 3 An error is detected in the control unit Continue according to the instructions for the diagnostic equipment Lack of dialogue with the control unit Restore the connection between the engine management control unit and the diagnostic connector See E5030 PETROL ENGINE ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT 3 PISTON CROWN CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Remove the cylinder head and check the condition of the piston crowns Continue to Step 4 Deposits on the piston crowns Remove the deposits or replace the pistons and connecting rods (see Assembly 1028H) 4 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

There is buzzing (low frequency noise) coming from the engine, whose intensity varies with the number of revs Results of the tests 1 AIR CIRCUIT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check: the condition and seal of the air supply circuit Continue to Step 2 Circuit component damaged Replace the component (see Assembly 1048A) 2 ENGINE EXHAUST CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check: the condition and the seal of the engine exhaust pipes Continue to Step 3 Pipe, silencer or connector damaged Replace the components (see Assembly 1076B) 3 VALVE LEAKAGE TEST All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition and the seal of the timing valves Continue to Step 4 Valves damaged Replace the component (see ENGINE OVERHAUL, Subassembly 1016) 4 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

There is a whistling (extremely high intensity noise) coming from the area of the engine which varies with the engine speed Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition of the auxiliary shaft drive belt and check that the tension is correct Check that, as the electrical loads engaged increase, the whistling does not increase, but remains constant Continue to Step 1 Tension incorrect Replace the belt Op. 1092G10 The whistling increases: alternator faulty (voltage regulator not working properly) Replace the voltage regulator Op. 5530A22 The whistling increases: alternator faulty (connections between alternator and battery not correct) Restore the connections ( See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING 1 CHECK AUXILIARY SHAFT BELT All OK Problems met Operation Disconnect the belt to see if the whistling stops. ATTENTION do not run the engine too long with the belt disconnected The whistling disappears: Continue to Step 2 The whistling remains constant Restore the belt control system, in particular, belt tensioner P Op. 1092G10 2 CHECK ON COMPONENTS DRIVEN BY THE BELT All OK Problems met Operation Check the operation of all the components driven by the belt: water pump power assisted steering pump air conditioning compressor Continue to Step 3 Water pump faulty Restore or replace the water pump Op. 1088C12 Power assisted steering pump faulty Restore or replace the water pump Op. 4130B20 Air conditioning compressor faulty Restore or replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

There is a constant, loud noise coming from the area of the engine, which is only heard within a certain engine speed range Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition and seal of the air supply circuit Continue to Step 1 Circuit component damaged Replace the component (see Assembly 1048A) 1 ENGINE SUPPORT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition and the correct fixing of the engine supports and flexible mountings and the reaction rods Continue to Step 2 Engine supports faulty Bed in the fixings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque (see Assembly 1008A) Flexible mountings faulty Bed in the fixings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque (see Assembly 1008B) Reaction rod faulty Bed in the fixings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque (see Assembly 1008C) 2 ENGINE EXHAUST CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition and the correct fixing of the engine exhaust pipe flexible supports Continue to Step 3 Support slack or damaged Restore or replace the support (see Assembly 1076A) Pipe, silencer or connector damaged Replace the components (see Assembly 1076B) 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

There is a constant load noise coming from the area of the engine, which is repeated at regular intervals Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition and tension of the auxiliary shaft drive belt Continue to Step 1 Tension not correct Replace the belt Op. 1092G10 1 AUXILIARY DRIVE BELT CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the belt tensioners and, in particular, the bearings Continue to Step 2 Belt tensioner bearings damaged Replace the belt tensioner (see Assembly 1092G) 2 WATER PUMP CHECK All OK Problems met Operation 1.6 TS 1.8 TS [d] 1.9 JTD 8v 2.4 JTD 10v Check the water pump and, in particular, the condition of the bearing Continue to Step 3 Water pump bearing damaged Replace the water pump Op. 1088C12 2.5 V6 Check the water pump and, in particular, the condition of the battery, making sure it is correctly fixed Continue to Step 3 Pulley damaged or fixing incorrect Renew the correct fixing or replace the pulley Op. 1088C24 3 ALTERNATOR CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the alternator and, in particular: the condition of the bearing the correct fixing of the pulley Continue to Step 4 Alternator bearing damaged Replace the alternator Op. 5530A14 Pulley fixing incorrect Restore the correct pulley fixing Op. 0 5530A30 4 CORRECT OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

There is a constant, low frequency noise, only noticeable for short periods of time Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Carry out a preliminary test to check the conditions which give rise to the noise The noise does not reoccur: Continue to Step 3 The noise increases considerably with the steering in the end of travel position See table S35 The noise also occurs with the engine switched off (when warm) Continue to Step 1 The noise increases during braking Continue to Step 2 1 MULTI-PURPOSE VALVE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition of the multi-purpose valve, located on the fuel filler pipe Continue to Step 3 Valve faulty Replace the valve pump Op. 1040A30 2 BRAKE SERVO VACUUM VALVE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the condition of the one-way valve on the brake servo vacuum pipe Continue to Step 36 Brake servo valve faulty Replace the valve Op. 3330D20 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

With the engine running and the vehicle moving, there is a noise from the area of the gearbox in all conditions. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Carry out a preliminary test to check the conditions which give rise to the noise General noise: Continue to Step 1 Noise during take-off See table S21 Noise in neutral See table S22 Noise in one gear only See table S23 Noise round bends See table S24 1 GEARBOX/DIFFERENTIAL OIL LEVEL CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the gearbox / differential oil level Op. 2110A04 Continue to Step 2 Level too low Restore the correct level 2 CHECK GEARS All OK Problems met Operation Service the gearbox (SEE GEARBOX SERVICING Assembly 2110B) Op. In particular, check the gear teeth: they should not be worn or show traces of seizing 2110B32 Continue to Step 3 Gears worn Replace the gears involved 3 CHECK SYNCHRONIZER RINGS All OK Problems met Operation Service the gearbox (SEE GEARBOX SERVICING Assembly 2110B) In particular, check the gear teeth: they should not be worn or show traces of seizing Continue to Step 4 Seals worn Replace the synchronizers 4 REDUCTION TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the crown wheel and pinion reduction gear (see OVERHAULING GEARBOXES Assembly 2110D) In particular: it should not be worn or damaged there should not be excessive clearance Continue to Step 5 Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear 5 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

With the engine running, when the various gears are engaged, there is a noise during take-off: the noise varies as the speed varies Results of the tests 1 CHECKING THE GEAR SET All OK Problems met Operation Check the crown wheel and pinion reduction gear (see OVERHAULING GEARBOXES Assembly 2110D) In particular: it should not be worn or damaged there should not be excessive clearance the ring gear fixings should not be slack Continue to Step 2 Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear 2 CHECKING PLANET CARRIER All OK Problems met Operation Check the wear of the planet carrier or the housing in the differential case (see OVERHAULING GEARBOXES Assembly 2110D) Continue to Step 3 Differential case worn Replace the differential casing 3 CHECKING CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

With the engine running and the gearbox in neutral, there is noise from the area of the gearbox Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Visually inspect whether the fault is accompanied by an oil leak from the gearbox / differential Press the clutch pedal and check whether the noise increases Check the gearbox / differential oil level Op. 2110A04 Continue to Step 1 Oil leaks from the gearbox See table X15 With the clutch pressed, the noise disappears or decreases considerably The noise is coming from inside the gearbox: See table S20 Oil level too low Restore the correct level and carry out a road test. If the defect persists, Continue to Step 1 1 CHECK SPLINED HUB All OK Problems met Operation Check for excess grease on the clutch plate hub bushes and the gearbox main shaft Continue to Step 2 Gearbox main shaft hub faulty Replace the gearbox main shaft (see OVERHAULING GEARBOXES Assembly 2110B) Clutch plate hub bushes faulty Restore the correct lubrication for the bushes If necessary, replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 2 CLUTCH PLATE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check: clutch plate wear clutch plate fouling (oil or grease) that the clutch plate is not distorted that there is no damage to the pressure plate diaphragm spring Continue to Step 3 Clutch plate or pressure plate faulty Replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 Presence of oil or grease Also replace the gearbox input oil seal Op. 2110C22 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

With the engine running, a noise is heard (whilsting inside the gearbox) when a specific gear is engaged This noise decreases or disappears on changing gear. Results of the tests 1 CHECK SYNCHRONIZER RINGS All OK Problems met Operation Overhaul the gearbox (see OVERHAULING GEARBOX Assembly 2110B). In particular, check the synchronizer rings for the gear involved: they should not show signs of wear on the inner surfaces Continue to Step 2 Seals worn Replace the synchronizers 2 CHECK GEARS All OK Problems met Operation Overhaul the gearbox (see OVERHAULING GEARBOX Assembly 2110B). In particular, check the teeth of the gear concerned: they should not be worn or show signs of seizing Continue to Step 3 Gears worn Replace the gears involved 3 REDUCTION TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the crown wheel and pinion reduction gear (see OVERHAULING GEARBOX Assembly 2110D) In particular: it should not be worn or damaged there should not be excessive clearance Continue to Step 4 Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear 4 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

Whilst driving round a bend (right or left) there is a noise from the area of the gaerbox. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Steer to the right or the left and check whether the noise increases. Steer on full lock and then release the steering wheel: check whether the intensity of the noise increases or decreases with the steering angle Continue to Step 1 The noise only increases when steering to the right or the left See table S40 The noise stops along a straight line See table S45 The noise level increases as the steering angle increases Check the constant velocity joints: Continue to Step 2 The noise remains constant as the steering angle increases Check the differential: Continue to Step 1 1 DIFFERENTIAL CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the differential, in particular the bearings (see OVERHAULING GEARBOXES Assembly 2110D) Continue to Step 3 Bearings damaged Replace the bearings Gears worn or damaged Overhaul or replace the differential housing 2 CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINTS CHECK All OK Problems met Operation Check the transmission constant velocity joints Continue to Step 3 Joint damaged Replace the joint Op. 2710A20 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis Fault persists Search for the fault starting from another symptom'

When operating the clutch pedal, there is a noise Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation With the engine idling and the gear lever in neutral, press the clutch pedal. During braking, a whistle or screech may be heard from the area of the wheels. Vibration may also be detected in the interior compartment. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems met Operation Steer to the right or the left and check whether the noise increases. Noise does not change: Continue to Step 1 The noise varies during steering See table S45 1 CHECK PAD TYPE AND SURFACE All OK Problems met Operation Check: condition of pad friction surfaces pad type Continue to Step 2 Front friction surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water Brake pads wrong type Clean, check and eliminate the causes of the fault. Replace the pads if necessary Op. 3310A60 Rear friction surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water Brake pads wrong type Clean, check and eliminate the causes of the fault. Replace the pads if necessary. WARNINGS The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperature and live electrical wires. The precautions given below should be scrupulously followed when working in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. No smoking. No naked flames. Ensure that there is a fire extinguisher nearby. WARNINGS During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts and all components which have deteriorated.

Loosen the bands and remove the pipe between the fuel filter and the pressure pump. Connect a pressure gauge (0 - 5 bar) between the fuel filter and the pressure pump. Place the ignition key in the ON position and, within 30 seconds, check that the pressure is 1.8 - 3.0 bar.

Proceed with the removal . 1016A10 sound-proofing cover - r + r Proceed with the removal . 1060G16 pressure relief sensor - r r Connect the tool (1a) with the connecting pipe (1b) to the intake chamber in the housing for the excess pressure sensor. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the Examiner/SDC diagnostic instrument in the interior compartment and make the connections. Select the 'pressure gauge' instrument on the Examiner and set it to acquire data in 'inlet pressure' mode with full scale of 2000 mmHg and time selection 10 seconds. Go out onto the road (observing the legal speed limits) and carry out the following test. On a stretch of motorway, drive the car at 2500 rpm in 4th gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part (*), excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 1900-2080 mbar (1444-1581 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 900-1080 mbar. On a fast non-urban journey, drive the car at 2500 rpm in 3rd gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part (*), excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 1900-2080 mbar (1444-1581 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 900-1080 mbar. This test works for the Examiner diagnostic instrument. For the SDC diagnostic instrument, the part relating to the setting of the instrument and graphic acquisition should be revised. Visually inspect that whilst the engine is being started (key in AVV position) the turbocharger actuator connecting rod (turbine stator vane positioning device) moves by about 10 mm in the direction of the actuator. With the engine switched off, connect connector EX09 with transducer EX06 to the section of pipe between the actuator and the solenoid valve. In the instrument ambient, select the intake pressure measurement pressure gauge. Start the engine and let it idle, then wait until the pressure level stabilizes. The pressure reading should be between 450 and 500 mmHg. The graphic acquisition of the pressure can be made by selecting the scale 2000 - 4000 mmHg. The pressure reading should be between 250 and 350 mmHg. The graphic acquisition of the pressure can be made by selecting the scale 2000 - 4000 mmHg. Visually inspect that whilst the engine is being started (key in START position) the turbocharger actuator connecting rod (turbine stator vane positioning device) moves by about 10 mm in the direction of the actuator. CHECK USING EXAMINER With the engine switched off, connect connector EX09 with transducer EX06 to the section of pipe between the actuator and the solenoid valve. In the instrument ambient, select the intake pressure measurement pressure gauge. Start the engine and let it idle, then wait until the pressure level stabilizes. The reading must not exceed 450 - 550 mmHg. The graphic acquisition of the pressure can be made by selecting the scale 2000 or 4000 mmHg.

The test should be carried out at an ambient temperature of between 18° C and 30° C. Close all the doors and windows. Position the gear lever in neutral. Start up the engine and keep it running at 1250 - 1300 rpm. Open the centre vents and place a temperature sensor inside. Switch on the air conditioning (A/C button pressed and LED on). Switch on the recirculation (button pressed and LED on). Place the fan speed selector in position "2". Place the temperature selector in the maximum cold position. Place the distributor selector in the "frontal" position. Check that within 2 - 4 minutes the temperature reading is 8 - 12° ?.

The test should be carried out at ambient temperatures of between 18 ° C and 30 ° C. Close all the doors and windows. Position the gear lever in neutral. Start up the engine and let it reach 1250 - 1300 rpm. Connect the vehicle system to the special recharging equipment (see Op. ), so that the low pressure values (1a) (pressure gauge A) and the high pressure values (1b) (pressure gauge B) can be read. 5040A10 Air conditioning refrigerant CIRCUIT - Draining and Refilling Make sure that the air conditioning is switched off (A/C button released and LED off). Switch on the recirculation (button pressed). Place the fan speed selector in position "2". Place the temperature selector in the maximum cold position. Place the distribution selector in the "frontal" position. Check on the recharging equipment high and low pressure gauges that the pressure is 5 - 6 bar. Switch on the air conditioning (A/C button pressed and LED on). Check, within a minute, that the reading on the low pressure gauge is 2.5 - 3.0 bar and that on the high pressure gauge is 15 - 16 bar. Wait for the engine cooling fan to switch on and check, on the low pressure gauge, that the pressure is 1.5 - 1.8 bar and, on the high pressure gauge, that the pressure is 10 - 12 bar.

Apply a solution of soapy water to the entire perimeter of the window exterior. From inside the passenger compartment, blow through with an air jet along the entire perimeter. If necessary, move the covers sideways and upwards. Visually inspect for the formation of air bubbles on the outside surface: this makes it possible to identify any points where the sealant is insufficient or damaged. If there is insufficient sealant on the vertical pillars, the pillar cover can be moved and a rubber type sealant injected inside. If there is insufficient sealant on the top section, then the roof lining can be moved and rubber type sealant injected from the inside. If there is insufficient sealant on the botton section, then the windscreen base cover (for the front windscreen) and the rear parcel shelf (for the rearscreen) can be moved aside and rubber type sealant injected from the inside. If there is insufficient sealant in a generalized more widespread area, then the seal of the window is not guaranteed and the glass must be removed and new sealant completely reapplied (see Op. Wait a few minutes (5 minutes) after the engine is turned off. 1. Remove the engine oil dipstick, clean and then fully reinsert. Remove and check the level is between the MIN and MAX limits. The gap between the MIN and MAX limits corresponds to about one litre of oil. Work carefully inside the engine bay when the engine is warm to avoid the danger of burns. Remember that the fan may start moving when the engine is very hot: risk of injury. 2. If the oil level is close to or even below the MIN level, add the recommended oil through the oil filler opening up to the MAX mark. When the engine oil level is over the MAX level following a normal check, adjust the level. After topping up the engine oil, allow the engine to run for a few seconds, then turn off and leave for a few minutes before checking the level again. Finish filling until the MAX level on the engine coolant reservoir is reached. Start the engine and run it at idle speed for 2 or 3 minutes. CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Before any operation on the electrical equipment components, including the battery, make sure that the ignition is in the OFF position. In order to release parts which are sticking, tap lightly using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated bolts and all components which have deteriorated. Protect adequately with adhesive tape or clean rags those parts of the engine which, remaining uncovered following dismantling, offer entry passages to dust or foreign bodies. The replacement of removed assemblies or components should be carried out using genuine spare parts only: this is the only way that the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components can be guaranteed. Before any interventions on components of the fuel system, discharge the pressure in the system using tool N. 1.870.684.000 connected to the specific valve located on the fuel distribution manifold. Starting from engine number 02030116, main journal half-bearings have been fitted on crankshafts which have been selected so that the matching clearance is optimum. The crankshaft is supplied, by the Parts Dept., without the appropriate half-bearings for 'normal' dimension main journals and crank pins; it is therefore necessary to select the main journal half-bearings to be fitted identifying the grade for each main journal and crank pin for the new crankshaft. The following is needed for selecting the main journal half-bearings: the code number stamped on the flywheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals. Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades. 1. Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines; for 5 cylinder engines the numerical code for the 5th crank pin is found in place of the 'N'. 2. Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines; for 5 cylinder engines the numerical code for the 6th main journal is found in place of the 'N'. 3. Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first bearing on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the main journal grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 2. In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red colour) as described below. A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 in the figure (if present). In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimension 52.994 for the first bearing on the timing side which identifies Grade A (red colour); the same method can be used for all the other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94). Grade A bearing - Normal, diameter 52.994 - 53.000 mm, RED paint mark, code number 1 (94 00)° Grade B bearing - Normal, diameter 52.988 - 52.994 mm, BLUE paint mark, code number 2 (88 94)° Grade C bearing - Normal, diameter 52.982 - 52.988 mm, YELLOW paint mark, code number 3 (82 88)° Grade D bearing - Undersize, diameter 52.867- 52.873 (*) mm, BROWN paint mark, code number 6 (67 73)° Grade E bearing - Undersize, diameter 52.861 - 52.867 (*) mm, GREEN paint mark, code 7 (61 67)° Grade F bearing - Undersize, diameter 52.855 - 52.861 (*) mm, BLACK paint mark, code number 8 (55 61)° (*) 0.127 mm undersize (°) Last two numbers (thousandth part) of the dimensions of the main journals If a crankshaft is being used where the maximum bearing undersize through regrinding is 0.127 mm, then the grade should be selected by measuring the dimensions of the diameter of the bearing with reference to the above. Having defined the grade and colour for each new or reground crankshaft bearing, it is necessary to select the pair and the size for the bearings which should be the same colour as the corresponding bearing; at the Parts Dept. it is possible to go back to the part no. of the pair of half-bearings required. The above is designed to ensure the optimum operating clearance for all bearings. Starting from engine number 02030116, main journal half-bearings have been fitted on crankshafts which have been selected so that the matching clearance is optimum. The crankshaft is supplied, by the Parts Dept., without the appropriate half-bearings for 'normal' dimension main journals and crank pins; it is therefore necessary to select the main journal half-bearings to be fitted identifying the grade for each main journal and crank pin for the new crankshaft. The following is needed for selecting the main journal half-bearings: the code number stamped on the flywheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals. Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades. 1. Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines; for 5 cylinder engines the numerical code for the 5th crank pin is found in place of the 'N'. 2. Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines; for 5 cylinder engines the numerical code for the 6th main journal is found in place of the 'N'. 3. Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first bearing on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the main journal grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 2. In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red colour) as described below. A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 in the figure (if present). In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimension 52.994 for the first bearing on the timing side which identifies Grade A (red colour); the same method can be used for all the other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94). Grade A bearing - Normal, diameter 52.994 - 53.000 mm, RED paint mark, code number 1 (94 00)° Grade B bearing - Normal, diameter 52.988 - 52.994 mm, BLUE paint mark, code number 2 (88 94)° Grade C bearing - Normal, diameter 52.982 - 52.988 mm, YELLOW paint mark, code number 3 (82 88)° Grade D bearing - Undersize, diameter 52.867- 52.873 (*) mm, BROWN paint mark, code number 6 (67 73)° Grade E bearing - Undersize, diameter 52.861 - 52.867 (*) mm, GREEN paint mark, code 7 (61 67)° Grade F bearing - Undersize, diameter 52.855 - 52.861 (*) mm, BLACK paint mark, code number 8 (55 61)° (*) 0.127 mm undersize (°) Last two numbers (thousandth part) of the dimensions of the main journals If a crankshaft is being used where the maximum bearing undersize through regrinding is 0.127 mm, then the grade should be selected by measuring the dimensions of the diameter of the bearing with reference to the above. Having defined the grade and colour for each new or reground crankshaft bearing, it is necessary to select the pair and the size for the bearings which should be the same colour as the corresponding bearing; at the Parts Dept. it is possible to go back to the part no. of the pair of half-bearings required. The above is designed to ensure the optimum operating clearance for all bearings. Starting from engine number 02030116, main journal half-bearings have been fitted on crankshafts which have been selected so that the matching clearance is optimum. The crankshaft is supplied,bythe Parts Dept.,without the appropriate half-bearingsfor 'normal' dimension main journals and crank pins; it is therefore necessary to select the main journal half-bearings to be fitted identifying the grade for each main journal and crank pin for the new crankshaft. The following is needed for selecting the main journal half-bearings: the code number stamped on the flywheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals. Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades. 1. Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines; for 5 cylinder engines the numerical code for the 5th crank pin is found in place of the 'N'. 2. Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines; for 5 cylinder engines the numerical code for the 6th main journal is found in place of the 'N'. 3. Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first bearing on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the main journal grade, reer to the numerical code for reference 2. In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red colour) as described below. A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 in the figure (if present). In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimension 59.994 for the first bearing on the timing side which identifies Grade A (red colour); the same method can be used for all the other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94). Having defined the grade and colour for each new or reground crankshaft bearing, it is necessary to select the pair and the size for the bearings which should be the same colour as the corresponding bearing; at the Parts Dept. it is possible to go back to the part no. of the pair of half-bearings required. The above is designed to ensure the optimum operating clearance for all bearings. The following is needed for selecting the main journal half-bearings: the code number stamped on the flywheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals. Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades. 1. Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; For 4 cylinder engines, an 'N' is used instead of the last number relating to the 5th crankpin. 2. Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; For 4 cylinder engines, an 'N' is used instead of the last number relating to the 6th crankpin. 3. Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first bearing on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the main journal grade, reer to the numerical code for reference 2. In the case of the example, the numbers 111111 indicate that all six bearings are Grade A (red colour) as described below. A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 in the figure (if present). In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimension 59.994 for the first bearing on the timing side which identifies Grade A (red colour); the same method can be used for all the other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94 - 95). Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades. 1 - Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines. 2 - Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines. 3 - Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first bearing on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the main journal grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 2 in the key. In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red colour) as described below. A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 in the figure (if present). The following is needed for selecting the main journal half-bearings: the code number stamped on the flywheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals. Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades. 1 - Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines. 2 - Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines. 3 - Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first bearing on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the main journal grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 2 in the key. In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red colour) as described below. A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 in the figure (if present). In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimension 52.994 for the first bearing on the timing side which identifies Grade A (red colour); the same method can be used for all the other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94). Dismantling Reassembling Remove the ring gear from the engine flywheel using a hydraulic press. Reassembling Dismantling Thoroughly clean and degrease the contact surfaces of the new ring gear and the flywheel. Heat up the new ring gear evenly in an oven at a temperature of 80° C. The crankshaft is supplied, by the Parts Dept., without the appropriate half-bearings for 'standard' dimension main journals and crank pins; it is therefore necessary to select the half-bearings to be fitted by identifying the grade for each main journal and crank pin for the new crankshaft. The following is needed for selecting the main journal half-bearings the code number stamped on the phonic wheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the crankpins. Below is an example of the identification of crankpin grades. 1 - Crank pin identification number: the number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines. 2 - Main journal identification code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing side bearing; the final 'N' is a code that does not matter for 4 cylinder engines. 3 - Set of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the crankpins: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first pin on the timing side. Only use the codes in the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used. For the identification of the crankpin grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 1 in the key. If a crankshaft is being used where the maximum bearing undersize through regrinding is 0.127 mm, then the grade should be selected by measuring the dimensions of the diameter of the bearing with reference to the above. During this procedure, from the moment when the instrument panel is supplied with power until the end of learning, do not press the accelerator, brake or clutch pedals. Make sure that the ignition is off (STOP position). Connect the tool to the diagnostic socket and place the knob in position 3. Name Country - MPX 97 switch 1.806.365.000 Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Turn the ignition to the ON position). Wait 60 seconds, the time required for the control unit to check the throttle body's internal spring and the butterfly's maximum/minimum angles. Turn the ignition off (STOP position). Wait 15 seconds, the time required for the control unit to save the learnt values in EPROM. Using the Examiner, check that the self-learning of idle speed has finished correctly (LEARNING RESULT - Correct; SELF-LEARNING MEMORIZATION - Completed). If the self-learning procedure is not correct, turn the ignition off (STOP position) and repeat the above procecure. If the incorrectness continues, check that the diagnostic cable connection is secure and that the instrument is working. Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position. Check that: the air conditioning is switched off, the accelerator pedal is never pressed and the accelerator cable is correctly positioned (refer to op. ). 1068A30 accelerator control cable - r + r Connect the tool to the diagnostic socket and place the knob in position 3. Name Country - MPX 97 switch 1.806.365.000 Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Using the Examiner, enter the "Control Unit Test" ambient. Place the ignition key in the ON position. Using the Examiner, enter the "Active Diagnosis" ambient, then select "Reset self-adjustment parameters" and "Idle actuator". Using the Examiner, press "Carry out active diagnosis". Place the ignition key in the OFF position and wait for 30 seconds. Place the ignition key in the ON position and wait for 30 seconds. Using the Examiner, re-establish the dialogue with the engine control system. Using the Examiner, enter the "Parameters" ambient and select the following tests from the menu - "Idle recognition test - carried out" and "Idle recognition signals - synchronized". If at least one of the parameters does not conform, place the ignition key in the OFF position and repeat the procedure. If this non conformity persists, check that the diagnostic cable is correctly connected and check the operation of the instrument. Place the ignition key in the OFF position and wait for 30 seconds. Start up the engine without acting on the accelerator pedal. Disconnect the diagnostic equipment. Test the vehicle by driving for several kilometres then, with the engine warmed up, check that it is idling correctly.

Start the engine and warm up until the radiator cooling fan comes on for the second time. Leave as little time as possible between the engine preheating stage and the moment the test begins and avoid a prolonged idling period. Check that sensor diameter is at least 0.22 times exhaust pipe diameter. Ensure that the exhaust gas uptake fitting joints are effective enough to prevent leaks. Position the fume measurement device sensor in the exhaust tail-pipe. Take care that the end is placed in a pipe section where the gas flow is uniformly distributed. If necessary, to meet the above requirements, fit an exhaust pipe extension so that the exhaust pipe coupling is sealed and the sensor end is located in a straight section at least six times as long as the exhaust tail-pipe diameter toward the engine and at least three times the tail-pipe diameter downstream. Check that the sensor uptake pipe from the exhaust tail-pipe to the fume measurement device is on an upward slope and does not include acute angled kinks. Ensure that the counter-pressure to the sensor is as specified and does not exceed 7.5 mbars during the test. With the engine on and idling, place the gearbox in neutral and release the clutch pedal. Position the fume measurement meter to allow the uptake of exhaust gas. Record the reading shown on the fume meter gauge. As the engine is idling, rapidly and gently pump the accelerator pedal until the engine is turning at maximum speed and the governor cuts in. Record and note the maximum fume value marked on the fume meter during the acceleration without considering values during the release stage. As soon as the maximum rotation speed is reached, release the accelerator pedal until the engine is idling again. Check that the fume meter point returns to the position corresponding to the idling reading. Repeat the above operations at least six times until the fume readings entered have stabilised. The readings are considered to have stabilised when four consecutive readings are within a 0.25 m -1 range and are not in decreasing order. The fume values to be considered are the arithmetic mean of the four stabilised values. Ensure that the counter-pressure to the sensor is as specified and does not exceed 7.5 mbar during the test. With the engine on and idling, place the gearbox in neutral and release the clutch pedal. Position the fume measurement meter to allow the sampling of exhaust gases. Record the reading shown on the fume meter gauge. As the engine is idling, rapidly and gently pump the accelerator pedal until the engine is turning at maximum speed and the governor cuts in. Record and note the maximum fume value marked on the fume meter during the acceleration without considering values during the overrunning stage. As soon as the maximum rotation speed is reached, release the accelerator pedal until the engine is idling again. Check that the fume meter point returns to the position corresponding to the idling reading. Repeat the above operations at least six times until the fume readings entered have stabilised. The readings are considered to have stabilised when four consecutive readings are within a 0.25 m -1 range and are not in decreasing order. The fume values to be considered are the arithmetic mean of the four stabilised values. CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. WARNINGS All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damage to the vehicle. prevent brake-clutch fluid coming into contact with painted parts; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Do not reuse brake-clutch fluid drained during bleeding. Before any interventions on electrical components, including battery disconnection, make sure that the ignition is off ("STOP" position). In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. Protect adequately with adhesive tape or clean rags those parts of the engine which, remaining uncovered following dismantling, offer entry passages to dust or foreign bodies. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated bolts and all components which have deteriorated. The replacement of removed assemblies or components should be carried out using genuine spare parts only: this is the only way that the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components can be guaranteed.

CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperature and live electrical cables. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. If necessary, the Manual indicates cases where special attention is required to avoid dangerous situations occurring. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). WARNINGS All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. Prevent brake-clutch fluid coming into contact with painted parts; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Do not reuse brake-clutch fluid drained during bleeding. Before any interventions on electrical components, including battery disconnection, make sure that the ignition is off ('STOP' position). In order to release parts which are sticking, tap lightly using an aluminium or lead hammer for ferrous materials, and a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nut and all components which have deteriorated. To avoid possible damage to the gearbox casing whilst tightening the oil drainage and/or filler plug(s), it should be pointed out that the torque figures given in the Service Manuals refer to 'dry' threads (without a trace of oil or other lubricants). In effect, lubricating the thread reduces friction and assists the tightening of the components concerned; therefore when the tightening is completed, the effect of the torque applied will be greater than recommended figure. The above requires the thread to be thoroughly cleaned, before each tightening, of any traces of lubricant (both on the plug(s) and the gearbox casing).

Carry out a preliminary check of the automatic transmission fluid level when cold as follows. Park the car on level ground and engage the hand brake. With the engine idling, starting from the P position select all the other gears 2 or 3 times then return to the P position. Withdraw the oil level dipstick, clean it, then insert it fully into its housing. Withdraw the dipstick again and check that the oil level is between the MIN and MAX references on the side of the stick marked "COLD". If the oil level is low, top up with the specified oil. Type Component Name Qty. - Oil AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT TUTELA GI/2 - The final gearbox oil level check must be carried out with the engine and gearbox at normal operating temperature (gearbox oil temperature 70° - 80° C), so the car should be driven for an appropriate time before the check. Carry out the final check of the automatic transmission fluid level when warm as follows. Park the car on level ground and engage the hand brake. With the engine idling, starting from the P position select all the other gears 2 or 3 times then return to the P position. Withdraw the oil level dipstick, clean it, then insert it fully into its housing. Withdraw the dipstick again and check that the oil level is between the MIN and MAX references on the side of the stick marked "HOT". If the oil level is low, top up with the specified oil. The quantity of oil need for filling if necessary is as follows: Type Component Name Qty. - Oil AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT TUTELA GI/2 3.8

CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Great care should be taken when working on this system or near its components. WARNINGS CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Great care should be taken when working on this system or near its components. WARNINGS All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. Prevent brake-clutch fluid from coming into contact with painted parts; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Before any interventions on electrical components, including battery disconnection, make sure that the ignition is off ("STOP" position). In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. Protect adequately with adhesive tape or clean rags those parts of the engine which, remaining uncovered following dismantling, offer entry passages to dust or foreign bodies. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated bolts and all components which have deteriorated. The replacement of removed assemblies or components should be carried out using genuine spare parts only: this is the only way that the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components can be guaranteed.

CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Prevent brake-clutch fluid from coming into contact with painted parts; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Do not reuse brake-clutch fluid drained during bleeding. Before any interventions on electrical components, including battery disconnection, make sure that the ignition is off ("STOP" position). In order to release parts which are sticking, tap lightly using an aluminium or lead hammer for ferrous materials, and a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. Before working on the system, follow the safety instructions for the Air Bag system (see ). See assembly 5580C air bag system The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Great care should be taken when working on this system or near its components. WARNINGS CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Great care should be taken when working on this system or near its components. WARNINGS All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. Prevent brake-clutch fluid coming into contact with painted parts; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Before any interventions on electrical components, including battery disconnection, make sure that the ignition is off ('STOP' position). In order to release parts which are sticking, tap lightly using an aluminium or lead hammer for ferrous materials, and a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting, it is vital to follow the recommended tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated bolts and all components which have deteriorated. The replacement of removed assemblies or components should be carried out using genuine spare parts only: this is the only way that the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components can be guaranteed. To avoid possible damage to the rack and pinion steering box duringservicing operations carried out on vehicles with the wheels raised off the ground (for example on a lift) do not steer using the wheel. These incorrect manouevres, with the force amplified by the linkage, plus the inertia force of the steering column and the steering wheel rotating freely, on reaching the end of travel position sharply at excessive speed, can cause damage to the rack teeth and, in extreme cases, they may even break.

CAUTION CAUTION All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For certain procedures, the use of Alfa Romeo special tools is recommended. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. For the use of chemical products, stick to the warnings on the safety card which the supplier must give the consumer (in Italy in accordance with D.M. No. 47/1992). The electronic ignition system generates voltages of 20,000 V and higher which could be very dangerous to people, especially if they suffer from a heart condition. Great care should be taken when working on this system or near its components. WARNINGS All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. Prevent brake-clutch fluid coming into contact with painted parts; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Before any interventions on electrical components, including battery disconnection, make sure that the ignition is off ('STOP' position). In order to release parts which are sticking, tap lightly using an aluminium or lead hammer for ferrous materials, and a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated bolts and all components which have deteriorated. The replacement of removed assemblies or components should be carried out using genuine spare parts only: this is the only way that the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components can be guaranteed. In the case of a servicing operation which involves removing and refitting mechanical components which have the function of defining the position of the wheels in relation to the bodyshell (e.g.: track control arms, steering knuckles, stub axles, Mc Pherson shock absorbers, suspension frame/crossmember, etc.) the wheel geometry has to be checked and, if necessary, adjusted.

Follow the preliminary instructions below. The efficiency of BOGE NIVOMAT self-levelling units is checked by measuring the height of the vehicle when empty and fully laden, under static conditions and after a journey to allow bedding. The fuel tank should be half full. Check that the tyre pressures are correct. Inspect the underbody and remove any dirt, dust, mud or sand. Remove everything from the luggage compartment which is not part of the vehicle's original equipment. TEST WITH CAR UNLADEN AND LEVELLED Place the vehicle on a horizontal plane; do not use the brakes to stop the vehicle, but let it come to a halt by itself, then place the gear lever in first (manual gearbox) or in P (automatic transmission). Measure levelled distance H with the vehicle unladen without a driver and check that it is within the following limits. The maximum permissible difference between the left and right sides is 6-8 mm. Values for distance H for petrol versions. Measurement Value - H (mm) 362 ± 8 With unladen vehicle levelled (-) - Values for distance H for diesel versions. Measurement Value - H (mm) 367 ± 8 With unladen vehicle levelled (-) - TEST WITH CAR FULLY LADEN ON LEVEL Place a load of 50 kg in the luggage compartment. Seat three people on the rear seat (or a weight equivalent to 70 kg per person) and two people in the front seats. In these load conditions, drive the vehicle for 2000 m on a road with an uneven surface. Place the vehicle on a horizontal plane; do not use the brakes to stop the vehicle, but let it come to a halt by itself, then place the gear lever in first (manual gearbox) or in P (automatic transmission). Measure levelled distance H without removing the load or the passengers and check that it is within the recommended limits: The maximum permissible difference between the left and right sides is 6-8 mm. Measurement Value - H (mm) 354 ± 8 With vehicle fully laden levelled (-) - TEST WITH CAR UNLADEN AND LEVELLED Let the people come out of the vehicle or remove the corresponding weights and remove the load from the luggage compartment. Drive the vehicle for 2000 m. Measure levelled distance H with the vehicle unladen without a driver and check that it is within the following limits. The maximum permissible difference between the left and right sides is 6-8 mm. Values for distance H for petrol versions. Measurement Value - H (mm) 362 ± 8 With unladen vehicle levelled (-) - Values for distance H for diesel versions. Measurement Value - H (mm) 367 ± 8 With unladen vehicle levelled (-) - If the height measurements do not correspond with the recommended values, replace the self-levelling unit.

Do not on any account carry out fast recharging. To recharge the battery correctly, use a battery charger recommended by the Service Outlets (e.g. ISEAT CB1): this is a 'constant voltage' battery charger with microprocessor, which recognizes the battery conditions and automatically determines the best recharging cycle; in this way a battery charge of close to 100% can be achieved. Always disconnect the battery negative terminal before recharging; while recharging, do not touch the battery terminals using your hands and do not bring naked flames close to the battery; operate the battery charger only after connecting the leads to the battery. If the measurement of the battery voltage without load is less than 12.10 V, recharging is not recommended and the battery should be replaced ( ). 5530B10 battery - r+r

Follow these precautions. A low electrolyte level often indicates an operating fault in the alternator, and in particular the electronic voltage regulator. On batteries with an opticam hydrometer, electrolyte level and battery charge status can be monitored qualitatively by examining the indicator colour: a light, bright colour indicates low electrolyte level: top up with distilled water; a dark colour without a green area in the centre indicates that the electrolyte level is correct but charge is low: recharge the battery; a dark colour with a green area in the middle indicates that both electrolyte level and charge status are correct: no action is necessary. For more details . See subassembly 5530 CURRENT GENERATOR However, this device does not give absolute guarantees concerning the correct measurement of the state of charge; a more accurate check on the battery charge should be carried out during servicing. Proceed as follows. Check the battery voltage without load using the test device recommended by the Service outlets (e.g. 'MICRO 360'). Depending on the voltage values measured, which define the state of charge of the battery, proceed as follows: If the voltage without load is less than 12.10 V, replace the battery ( ). 5530B10 battery - r+r If the voltage without load is over 12.10 V but less than 12.50 V, recharge the battery ( ). 5530B14 battery - recharge If the voltage without load is over 12.50 V, the battery is efficient. If necessary, top up the electrolyte as follows. Carefully remove the cap strip. Top up with distilled and deionized water, taking care not to allow electrolyte to splash out. The electrolyte is acid and can cauase damage to eyes, hands and clothing.

Removing Refitting Position the vehicle on a four column type lift. Raise the vehicle. 1. Undo the lower bolts fixing the trim. 1. Undo the lower bolt fixing the additional front wheel arch liner. 2.
