Remove the trim, releasing the adhesive tape (1a), the bolt (1b), the centering pin (1c) and the retainers (1d). Refitting Removing Check that the moulding is undamaged. 1. Degrease the area of the bodywork where the adhesive tape is stuck using heptane. 2. Place the head of the bolt in position. 3. Detach a section of protective film at the two ends of the adhesive tape. 4. Position the trim and fit the bolt (2) and the centering pin (4a) in the bodyshell. 5. Centre the trim with the bodywork profile. 6. Remove the protective film from the adhesive tape by pulling the two ends (3). 7. Engage the retainers. 8. Tighten the nut. 9. Place the additional wheel arch liner back in position. 10. Tighten the bolt. 1. Tighten the lower bolts fixing the trim. Lower the vehicle and remove it from the lift. Removing Refitting Position the vehicle on a four column type lift. Raise the vehicle. 1. Undo the lower bolts (1a) fixing the front trim (1b) and the rear trim (1c). Lower the vehicle. 1. Using cutters, cut the bead of sealant (1a) along the upper perimeter of the front trim (1b) and the rear trim (1c), taking care not to nick the vehicle paintwork. 2. Keep the trims (1b) and (1c). Refitting Removing Check that the two parts of the trim are not damaged. 1. Clean the surface of the vehicle where the trims are attached using adhesive, removing any residues of adhesive; then degrease the surface using heptane. 2. Test fit the trims. 3. Have suitable equipment ready to keep the trims pressed against the vehicle after the sticking process described below. 4. Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults "at source"; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first category involves careful design of wiring with thorough positioning and anchorage. Wiring is shielded and protected and the routes are carefully determined. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps, etc. Passive protection includes all interventions (normally carried out in any case) to reduce high failure currents (overload and short-circuit). All fuses included in the system are rated on the basis of nominal absorption of loads which cannot be served simultaneously, to ensure cut-in in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is in turn recharged by the alternator ( ) during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, contained in two fuse boxes located near the battery and supplied directly from the latter. The power supplies for all the services and systems are protected by specific fuses, contained in the junction unit, or shunt fuses. The shunt fuses are located under the dashboard either just above the junction unit, or on the right above the glove compartment. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to different positions: when the key is inserted and turned to the first click, the ignition is turned on (ON position) and several circuits are supplied, which are thus called "ignition-operated" (lines "INT" and "15/54"); the second click - start up position - supplies the starter motor (line "50"), (line "50")., while also disconnecting certain circuits (i.e. those that take up most power) to ensure maximum current flow to the motor; (INT/A line) by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction (and pressing the special button) the PARK position is engaged which supplies the side lights even with the key switched off ("STAZ" and "POS" lines); ( ). See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first category involves careful design of wiring with thorough positioning and anchorage. Wiring is shielded and protected and the routes are carefully determined. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps, etc. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is, in turn, recharged by the alternator during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, grouped together in a box directly on the positive battery terminal and connected directly to it. The box contains up to eight maxifuses. The power supplies to all services and systems are protected by fuses grouped in the junction unit or in two special multiple connectors, one for the front wiring and other other for the facia wiring in accordance with a pre-established order. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various different positions: when the key is inserted and turned to the first click, the ignition is turned on (ON position) and several circuits are supplied, which are thus called 'ignition-operated' (lines 'INT' and '15/54'); the second click - AVV position - instead supplies the starter motor (line '50')., disconnecting some circuits (those which absorb most power), thus ensuring the maximum flow of current to the starter motor; ('INT/A' line). on the other hand, by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction (and pressing the special button) the PARK position is engaged which supplies the side lights even with the key switched off ('STAZ' and 'POS' lines); See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. This general diagram shows all the lines which depart from the battery and the MAXIFUSE boxes; reference should be made to the specific diagrams for greater detail.

Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first kind involves the thoughtful design of wiring, attentive to location and anchorage, and the careful planning of properly protected cable routes. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps, etc. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is, in turn, recharged by the alternator during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, grouped together in a box directly on the positive battery terminal and connected directly to it. The box contains up to eight maxifuses. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Description The car is equipped with two dipped beam headlamps. The dipped beam headlamps are switched on through the steering column switch unit by turning the special ring nut in the position after the side lights. A special relay - on the right hand side, under the dashboard - keeps the dipped headlamps on with the main beam headlamps on. The circuit is protected by two fuses, one for the right hand headlamp, one for the left hand headlamp. The dipped beam circuit also enables the headlamp alignment device and rear fog lamps for operation.

Functional description The circuit for the dipped beam headlamps is operated by the steering column switch unit H5 . By placing the switch in the dipped beam position, the line which supplies the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) is supplied controlled by the ignition. Each circuit is protected by a fuse for the junction unit B1 : F5 for the left headlamp and F4 for the right one. With the dipped beam headlamps on, this supply passes through the dipped beam headlamps maintenance relay/remote control switch J45 . If the lights are switched from dipped to main beam, the suply is interrupted, but it is replaced by the one from pin 87 of switch J45 : the signal for switching on the main beam headlamps, in effect, energizes the relay (pin 86) which switches the supply to the direct line (maxifuse J/B2 of B5 to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99) which thereby also keeps the circuit for the dipped headlamps and the main beam headlamps on. The supply line for the left lamp also acts as a go ahead signal for the headlamp alignment ( ) and the rear fog lamps (check device inside the rev counter module See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR E15) ( ). See E2031 REAR FOG LAMPS

Description The vehicle is equipped with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps. The electronic circuitry in each of the two headlamps switches the software on and off at the appropriate times and, in accordance with international regulations, the gas discharge headlamps. The system consists of an ignition system and ballast for each lamp which are activated when the dipped headlamps function is requested. The left headlamp is the Master control unit while the right acts as a Slave unit. The master receives the command for the dipped headlamps and the vehicle speed from the potentiometers on the wheel axles. According to the input, the switching on of the left front headlamp (dipped headlamps) is controlled and likewise that of the right headlamp via the serial line. The dipped beam headlamps are switched on through the steering column switch by turning the specific ring to the position after the side lights. The 'Follow me home' function is designed to keep the dipped headlamps and the side lights on after the engine has been switched off (key in OFF and/or PARK) for a time of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The funciton is switched on by operating the flasher lever within 2 minutes: each time the lever is operated the time the lights remain on increases by 30 seconds up to a maximum of 210 secs. Operating the flasher lever for longer than 2 seconds switches the function off; the function is also switched off if the ignition key is turned to the ON position. A special relay - on the left hand side, under the dashboard - keeps the dipped headlamps on with the main beam headlamps on. The circuit is protected by two fuses, one for the right hand headlamp, one for the left hand headlamp. The dipped beam circuit also enables the rear fog lamps for operation.

Functional description The circuit for the dipped beam headlamps is operated by the steering column switch unit H5 . By placing the switch in the dipped beam position, the line which supplies the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) is supplied controlled by the ignition. The signal is sent to the headlamp internal electronic circuit,w hich manages activation of the bulb. Each circuit is protected by a fuse for the junction unit B1 : F5 for the left headlamp and F4 for the right one. The supply passes throught the headlamps maintenance relay/remote control switch J45 which only interrupts this supply during starting (AVV signal from the starter motor). The supply line for the left lamp also acts as an enablement signal for the rear fog lamps (check device inside the rev counter module E15 ) See E2031 REAR FOG LAMPS

Functional description The main beam headlamps circuit is operated by the steering column switch unit H5 . When the switch is turned to the main beam position, or when the 'flashing' contact is closed, the line which supplies the (left) F10 and (right) F11 headlamps receives a supply controlled by the ignition. - - Each circuit is protected by a fuse for the junction unit B1 : F7 for the left lamp and F6 for the right one. The suppy line for the left headlamp also sends a signal to the rev counter module E15 (pin 4 of connector B) to light up the 'main beam headlamps on' warning light.

Description The brake lights are located at the rear in the side lights and in the central third brake light and consist of 10 separate bulbs. These are operated whenever the brake pedal is pressed, by means of a switch on the pedal itself. The correct operation of the side brake lights is controlled by the check device for the exterior lights, located inside the rev counter module. The following faults may occur: blown bulb bulb s.c. to earth or positive incorrect bulb (5W bulb instead of 21W) A special failure warning light, also in the rev counter module, comes on for all other faults in the various circuits. This warning light comes on for about 4 seconds when the ignition key is turned to MAR, to indicate it is working properly, then it goes off. The third centre brake light is not controlled by the check panel. The circuit is protected by the two fuses for the lights controlled by the check panel, one for the lights on the right hand side, the other for those on the left hand side and by a fuse on the supply line for all three brake lights. A braking signal is also sent from the switch to the ABS, which detects braking status and therefore introduces braking control. The same signal is also sent to some engine management systems, which take the braking condition into account when determining the engine control mode. On versions equipped with radios, a switch is fitted on the brake pedal with a special filter to prevent interference when the pedal is pressed.

Functional description The switch I30 is controlled by the ignition (INT)from the line for fuse F1 for the control unit B1 : when the brake pedal is pressed, the switch closes and sends the operating signal to the check device inside the rev counter E15 (pin 5 of connector A). The supply for the check device inside E15 arrives directly from the battery (maxifuse J/B2 of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99) to pins 10 and 16 of connector A, through fuses F2 and F3 of the junction unit B1 ; the former protects the circuits for the lights on the left-hand side, the latter those on the right. The check device thereby controls the supply (pin 18 and pin 13 of connector A) for the side brake lights in the rear light clusters F30 and F31 . In the case of failures in the circuit, the "lights failure" warning light - inside E15 - comes on, with the supply controlled by the ignition (IINT), pin 15 of connector A, of the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. The switch I30 sends the signal for operating the centre rear light cluster F40 via the junction unit B1 (pin 18, connector D and pin 14 of connector E). Description The car is equipped with two reversing lights situated iin the centre of the tail-light unit (on the boot). These are operated whenever reverse is engaged via a switch on the outside of the gear housing. The reversing light circuit is supplied with the ignition key turned to MAR - fully independently of the other lights - by a line protected by a fuse in the junction unit.

Functional description The switch for the reversing lights I20 is supplied when the ignition is switched on (INT) by the line for fuse F1 for the junction unit B1 . When reverse gear is engaged, the switch closes and sends the supply to the reversing lights in the centre rear light cluster on the left F35 and on the right F36 , via the junction unit B1 (pin 9 connector D and pins 6 and 7 of connector G). Functional description Reversing light switch I20 is not present. Pins 8 and 9 of the automatic transmission solenoids unit L50 , connector A, are connected to the reverse gear sensor and send the signals for switching on the reversing light in the same way as for other versions.

Description The vehicle has two additional fog lamps for use in poor visibility conditions. The rear foglamps are activated by a button on the central console between the seats. A special symbol is lit up when the side lights are on. The circuit for the fog lights is protected by a special fuse and operated by a special relay, on the right hand side, under the dashboard. A warning light in the panel (rev counter module) signals that the lamps have been switched on. The foglamps are enabled under the following conditions: the ignition in the ON position side lights on. In addition, if the side lights are switched off, the fog lights are also switched off even if the button is pressed. When the side lights are turned on again, the fog lamps come back on. If the ignition key is switched OFF and then turned back to the ON position, the operating button must be pressed once again in order to turn the fog lights back on. This control logic is managed by the integrated services control unit, also on the right hand side, under the dashboard.

Functional description The two front fog lights F15 (left) and F16 (right) are supplied through the fog lights relay J40 by the direct line from the battery - maxifuse J/B2 of B5 ) up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99. - and through the front fog light fuse B13 up to 2/99 or F1 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. The signal which energizes the coil for the relay J40 arrives from the integrated services control unit M40 (pin 11 of connector C) according to the enablement logic described. The control unit receives the signal that the side lights are on from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 (pin 8 of connector C) and the supply is controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 (pin 7 of connector B). When the engagement signal also arrives from the button H35 (pin 1 of connector B), the control unit M40 sends the command to the front fog lights relay J40 . The supply line for the two fog lights also sends a signal to the rev counter module E15 (pin 14 of connector B) to light up the "front fog lights on" warning light. Description The vehicle has two additional fog lamps for use in poor visibility conditions. The fog lights are activated by the button on the centre console between the seats; the specific symbol is lit up when the lights are on. The circuit for the fog lights is protected by a special fuse and operated by a special relay, on the right hand side, under the dashboard. A warning light on the instrument panel (rev counter module) indicates that the headlamps have come on. The fog lamps are enabled under the following conditions: the ignition in the ON position side lights on. In addition, if the side lights are switched off, the fog lights are also switched off even if the button is pressed. When the side lights are turned on again, the fog lamps come back on. If the ignition key is switched OFF and then turned back to the ON position, the operating button must be pressed once again in order to turn the fog lights back on. This control logic is managed by the integrated services control unit, also on the right-hand side under the dashboard.

Functional description The two front fog lights F15 (left) and F16 (right) are supplied through the fog lights relay J40 by the direct line from the battery - maxifuse J/B2 of B99 )- and through fuse F1 of the additional fuse box B98A . The signal which energizes the coil for the relay J40 arrives from the integrated services control unit M40 (pin 11 of connector C) according to the enablement logic described. The control unit receives the signal that the side lights are on from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 (pin 8 of connector C) and the supply is controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 (pin 7 of connector B). When the engagement signal also arrives from the button in H35 (pin 1 of connector B), the control unit M40 sends the command to the front fog lights relay J40 . This signal also lightsup the LED next to the button in H35 . The supply line for the two fog lights also sends a signal to the rev counter module E15 (pin 14 of connector B) to light up the 'front fog lights on' warning light. The switch H35 is lit up when the side lights are switched on by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 .

Description The front interior light includes two courtesy lights with two control switches. With the left switch (A) it is possible to select the following two operating modes: centre position: both lights come on for a timed period when the doors are opened left-hand position: both lights are off all the time; right-hand position: both lights are on all the time. The right-hand switch turns on only one of the lights: left-hand position: left-hand light always on; right-hand position: right-hand light always on; central position: both lights always off. Both rear interior lights contain a courtesy light that operates in different modes according to the position of the lens, which operates an internal switch. neutral position: light comes on for a timed period when the doors are opened; positioned to one side: light always off; positioned to the other side: lights always on. The courtesy light timing is controlled according to a logic managed by the integrated services control unit, on the right hand side, under the dashboard, which can be summarized as follows. When any of the four doors is opened, all front and rear courtesy lights are operated for a timed period. timed period of 7 seconds when the locks are unlocked using the key or the remote control; timed period of 7 seconds when a previously opened door is reclosed; timing is suspended when the key is turned to MAR (this function allows the driver to enter the car and insert the key in the ignition) timed interval of 3 minutes if one of the doors is left open (this function prevents the battery going flat if the car is left with a door open) When one of the other doors is opened, the current timer count is reset to zero. The courtesy light circuit is protected by a special junction unit fuse. two fuses also protect the integrated services control unit direct and ignition-operated supply lines.

Functional description The supply for the front ( G10 ) and rear ( G25 and G26 )courtesy lights arrives directly from the battery. (maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99 ) through fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 . They are switched on via a direct earth signal (permanently activated) or a signal coming from the integrated services control unit M40 . The supply for the control unit M40 is controlled by the ignition (INT) by the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 (pin 7 of connector B) and directly from the battery. (maxifuse J/B2 of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99) through fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 (pin 8 of connector B). The control unit sends a timed signal according to the door unlocking and door open signals which arrive: at pin 15 of connector C: release from the receiver for the remote control M35 .) Description The lighting of the luggage compartment is timed according to a logic managed by the integrated services control unit, on the right hand side, under the dashboard: When the boot is opened, a light is turned on for a timed interval of 20 minutes (this function ensures that the battery does not go flat if the car is left with the boot open). Timer operation is suspended when the boot is closed. A light inside the glove compartment is turned on - only with the ignition turned to MAR - when the compartment is opened, and goes off when the compartment is closed. A light under the sunblind is turned on - only with the ignition turned to MAR- when a switch on the blind is turned on. The circuit for the boot light and the sun visor light is protected by the same fuse as the courtesy lights, two fuses also protect the direct and ignition-controlled supply lines for the integrated services control unit. The circuit for the glove compartment light is protected by the fuse for the supplies controlled by the ignition, at the side of the junction unit. Numerous other interior instrument and control lights are present. These are turned on when the side lights are turned on. The lines are described and illustrated in the relevant component wiring diagrams.

Description All the instruments (dials and gauges) are lit up with the ignition switched ON. In the "night" position (side lights on), the brightness can be adjusted to three levels by an external button. On the sport version with white dials, these are not illuminated when the ignition is switched on, only when the side lights are switched on. This lighting logic is managed by a speedometer module which controls lighting of the rev counter module and the central instrument. The check control instrument is lit up directly by the electronic device inside. The adjustment button is on the left of the actual instruments, together with the button for zeroing the milometer and the headlamp alignment adjuster. The lighting circuit for all the instruments is protected by a special fuse, located at the side of the junction unit.

Functional description The supply for the speedometer E10 (pin 10 of connector A) is controlled by the ignition (INT) by the line for fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. Similarly, the rev counter E15 (at pin 15 of connector A) and the centre instrument E20 (pin 1.). An earth signal from instrument light dimmer control H10 reaches pin 6 of connector B of E10 . This also receives a side light activated signal, at pin 5 of connector B ( ). See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS According to the logic processed by the internal electronic device, the speedometer E10 sends the lighting signal to the other instruments: to the centre instrument E20 (pin 7) from pin 12 of connector A; and to the rev counter E15 (3 of connector B) from pin 4 of connector B. Switch H10 symbols are lit up when the side lights are switched on through the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 .

Description The car is fitted with a horn system which consists of two horns with different tones: a high tone and a low tone horn. Both horns are activated simultaneously. The horns are operated by pressing the sides of the steering wheel cover (Air Bag). The horn circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a specific relay located in the junction box. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time, even when the key is turned to OFF (or removed).

Functional description The horn system is supplied through the horn relay R2 , located in the junction unit B1 from the direct line through the fuse F13 - always for B1 - and the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99. The coil of the relay R2 is energized by an earth signal when one of the steering switches is closed; these switches are connected via the clock spring to the stalk unit H5 . The relay thereby supplies the high tone horn P10 and the low tone horn P11 .

Description The windscreen wash/wipe system is operated by a stalk switch on the right side of the steering wheel. The stalk switch can be set to five positions that correspond to different functions: windscreen wiper off (standstill); intermittent operation; continuous slow operation; continuous medium-fast operation; temporary fast operation (unstable stalk position). When the stalk switch is set to intermittent operation position, four different speeds can be selected by turning the relevant ring: slow intermittent; medium intermittent; medium-fast intermittent; fast intermittent. The windscreen wiper function is operated by pulling the stalk switch slightly toward the steering wheel. This action operates the washer pump. If the stalk switch is held in position, the windscreen wiper also operates (continuous operation). The windscreen wiper carries on working for a few sweeps after the stalk switch is released. The entire system is governed by an electronic device which is responsible for controlling the intermittent function and also the windscreen wiper motor and washer pump. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and is operated by the ignition-operated relay located in the junction unit. The windscreen wiper and washer can be operated with the ignition key turned to ON.

Functional description The windscreen wiper control on the steering column switch unit H5 selects the various operating modes of the windscreen wash/wipe. The stalk unit H5 is supplied at pin 3 of connector D from the ignition-operated line (INT/A) of the relay R1 protected by the fuse F14: both are contained in the junction unit B1 . Depending on the pre-selected function, the stalk unit H5 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the internal electronic device to the windscreen wiper motor N15: from pin 2 for continuous fast operation: the signal reaches the motor directly; from pins 3, 4 for continuous slow and medium-fast oeration: the signal arrives from the intermittent device and is then sent to the motor from pin 5 for intermittent operation: the signal reaches the intermittent device and is then sent to the motor; this signal differs according to adjustment ring position, which adds no resistance, one resistance or two resistances to the line to obain the three different intermittence speeds. The windscreen wiper motor N15 is then connected to earth. It consists of the actual geared motor, the end of travel contacts and the electronic adjustment and control device. When operated, the windscreen washer switch on the steering column switch unit H5 sends two signals from pin 8 and pin 9 of connector A, which reach the pump for operating the windscreen washer N20 directly. Description The windscreen wash/wipe system is operated by a stalk switch on the right side of the steering wheel. The stalk switch can be set to five positions that correspond to different functions: windscreen wiper off (standstill); intermittent operation (or automatic operation if rain sensor fitted); continuous slow operation; continuous medium-fast operation; temporary fast operation (unstable stalk position). When the stalk switch is set to intermittent operation position, four different speeds can be selected by turning the relevant ring: slow intermittent; medium intermittent; medium-fast intermittent; fast intermittent. if the rain sensor is fitted, the selection indicates mechanism intervention sensitivity. The windscreen wiper function is operated by pulling the stalk switch slightly toward the steering wheel. This action operates the washer pump. If the stalk switch is held in position, the windscreen wiper also operates (continuous operation). The windscreen wiper carries on working for a few sweeps after the stalk switch is released. The entire system is governed by an electronic device which is responsible for controlling the intermittent function and also the windscreen wiper motor and washer pump. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and is operated by the ignition-operated relay located in the junction unit. The windscreen wiper and washer can be operated with the ignition key turned to MAR. The system can also activate the windscreen wiper automatically if it rains by means of a special sensor positioned in contact with the windscreen on the rear view mirror.(for greater detail ). Characteristic of working principle 5050 SCREEN WASHERS AND HEADLAMP WASH/WIPE

Functional description The windscreen wiper control on the steering column switch unit H5 selects the various operating modes of the windscreen wash/wipe. The stalk unit H5 is supplied at pin 3 of connector D from the ignition-operated line (INT/A) of the relay R1 protected by the fuse F14 : both are contained in the junction unit B1 . The windscren wiper control unit M79 , pin A1, is also supplied by the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay R1 protected by fuse F14 . Depending on the pre-selected function, the stalk unit H5 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the windscreen wiper motor control unit M79: from pin 2 for continuous fast operation: the signal reaches pin B2 of M79 ; from pins 3, 4 for continuous slow and medium-fast oeration: the signals arrive at pins B3 amd A3 of M79 ; from pin 5 for intermittent or automatic operation: to pin C4 of M79 . Windscreen wiper control unit M79 in turn sends signals to windscreen wiper motor N15 to operate the motor: from pin A8 for high speed, from pin B8 for low speed and from pin C2 for reset control (return to rest position). The windscreen wiper motor N15 is then connected to earth (pin 5). It consists of the actual geared motor, the end of travel contacts and the electronic adjustment and control device. When operated, the windscreen washer switch on the steering column switch unit H5 sends two signals from pin 8 and pin 9 of connector A, the first to windscreen wiper control unit M79 (pin A4) while the second is directly connected to the windscreen washer pump motor N22 . The motor is operated upon a command from windscreen wiper control unit M79 , from pin B4. The signal sent from pin 6 of stalk unit H5 enables operation of headlamp washers . See E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER The rain sensor is connected to the control unit at pins C3 and C7 for the power supply and earth and at pin A2 for the actual signal. This sensor permits automatic wiper operation when it rains.

Description The rearscreen wiper is operated by turning the ring nut on the end of the lever located on the right of the steering wheel. By pushing the lever gently towards the steering wheel the rearscreen washer function is activated; the same pump is used as for the windscreen washer (two-way), but it rotates in the opposite direction and sends the detergent fluid to the rear. If the lever is kept pressed, the rearscreen wiper comes on and operates for a few moments after the lever is released. When the lever is released, the windscreen wipers will continue to operate for several strokes. The rearscreen wash/wipe can only be operated with the ignition switched ON. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and is operated by the ignition-operated relay located in the junction unit.

Functional description The stalk unit H5 is supplied at pin 3 of connector D from the ignition-operated line (INT/A) of the relay R1 protected by the fuse F14 : both are contained in the junction unit B1 . The rear wiper is activated by stalk switch H5 via a signal sent by pin 1 of connector D to rear wiper motor N16 . When operated, the windscreen washer switch on the steering column switch unit H5 sends two signals from pin 8 and pin 9 of connector A, which reach the pump for operating the windscreen washer N22 directly. The motor is operated upon a command from stalk switch H5 in the opposite manner to that described for the washer function (when the motor is operated in reverse, it sends fluid to the back instead of to the front). One of the two signals (pin 2 of connector D of H5 ) is sent to electronic device inside rear wiper motor N16 that controls the operation of the rear wiper in conjunction with the rear washer. The rear wiper motor N16 is then connected to earth. It consists of the actual geared motor, the end of travel contacts and the electronic adjustment and control device.

Description The headlamp washer device is responsible for washing the front windscreen and the headlamp lens. The headlamp washer function is operated automatically, with the side lights on, when the windscreen washer is operated by a stalk lever to the right of the steering wheel. The headlamp washer device consists of a detergent delivery pump and a nozzle in the bumpers that sprays a powerful jet onto the headlamp. The headlamp washer circuit is protected by a specific fuse and regulated by an electronic timer device, located on the right under the dashboard. The timer operates the headlamp washer pump in a series of half-second pulses.

Functional description The headlamp washer J50 is supplied (pin 30) by the direct line from the battery through the headlamp washer fuse B12 and the maxifuse J/B2 of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99. If the windscreen washer switch is operated, stalk switch H5 sends two signals to the windscreen wiper motor N15 ; one of these reaches headlamp washer timer J50 (pin S): it is the power source for the ignition-operated line (INT/A) of relay R1 protected by fuse F14 . ( ). See E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE With the side lights on, a signal reaches pin 56 of J50 from the steering column switch unit H5 line. ( ). See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS When there are both signals at pins S and 56, the relay, inside the device J50 which supplies the electric headlamp washer pump N25 with impulses of about half a second, is energized for a certain time.

Description The rear window heater element, door mirror demister coils and the windscreen heater element absorb a considerable amount of energy. They must therefore be turned off once they have been working for a certain period of time. The demisting of the heated rear windscreen and the rear view mirrors takes place with a timer, according to the following logic. The system is turned on with: the ignition in the ON position engagement signal coming from the special button, in the air conditioning/heater control panel (or from the "rapid demisting" function of the actual air conditioner). The resistances remain supplied for 20 minutes, then the power supply is cut off. The power supply is also cut off under the following conditions: ignition key in the OFF position; disengagement signal from the button (or from the "rapid demisting" function); after the initial 10 minutes of operation, if the battery voltage goes below 11.6 V (if the voltage goes back up above 13 V, then the supply is restored). This control logic is managed by the integrated services control unit on the right hand side, under the dashboard. (the climate control/heater control unit only "houses" the control button and the LED, but does not affect the activation logic in any way). The defrosting circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a specific relay located in the junction box. Description The power supply is also cut off under the following conditions: The control button always has priority over the "rapid demisting" function: for example, if the heated rear windscreen is switched on automatically by the "rapid demisting" function and the button is pressed, the heated rear windscreen is deactivated. Description The LED in the button stays on whilst the heated rear windscreen is activated.

Functional description The heated rear windscreen relay R3 , located in the junction unit B1 , controls the simultaneous activation of the demisting of both the rear windscreen P55 and the external rear view mirrors P60 and P61 . The relay R3 is supplied by the direct line from the battery through the fuse F11 - always for B1 - and the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99. The supply for the coil for relay R2 is controlled by the ignition. (INT/A) of line protected by fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. An earth signal coming from the integrated services control unit M40 (pin 9 of connector B) energizes the coil of the relay R1 , with the supply consequently sent to resistors P55 , P60 and P61 . (the control circuit of the heated rear window P55 passes through the aerial P22 control unit. ( ) See E3510 RADIO The control unit M40 is supplied when the ignition (INT) is switched on from the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 (pin 7 of connector B). Functional description When an earth command is received (pin 14 of connector B) coming from the climate control unit M70 (heated rear windscreen on button pressed), according to the control logic described previously, a command is sent which energizes the coil of the relay R1 . (pin 9 of connector B). Similarly, when the "rapid demisting" function is activated, the control unit M70 sends a signal to pin 17 of connector B of M40 . Functional description At the same time as the activation of the resistors, a signal is sent (from pin 11, of connector B of M40 ) to light up the LED in the control button which is located in the climate control unit M70 . Functional description When an earth command is received (pin 14 of connector B) coming from the heater H80 (heated rear windscreen on button pressed), according to the control logic described previously, a command is sent which energizes the coil of the relay R1 . (pin 9 of connector B). At the same time as the activation of the resistors, a signal is sent (from pin 11, of connector B of M40 ) to light up the LED in the control button which is located in H80 .

Description The two external rear view mirrors are adjusted by the control on the central console between the seats, which is lit up when the side lights are on. The two mirrors are adjusted by a single button pressed in the four directions: a switch selects the right or left mirror. The button, which can be pressed in four directions, controls two electric motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor rotates the mirror on a horizontal axis, while the other on a vertical axis. The motors which adjust the vertical position are connected to pin 5 of the mirrors P60 and P61 , the motors which adjust the horizontal position are connected to pin 3. According to the selector position, either the left motors (output signals from pins 6 and 8 of H30) or the right motors (output signals from pins 5 and 7 of H30 ) are connected; the common supply comes out of pin 3 and is connected to pin 5 of the motors. the common supply comes out of pin 3 and is connected to pin 5 of the motors. Functional description The two-way switch controlling mirrors H30 operates electrical motors located in the right and left electrically-operated door mirrors P60 and P61 respectively. According to the selector position, either the left motors (output signals from pins 4 and 9 of H30 ) or the right motors (output signals from pins 12 and 2 of H30 ) are connected; the common supply comes out of pin 8 and is connected to pin 5 of the motors. The switch H30 is lit up when the side lights are switched on by means of the line coming from the stalk unit switch H5 (pin 5).

Description The simultaneous operation of the four lock motors takes place upon a command: from the key from the front door switches (knobs); from the remote control Lock operation is controlled by the integrated service control unit located on the right hand side beneath the facia. The control unit monitors lock status by means of signals received from switches located on the four locks (these signals are also used to time the lighting). A lock command is issued only when all doors are properly closed and the front locks are released. Conversely, a release command is issued only when the front catches are locked. Conversely, a release command is issued only when the front catches are locked. The control unit also runs a series of safety checks: switch position is checked at the end of each operation. If this position does not agree with the action carried out (e.g. if a door is open), a repulsion command is issued, i.e. the opposite manoeuvre is carried out to realign all the locks. if the control unit detects too many complete, consecutive lock/release manoeuvres - at least 8 within 20 seconds - the system cuts in to limit the manoeuvres: the system is inhibited in release position for 30 seconds. if battery voltage drops below 9 V during a lock/release operation, the system suspends the operation. If battery voltage is lower than 9 V at the outset, no command is issued. The door lock circuit is protected by a special fuse located in the junction unit. The remote control receiver has supplies (direct and controlled by the ignition) protected by two fuses located in the junction unit.

Functional description The integrated services control unit M40 which manages the operation of the central locking. The direct supply for the control unit M40 (pin 8 of connector B) arrives directly from the battery via the line protect by maxifuse J/B2 (of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99) and fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 .; ; pin 13 of connector B provides the reference earth. The receiver for the remote control M35 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (IINT) from the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 and directly from the battery through the line of maxifuse J/B1 (of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99) and of fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 . The control unit M40 receives the following inputs: commands coming from the front locks N50 and N51 for locking (pin 15 of connector B) or for unlocking (pin 16 of connector B) the doors; signals on the state of the door locks, coming from the four geared motors N50 , N51 , N55 and N56 , respectively at pins 2 and 3 of connector B and 3 and 7 of connector C. ( ). See E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS (only with remote control) the signals from the remote control M35 receiver for locking (pin 6 of connector C) or for unlocking (pin 15 of connector C); In accordance with the logic described above, the control unit M40 controls the locks: the signals for the motors of the front doors ( N50 and N51 ) and rear doors ( N55 ed N 56 ) come from pins 4 and 5 of connector B.

Description The lock motors of all four doors are activated simultaneously upon a command: from the key from the front door switches (knobs); from the remote control; through the operation of the inertia switch. Lock operation is controlled by the integrated service control unit located on the right hand side beneath the facia. The control unit monitors lock status by means of signals received from switches located on the four locks (these signals are also used to time the lighting). A lock command is issued only when all doors are properly closed and the front locks are released. Conversely, a release command is issued only when the front catches are locked. The control unit also runs a series of safety checks: switch position is checked at the end of each operation. If this position does not agree with the action carried out (e.g. if a door is open), a repulsion command is issued, i.e. the opposite manoeuvre is carried out to realign all the locks. If the control unit detects several complete, consecutive lock/release manoeuvres - at least 8 within 20 seconds - the system cuts in to limit the manoeuvres: the system is inhibited in release position for 30 seconds. If battery voltage drops below 9 V during a lock/release operation, the system suspends the operation. If battery voltage is lower than 9 V at the outset, no command is issued. The door lock circuit is protected by a special fuse located in the junction unit. The remote control receiver has supplies (direct and controlled by the ignition) protected by two fuses located in the junction unit.

Functional description The integrated services control unit M40 which manages the operation of the central locking. The direct supply for the control unit M40 (pin 8 of connector B) arrives directly from the battery via the line protect by maxifuse J/B2 (of B99) and fuse F8 of the junction unit B1. ; pin 13 of connector B provides the reference earth. The receiver of the remote control M35 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 and directly from the battery via the line of the maxifuse J/B1 (of B99) and fuse F10 of the junction unit B1. The control unit M40 receives the following inputs: commands coming from the front locks N50 and N51 for locking (pin 15 of connector B) or for unlocking (pin 16 of connector B) the doors; signals on the state of the door locks, coming from the four geared motors N50, N51, N55 and N56, respectively at pins 2 and 3 of connector B and 3 and 7 of connector C. See E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS . the signals from the remote control M35 receiver for locking (pin 6 of connector C) or for unlocking (pin 15 of connector C); the signal for the inertia switch I50 at pin 10 of connector B; In accordance with the strategy described above, the control unit M40 controls the locks: the signals for the motors of the front doors ( N50 and N51 ) and rear doors ( N55 and N56 ) come from pins 4 and 5 of connector B.

Description The electric front windows are operated automatically, depending on how the switch is pressed: for the driver's window: the operation is manual (the glass goes up/down only when the button is pressed) when the button is held down for 60 to 300 milliseconds; the operation is instead automatic (the glass continues to go up/down to the end of travel, even if the button is released) when the button is held down for over 300 milliseconds; if the button is pressed again during movement of the glass, the glass is stopped instantly; if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, it is ignored (it is considered to have been knocked accidentally). for the passenger's window: closing is only manual; opening is the same as for the driver's window (automatic). Both windows can only be operated when the ignition is on. This operating logic is controlled by the integrated services control unit, on the right hand side, under the dashboard. The control unit also carries out a series of safety checks: the stopping of the electric windows (switching off the electric supply to the motor) is determined when the glass reaches the end of travel at top or bottom, or if an obstacle blocks the glass. This is regulated by checking the motor current. if there are faults on the electrical circuits, the control unit switches the system off temporarily (for example if the motor control signals are interrupted or if the absorbed current is below the usual values); if there is a fault in the control buttons (short circuit, or buttons jammed in the pressed position), the control unit switches the system off temporarily The control circuit for the front electric windows is protected by a specific fuse, in the junction unit. The operating buttons are also protected by the fuse which protects the other supplied controlled by the ignition. The control switch symbols are lit when the key is turned to MAR.

Functional description The integrated services control unit M40 manages the operation of the electric front windows. The direct supply from the battery for control unit M40 specific to the electric windows (pin 15 and 16 of connector A) arrives from the line protected by maxifuse J/B1 (of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99) and fuse F12 of junction unit B1 , while the supply controlled by the ignition reaches pin 7 of connector B from the line for fuse F1 ; pins 4 and 20 of connector A provide the reference earth for the passenger and driver's electric windows, respectively. The switches H40 (driver's electric window), H41 (passenger electric window on driver's door) and H50 (passenger electric windoe on passenger front door) receive a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) from the line from fuse B10 up to 2/99 or from fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99, and are earthed C20 : in this way they are also lit up when the ignition is switched on. When the switches are operated, they send control signals (positive and negative) to control unit M40: at pins 10 and 11 of connector A from switch H40 ; at pins 5 and 18 of connector A from switch H41 ; at pins 2 and 6 of connector A from switch H50 ; The control unit M40 operates the electric windows on the basis of the logic described previously: from pins 8 and 9 of connector A it sends commands to the driver's electric window motor N60 from pins 1and 3 of connector A it sends commands to the passenger electric window motor N61. When the positive and negative signals are reversed, the motor's direction of rotation is also reversed.

Description The sunroof offers extra ventilation for the interior compartment and ensures a rapid air exchange, if required, thus increasing passenger comfort. The moving part of the roof consists of a glass panel and an internal sliding blind which enters the actual roof lining. The latter can also be operated manually and guarantees protection against the sun's rays. The system is operated by a switch, located near the front courtesy light, which controls a motor with two different operating modes: press one end of the switch to raise the roof in "compass" fashion, and press the other end of the switch to slide the roof open and so pull the blind: when the switch is released, the roof stops in the position it is in at that moment. when the roof is closed, the blind is carried along a short distance by the forward motion of the panel. The entire system consists of a single unit which comprises: the control unit A, which manages the operation of the roof; the actuating motor C; the control switch B; the end-of-travel switches D, located on a ring nut outside the motor, which stop the motor when the roof is fully open or closed. For more details, . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 7030 SUN ROOF AND HOOD The sunroof circuit is protected by a specific fuse, and controlled by a relay which supplies other "ignition-operated" services. The fuse is located inside the junction unit, and the relay is located on the right hand side of the facia. The sunroof can only be operated with the ignition on.

Functional description The optional services relay J60 controls the roof circuit (as well as the electric rear windows and heated seats: and See E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS ). See E3075 HEATED SEATS The coil of the relay J60 is energized when the ignition is switched on (INT/A) by the line for fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99, while the supply at the relay contact arrives from the battery, through the line for maxifuse J/B2 (of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99). This supply passes through the sunroof B14 up to 2/99 or F1 of B98B from 2/99., which protects the circuit, and reaches the sunroof motor N35 , at pin 1: it is actually a single unit which includes: the control unit A, the switch B, the motor itself C and the limit switches D. The unit is also connected to earth C20 at pin 3. The switch is therefore active when the ignition is on (INT/A). The control unit controls engine movement according to switch position.

Description The front seats may be optionally fitted with a special heating system (consisting of two heater elements located in the cushion and squab): these heat the seat to ease the discomfort of entering a cold passenger compartment in very cold weather, e.g. when the car is left outside for long periods during winter. The heating device located on each seat consists of two resistors operated by a switch located on the side of the seat. Once a certain temperature is reached, the heating action is automatically cut off by a thermal contact inside the device. An LED indicates when the heater is on. The seat heating circuit is protected by a special fuse and is controlled by a relay which supplies other services controlled by the ignition. both are located on the right hand side under the facia. The seat heating operates only whe the key is turned to MAR.

Functional description The optional services relay J60 controls the heating circuit for the seats as well as the electric rear windows and sun roof: , See E3060 SUN ROOF . See E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS Functional description The coil for relay J60 is energized when the ignition is switched on (INT/A) by the line for fuse B10, whilst the supply at the relay contact arrives from the battery, through the line for maxifuse J/B2 of B5. Functional description The coil of the relay J60 is energized when the ignition is switched on (INT/A) by the line for fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B, while the supply at the relay contact arrives from the battery, through the line for maxifuse J/B2 of B99. Functional description By pressing the switch on the seat the resistors for the heaters in the left and right seats, 040 and 041, connected in parallel, are supplied, until a thermal contact inside the heaters disconnects the resistors when the temperature exceeds a certain limit. This supply passes through the heated seats fuse B20 , which guarantees the protection of the circuit and reaches the switches in the seats through connection D70 (left seat) and D71 (right seat): the supply for the two devices is therefore controlled by the ignition (INT/A) and they are connected to earth C20 . When the resistors are on, an LED signals the operation of the device.

Description A device allows the headlamp beam to be adjusted, directly from the driver's seat, in accordance with the load. The headlamps are thus always aligned quickly and correctly. The adjustment device consists of a motor mounted on each of the two headlamps which tilts them as appropriate, lowering the light beam if the car is heavily laden, and raising it if the load decreases. A specific knob on the dashboard selects the four positions indicated: position 0 - one or two persons on the front seats, full fuel tank, car fully equipped and in running order; position 1 - five persons; position 2 - five persons with luggage compartment full (about 50 kg); position 3 - driver and 300 kg load, all stowed in boot. The adjustment button is on the left of the actual instruments, together with the button for zeroing the mileometer and the instrument lighting dimmer switch; The control switches have symbols which are lit up when the side lights are on. The device is enabled only when the dipped beam headlamps are on. The headlamp adjustment circuit is protected by the same fuses as the dipped beam headlamps circuit, located in the junction unit.

Functional description The headlamp alignment device in H10 is supplied at pin 3 by a line coming from the circuit for the dipped beam headlamps, protected by fuse F5 of the junction unit B1 ; this line only supplies voltage to the regulator when the dipped beam headlamps are switched on. ( ) this line provides voltage to the regulator only when the dipped beams are on. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS Pin 4 of device H10 is earthed, whilst pin 2 sends the signal to adjust the motors N30 (left) and N31 (right), through a resistive divider which alters the output voltage depending on which of the four positions has been selected. Motors N30 and N31 contain a transducer that establishes actual motor travel on the basis of the voltage of an adjustment signal received by pin 2 from device H10 . The motors are supplied through pins 3 from the line (part of the dipped beam circuit) that supplies device H10 , while pins 1 are earthed. The headlamp alignment device H10 is lit up (at pin 1) when the side lights are switched on by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 and protected by the controls illumination fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99.

The headlamp aglinment device H10 is lit up (at pin 1) when the side lights are switched on by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 and is protected by fuse F1 of the additional fuse box B98B .

Description The vehicle is equipped with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps. For more details . Characteristic of working principle 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING The left headlamp is the Master control unit while the right acts as a Slave unit. The master downloads the dipped beam command, car speed and - to manage the function - signals from two sensors (potentiometric) on the wheel axles that manage front and rear ride. The control unit controls the adjustment motor - located in the headlamps - and tilts it by the required amount on the basis of input. on the version with gas discharge headlamps, the light beam is adjujsted automatically and the two buttons on the left side of the panel are no longer active. The device is enabled only when the dipped beam headlamps are on. The electronics for the two headlamps are supplied by a fuse that also protects other power supplies controlled by the ignition.

Functional description The two electronics inside the headlamps F10A (left) and F11A (right) are supplied - pin 6 - by the line controlled by the ignition (INT) protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B ; pin 14 of F10A and F11A are earthed. Pin 8 of F10A and F11A are connected to one another (serial communication line between MASTER and SLAVE), whilst pin 13 of the control unit located in headlamp F10A receives the speedometer signal from instrument E10 . Headlamp F10A incorporates the headlamp alignment function: the two sensors (potentiometers) that record ride at the front K1 and the rear K2 are connected: a supply and reference earth are sent from pins 9 and 10 of F10A : the signals proportional to the load return to pins 11 and 12; according to these signals the headlamp electronics automatically adjust the light beam by means of a special motor. The left headlamp motor is adjusted directly, whilst the right one is adjusted via the serial line between F10A and F11A . The dipped headlamps control signal reaches F10A and F11A at pin 1 . See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The diagnostic line for connector R10, pin 12, leaves pin 7 of F10A and F11A.

Description The parking assistance system provides the driver with information whilst reversing relating to distance when approaching obstacles which are behind the vehicle, which could be outside the driver's field of view. The information that there is an obstacle and its distance is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic signals whose frequency varies according to the distance of the vehicle from the obstacle. An electronic control unit activates and controls the operation of the four sensors located in the rear bumper, processing the signals received and activating the acoustic signal inside the luggage compartment on the left hand side. The system is activated when reverse gear is engaged: under these conditions the control unit energizes the transducers and sends them a request signal, receiving response signals. The ultrasound technology sensors act as intelligent transmitters/receivers through a triangulation technique: this allows improved detection in critical situations or in the presence of small obstacles. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer therefore receives an echo which is converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit. The distance of the obstacle is signalled by sounds with intermittent impulses: the frequency of this signal increases gradually as the bumper approaches an obstacle: when the distance calculated is less than about 30 cm, the sound becomes high pitched and constant; the acoustic signal, on the other hand, ceases when the distance of the obstacle increases. For more details and information on the operation of the system, Characteristic of working principle 5580H parking obstacle detection device The control unit has an autodiagnostic function: when it is switched on the control unit carries out an initial test on the sensors.which are then continuously diagnosed during the operation of the system. A fault with only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system: in this case, the system excludes itself: the failure status is signalled sending a suitable high frequency acoustic warning. The system is activated with reverse gear engaged; the signal that the reversing light has come on supplies the parking sensors control unit directly. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS

Functional description The parking sensor control unit M84 is supplied at pin 1 of connector A by the ignition-operated line INT protected by fuse F1 of junction unit B1 with this line sending the power supply to the control unit M84 with reverse gear engaged (switch I20) this supply is also sent from pin 6 to pin 9 of connector A of M84; pins 16 of connector A of M84 is earthed. The control signals for activating the buzzer P44 are sent from pins 2 and 10 of connector A of M84. The four parking sensors K97 are connected to connector B of control unit M84; pin 1 provides the reference earth, pin 6 the power supply to the sensors; pin 4 supplies the signal to the right outer sensor K97D, pin 2 to the right inner sensor K97C, pin 3 to the right inner sensor K97B and pin 5 to the left outer sensor K97.

Description The vehicle is prepared for the installation of a radio system. This preparation comprises: radio compartment radio supply cables separate front power and tweeter speakers, located in the doors; rear speakers, located in the doors; rear speakers on the rear parcel shelf leads connecting the radio to the speakers; aerial built into the heated rear windscreen by means of a suitable electronic device and connected to the radio through a coaxial cable. The radio circuit is supplied with the key turned to the ON position, or directly from the battery (which allows tuning settings, security codes, etc. to be stored). The above two lines are protected by a fuse in the junction unit. In addition to the radio there is also a supply with the side lights on to light up the radio controls. On request, a radio specially designed for this car may be fitted during production. There are two different types to choose from. Full radio specifications and operating instructions are given in the OWNER'S HANDBOOK. Several anti-interference suppressors have been fitted to the wiring to silence all those electrical consumers which could interfere with the radio circuit. A multi-polar cable, connecting the radio with the CD player, located in the boot, can be fitted on request.

Functional description The radio P20 is supplied directly (pins 4 and 7 of connector A) by the battery via the line for fuse F10 of junction unit B1 and maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99. It receives a supply when the ignition is switched on (INT) (pin 3 of connector A) via the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . With the side lights switched on, the supply reaches pin 6 of connector A by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 , protected by the controls illumination fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99; the radio controls are therefore lit up when the lide lights are switched on. Pin 8 of connector A, on the other hand, is earthed ( C20 ). Pin 5 of connector A is connected to the control unit P22 which controls the aerial built into the heated rear windscreen. The control unit P22 is then connected to the radio by means of the specific aerial lead. Connector B sends out cables carrying signals to the speakers: pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45 , pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46 , pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P40 , pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P41 .

Description La vettura è predisposta per l'installazione di un impianto autoradio. La predisposizione prevede: vano autoradio cavi di alimentazione della radio stessa altoparlanti anteriori di potenza e tweeter separati collocati nelle porte; altoparlanti posteriori collocati nelle porte; altoparlanti posteriori sul ripiano sottolunotto cavi di collegamento dell'autoradio con gli altoparlanti stessi; antenna integrata nel lunotto termico mediante un opportuno dispositivo elettronico, e collegata mediante cavo coassiale con l'autoradio. Il circuito autoradio è alimentato sia con chiave su MAR, che con un'alimentazione diretta dalla batteria (che consente la memorizzazione di sintonie, codici di sicurezza, ecc.). Le due linee suddette sono protette da due fusibili della centralina di derivazione. All'autoradio giunge anche un'alimentazione a luci di posizione inserite, per illuminare i comandi della radio stessa. A richiesta viene inoltre installata direttamente in produzione un'autoradio appositamente disegnata per questa vettura.. E' possibile scegliere tra due tipi diversi. Tutti i dettagli sulle caratteristiche e sul funzionamento di tali radio sono riportati sul libretto "USO E MANUTENZIONE". Sono stati anche inseriti sul cablaggio alcuni soppressori antidisturbo, a garanzia di un "silenziamento elettronico" di tutte quelle utenze elettriche che potrebbero interferire sul circuito radio. A richiesta è possibile l'installazione di un cavo multipolare di collegamento dell'autoradio con un lettore di CD collocabile nel baule.

Functional description L'autoradio P20 è alimentata direttamente (pin 4 e 7 del connettore A) dalla batteria tramite la linea del fusibile F10 della centralina di derivazione B1 e il maxifuse J/B1 di B5 [fino a 2/99] oppure di B99 [da 2/99]. Riceve invece l'alimentazione "sotto chiave" (INT) (pin 3 del connettore A) tramite la linea del fusibile F1 della centralina di derivazione B1 . Al pin 6 del connettore A giunge l'alimentazione a luci di posizione inserite tramite la linea proveniente dall'interruttore del devioguida H5 e protetta dal fusibile illuminazione comandi B11 [fino a 2/99] oppure dal fusibile F4 della scatola portafusibili supplementare B98B [da 2/99]: in tal modo i comandi dell'autoradio sono illuminati a luci di posizione inserite. Il pin 8 del connettore A è invece a massa ( C20 ). Il pin 5 del connettore A è collegato con la centralina P22 , che controlla l'antenna integrata nel lunotto termico. La centralina P22 è poi collegata alla radio per mezzo dell'apposito cavo antenna. Dal connettore B escono i cavi con i segnali verso gli altoparlanti: pin 5 e 6 agli altoparlanti anteriori lato sinistro P35 e P45 , pin 3 e 4 agli altoparlanti anteriori lato destro P36 e P46 , pin 7 e 8 agli altoparlanti posteriori lato sinistro P30 e P40 , pin 1 e 2 agli altoparlanti posteriori lato destro P31 e P41 ,

Functional description The radionavigator P20 is supplied directly (pin 4 of connector A) by the battery via the line for fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 and the maxifuse J/B1 of B99 . It receives a supply when the ignition is switched on (INT) (pin 7 of connector A) via the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . With the side lights switched on, the supply reaches pin 6 of connector A by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 , protected by the controls illumination fuse F1 of the additional fuse box B98 B ; the radionavigator controls are therefore lit up when the lide lights are switched on. Pin 8 of connector A, on the other hand, is earthed ( C20 ). Pin 5 of connector A is connected to the control unit P22 which controls the aerial built into the heated rear windscreen. The control unit P22 is then connected to the radio by means of the specific aerial lead. On the version with a NAVIGATOR, an interface P132 connecting the radio navigator and the BOSE amplifier P70 is required. The amplifier P70 is supplied directly by the battery via the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 C . It is then connected by a special line to the radio P20 - pin 6 of connector C - which sends the signal to switch on the amplifier. The interface P132 also receives the amplifier on signal - at pin 6 - from pin 6 of connector C; pin 7 of connector B is earthed. Pins 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 16, 11 and 12 send out signals to the 'Bose' HIFI system amplifier P70 which, in turn, is connected to the speakers: P35 , P40 , P41 and P36 . Control signals from connector C of P20 reach pins 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5; these signal are together in a suitably screened five-pole cable. Functional description The rear woofer speaker P92 is outside the amplifier located in the rear parcel shelf. Functional description The rear woofer speaker P92 is built into the casing that also houses the amplifier.

Description A Blaupunkt radio, with a built-in GSM cellular telephone, called "RADIOPHONE", is available as an optional extra. (r) The radio is the same size as a regular radio console. The "RADIOPHONE" may be used as a radio when not using the phone or waiting for a call. The telephone system (the keyboard on the Radiophone allows the desired number to be dialled) has the following features: GSM type equipment; SIM card (which also acts as a KEY CARD); incoming number identification; debit indication. The complete system consists of: two separate aerials (one for the radio and one for the phone): the first is the aerial normally built into the rear window for the standard radio set. The second is a special aerial located at the rear in the middle of the roof. phone microphone, located on the interior rear view mirror base separate front power and tweeter speakers, located in the doors; special "twin cone" right front speaker (used by both the radio and the telephone); rear speakers, located in the doors; rear speakers on the rear parcel rack leads connecting the radio to the speakers; The radio circuit is supplied both with the ignition key in the ON position and directly from the battery. The above two lines are protected by a fuse in the junction unit. In addition to the radio there is also a supply with the side lights on to light up the radio controls. Full details of the specifications and the operation of the RADIOPHONE are given in the "OWNER'S HANDBOOK".

Functional description The radio P20 is supplied directly (pins 4 and 7 of connector A) by the battery via the line for fuse F10 of junction unit B1 and maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99. It receives a supply when the ignition is switched on (INT) (pin 3 of connector A) via the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . With the side lights switched on, the supply reaches pin 6 of connector A by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 , protected by the controls illumination fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99; the radio controls are therefore lit up when the lide lights are switched on. Pin 8 of connector A, on the other hand, is earthed ( C20 ). Pin 5 of connector A is connected to the control unit P22 , which controls the aerial built into the heated rear windscreen (radio operation). The control unit P22 is then connected to the radio by means of the specific aerial lead. Connector B sends out cables carrying signals to the speakers: pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45 , pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46 , pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P40 , pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P41 . Description For the first time special preparation is available for the installation of the "TELEPASS" device (Italian market only). This communcations system pays motorway tolls without the need to stop at a paybooth. An electronic device fitted to the car emits a sound pulse that is picked up by a receiver on the paybooth, through which the car drives at moderate speed but without stopping. The option takes the form of a specific rear view mirror that contains housing for this electronic device in addition to device wiring. The device is operated when the ignition key is turned to MAR. The above lines are protected by a fuse in the junction unit.

Functional description The connection for the TELEPASS device D76 consists of a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) (pin 1) coming from the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 and a connection (pin 3) to earth C30 .
