Description The module includes electronic speedometer milometer and trip meter / outside temperature gauge; and a series of warning lights. The speedometer signal comes from the ABS control unit; there are three 'repeater' outputs of the signal for other systems; only two are used for the electronic fuel injection and climate control system. The gauge display is produced by an electronic circuit inside the module. The milometer consists of an LCD which simultaneously displays the total and trip mileage. A special button zeros the trip meter and allows the outside temperature to be displayed. For greater detail, see . Characteristic of working principle 5560 INSTRUMENT PANEL The outside temperature reading comes from the climate control unit . Characteristic of working principle 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The button is on the left of the instruments, together with the instrument light adjustment button and the headlamp alignment control. The following warning lights are contained in this module: seat belts brake pad wear maximum catalytic converter temperature (preparation) heater plugs passenger Air Bag disabling water in diesel filter The seat belts warning light comes on when the ignition is switched ON for about 15 seconds, irrespective of whether or not the belts are fastened, to remind the driver and passengers. The brake pad warning light comes on for about 4 seconds, when the ignition is switched ON, to check that they are working properly, then it goes out. The electronic circuits inside the module also manage the test function for the warning lights of all the modules: . See E4040 INSTRUMENT WARNING LIGHTS CHECK The operation of the warning lights which are not included in other functions is illustrated; the others are described and illustrated in the diagrams dealing with the components to which they refer. The speedometer operates when the ignition is switched ON. In the 'night' conditions (side lights on), the brightness can be adjusted to 3 levels by an external button. See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING

Functional description The supply to the speedometer module E10 reaches pin 9 of connector A directly from the battery (maxifuse J/B1 of B5 ), via fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 ; the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 10 of connector A from the line protected by fuse B11 . Functional description The supply to the speedometer module E10 reaches pin 9 of connector A directly from the battery (maxifuse J/B1of B99 ) via fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 ; the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 10 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B . Functional description Pin 1 of connector A is earthed. The ABS control unit M50 sends the speedometer signal to pin 11 of connector A of E10 . The speedometer signal is sent again from pin 15 of connector A to the engine control unit M10 , which differs for the various versions and from pin 16 of connector A towards the climate control unit M70 . Functional description The same signal is sent from pin 14 of connector A to the automatic transmission control unit M54 . Functional description Pin 7 of connector A of E10 receives the signal for the outside temperature from the climate control unit M70 . The zeroing signal for the trip meter reaches pin 12 of connector B from H10 . The switch H10 has ideograms lit up when the side lights are switched on through the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 . . See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING The earth signals which provide information on the state of wear of the brake pads, coming from sensors K20 and K21 reach pin 11 of connector B. For all the other warning lights, refer to the diagrams relating to the components to which they refer. Description The module includes electronic speedometer milometer and trip meter / outside temperature gauge; and a series of warning lights. The gauge display is produced by an electronic circuit inside the module. The milometer consists of an LCD which simultaneously displays the total and trip mileage. The speedometer operates when the ignition is switched ON. In the 'night' conditions (side lights on), the brightness can be adjusted to three levels by an external button. Pin 1 of connector A is earthed. The ABS control unit M50 sends the speedometer signal to pin 11 of connector A of E10 . Functional description The same signal is sent from pin 14 of connector A to the automatic transmission control unit M54 . Functional description The same signal is sent from pin 14 of connector A to the electronics of the headlamp F10A Functional description The ABS control unit M50 also sends the 'ABS failure' signal to pin 6 of connector A of E10 which lights up the warning light. The signals for the handbrake switch I40 and brake fluid level sensor K25 both reach pin 7 of connector A of E10 . The low brake fluid level and handbrake warning light also comes on upon a command from the ABS control unit., together with the ABS failure warning light, to indicate a fault in the EBD braking system. If it comes on by itself, the brake fluid level is low or the handbrake is on. The earth signals which provide information on the state of wear of the brake pads, coming from sensor K20, reach pin 11 of connector B of E10 . The zeroing signal for the trip meter reaches pin 12 of connector B from H10 ; an earth signal from E10 reaches pin 6 of connector B; according to the logic processed by the internal electronic device, the speedometer receives the side lights on signal at pin 5 of connector B and sends the lighting signal to the other instruments: to the centre instrument E20 from pin 12 of connector A; and to the rev counter E15 from pin 4 of connector B . Description The module includes: electronic speedometer; milometer and trip meter / outside temperature gauge; and a series of warning lights. The speedometer signal comes from the ABS control unit; there are three 'repeater' outputs of the signal for other systems; only two are used for the electronic fuel injection and climate control system. The gauge display is produced by an electronic circuit inside the module. The milometer consists of an LCD which simultaneously displays the total and trip mileage. A special button zeros the trip meter. The button is on the left of the instruments, together with the instrument light adjustment button and the headlamp alignment control. . The following warning lights are contained in this module: brake pad wear 'VDC/ASR failure/on' 'ABS failure' 'insufficient brake fluid level/handbrake applied' 'EOBD function' The electronic circuits inside the module also manage the test function for the warning lights of all the modules . The operation of the warning lights which are not included in other functions is illustrated; the others are described and illustrated in the diagrams dealing with the components to which they refer. The speedometer operates when the ignition is switched ON. In the 'night' position (side lights on), the brightness can be adjusted to three levels by an external button. See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING for versions without the VDC option, refer to the specific wiring diagram

Functional description The supply to the speedometer module E10 reaches pin 9 of connector A directly from the battery (maxifuse J/B1of B99 ) via fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 ; the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 10 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B . Pin 1 of connector A is earthed. The ABS control unit M50 sends the speedometer signal to pin 11 of connector A of E10 . The speedometer signal is resent from pin 15 of connector A towards the climate control system control unit M70. A fuel consumption figure is sent from pin 16 of connector A towards the engine management control unit M10. Functional description The same signal is sent from pin 14 of connector A to the automatic transmission control unit M54 . Functional description The same signal is sent from pin 14 of connector A to the electronics of the headlamp F10A Functional description The ABS control unit M50 also sends the 'ABS failure' signal to pin 6 of connector A of E10 which lights up the warning light. The signals for the handbrake switch I40 and brake fluid level sensor K25 both reach pin 7 of connector A of E10 . The low brake fluid level and handbrake warning light also comes on upon a command from the ABS control unit., together with the ABS failure warning light, to indicate a fault in the EBD braking system. . See E7020 ABS If it comes on by itself, the brake fluid level is low or the handbrake is on. The earth signals which provide information on the state of wear of the brake pads, coming from sensor K20, reach pin 11 of connector B of E10 . The zeroing signal for the trip meter reaches pin 12 of connector B from H10 ; an earth signal from E10 reaches pin 6 of connector B; according to the logic processed by the internal electronic device, the speedometer receives the side lights on signal at pin 5 of connector B and sends the lighting signal to the other instruments: to the centre instrument E20 from pin 12 of connector A; and to the rev counter E15 from pin 4 of connector B . See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING A signal reaches pin 3 of connector B from the left front door switch N50 which signals that the door is open. Pin 2 of connectorA of E10 receives the earth signal from the switch l45 , located on the driver's seat anchorage, which indicates that the belt is fastened: this signal is sent again from pin 3 of connector A to the check module E30 . A serial line connects module E10 - from pin 8 of connector A - to the Infocenter module E63 . Pins 2 and 7 of connector B receive (positive and negative) signals coming from the fuel gauge N40 located in the fuel pump assembly: these signals are then sent again - from pins 9 and 10 of connector B - to the centre instrument E20 . If, on the other hand, it comes on by itself, the brake fluid level is low or the handbrake is on. Functional description The supply controlled by the ignition (INT) for the check module E30 reaches pin 13 of the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B ; pins 2, 5, 10, 12 and 14 are earthed. The signals for the handbrake switch I40 and brake fluid level sensor K25 both reach pin 7 of connector A of E10. and from there are resent to the check module E50, pin 4. The low brake fluid level and handbrake warning light also comes on upon a command from the ABS control unit., together with the ABS failure warning light, to indicate a fault in the EBD braking system. . See E7020 ABS If it comes on by itself, the brake fluid level is low or the handbrake is on. For all the other warning lights, refer to the diagrams for the components to which they refer.

Description The module in the centre of the dashboard includes the: fuel gauge, with reserve warning light engine coolant temperature gauge, with maximum temperature warning light analogue clock. The fuel level is displayed via electronic circuitry inside the module, which operates the gauge and the reserve warning light (about 7 litres) and "dampens" the signal preventing fluctuations. During starting, when the ignition is turned on, the warning light comes on for about 4 seconds as a self-test, then goes out. If it flashes and stays on, a fault has been detected in the connection or the level gauge. The coolant temperature gauge is controlled directly by a sensor on the engine. The maximum temperature warning light is controlled by a sensor on the engine with another signal, independent of the gauge, or by the engine control unit. During starting, when the ignition is turned on, the maximum temperature warning light comes on for about 4 seconds as a self-test, then goes out. The analogue clock consists of a face with hour and minute hands. It is electronic with a quartz oscillator. It is adjusted by means of a button inside the dial. The centre instrument operates when the ignition is switched ON. In the "night" position (side lights on), the brightness can be adjusted to three levels by an external button. ( ). See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING

Functional description The supply for the centre module E20 arrives directly from the battery. (maxifuse J/B1 of B5 ) to pin 2 via fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 . the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 1 from the line protected by fuse B11 . Pin 3 is earthed. Functional description The standard engine temperature sender unit K36 sends a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant (pin 1) to pin 10 of E20 . The minimum temperature signal, on the other hand, arrives at pin 9 of E20 from the engine control unit M10 . Functional description Sender unit K35 sends two independent signals: the first is proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant: it reaches pin 10 of module E20 and acts on the gauge; the second signal, connected to the maximum temperature thermal contact, reaches pin 9 and causes the relevant warning light to come on. Functional description Sender unit K35 sends a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant to pin 10 of module E20 . The overheating signal reaches pin 9 from the engine control unit M10 . Functional description Pins 4 and 5 of the centre instrument E20 receive signals (positive and negative) coming from the fuel gauge N40 located in the fuel pump unit.

Description This is a dot matrix display with electronic management/calculation and operation and a buzzer for warning signals. The selection/confirmation controls for the functions displayed by the infocenter are located near the climate control system controls and consist of 3 buttons (+/-/INFO); the SET function control button is located on the left steering column switch unit lever. Functions displayed: Engine oil level (histrograms) Service messages Speed limit (acoustic warning as well) Date Fault signal repetition Outside temperature Lighting adjustment through histrograms Language selection Doors check Operation of inertia switch Engine oil temperature (GTA only) Trip computer The instrument works with the ignition switched ON.

Functional description The supply for module E63 arrives directly from the battery. (maxifuse J/B1 of B99 ) to pin 1 via fuse F10 of junction unit B1 ; the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 3 of the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B . Description During starting (ignition switched ON), the operation of all the instruments and warning lights is tested: all the warning lights and the LEDs are switched on for around 4 seconds to check their operation. In the case of the milometer (LCD), all the LCD segments are lit up for about 4 seconds to check that they are working. This test function for the warning lights is managed by the electronic circuits inside the speedometer module which controls the test for the speedometer circuits and sends signals to the rev counter and to the auxiliary instrument and the check module.

Functional description The supply controlled by the ignition (INT) for the speedometer module E10 reaches pin 10 of connector A from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. Pin 1 of connector A is earthed. The "warning lights test" signal is sent: to the auxiliary instrument E20 (pin 6) from pin 4 of connector A; to the check panel E30 (pin 14) from pin 3 of connector A; to the rev counter E15 (pin 10 of connector B) from pin 3 of connector B.

Description The navigation system informs you of the vehicle's position on the map (in relation to both urban and non-urban/motorway road networks). In this way, the driver is taken to the desired destination, guided step-by-step by voice messages and visual information. The system also provides additional information for reaching services of general interest, such as hotels, car parks, restaurants, pharmacies, service stations, hospitals, ALFA ROMEO garages, railway stations, airports, etc. The navigator is incorporated in the radio unit: it is a BOSCH radio navigator personalized especially for ALFA ROMEO. The navigation system uses the GPS (Global Positioning System) satellite location technology; it has the following functions: vehicle location calculation of the route identification of 'route guidance' manoeuvres management of the map data base (on CD-ROM) The navigation CD-ROM reader is located in the radio unit itself. the navigation system operates only with the CD-ROM inserted in the specific drive; however it is possible to listen to a music CD during navigation. In this case, the navigation function requires the map CD to be inserted during execution of the route calculation procedures. The GPS system consists of an aerial which allows the GPS satellite location of the vehicle: the aerial is connected to the relevant receiver, located in the integrated unit, via a specific shielded cable. The antenna is mounted at the rear of the roof: it has two functions (GSM/GPS) as it also incorporates the GSM aerial where the CONNECT system is also fitted. See E4091 CONNECT The vehicle position is identified by the analysis of the GPS data and the speedometer and reverse gear signals coming from the car. This position is shown on the monochromatic display in the centre of the radionavigator. When the vehicle is new or after any operation on the navigation system, the test and calibration procedures must be carried out as indicated in . Characteristic of working principle 5570 ACCESSORIES On the CONNECT version with a NAVIGATOR it is not possible to have a direct connection between the radio and the GSM/GPS aerial. A special GSM BOX, located in the glove compartment, is fitted to act as an electronic interface. For more details . Characteristic of working principle 5570 ACCESSORIES

It receives a supply when the ignition is switched on (INT) (pin 7 of connector A) via the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . With the side lights switched on, the supply reaches pin 6 of connector A by means of the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 , protected by the controls illumination fuse F1 of the additional fuse box B98 ; the radionavigator controls are therefore lit up when the lide lights are switched on. Pin 8 of connector A, on the other hand, is earthed ( C20 ). Pin 1 receives a speedometer signal from instrument E10 . Pin 3 receives a reverse engaged signal from switch I20 . See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS The GSM BOX interface electronic device P131 is supplied directly (pin 11); it receives a supply directly from the battery via the line for fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 and the maxifuse J/B1 of B99 ; it also receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) (pin 10) via the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . Pins 9 and 18 are connected to the microphone P26 by means of a suitably screened cable; pins 16, 7 and 4 (outputs to the speakers) are connected to the radionavigator P20 , connector D, whilst pins 8 and 17 are connected to the connector P20 F (CAN communication network between GSM BOX and radio).

Description The ignition and recharging circuit comprises a battery, starter motor and alternator. The battery (12V) is low maintenance lead type. The starter motor consists of a direct current motor supplied by the battery and an excitation solenoid. When the ignition key is turned to the extreme position (AVV), the starter motor windings are supplied, producing electro-magnetic forces which rotate the motor pinion. At the same time, the solenoid is energized and operates the mechanism for engaging the pinion in the flywheel ring, thus turning the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft by means of a belt. When supplied with an excitation current, the rotor sets up a magnetic field that induces an alternating current in the fixed coil (stator). A diode rectifying bridge located on the back of the alternator transforms the alternating current into a direct current, which is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage regulator, also built into the alternator, maintains a constant voltage supply (about 14V) throughout the load and engine speed ranges.

Functional description When the ignition key for the switch H1 is turned to the extreme position (AVV) the solenoid winding (pin 50) of the starter motor A20 is supplied. This supply comes from the battery via the line of maxifuse IGN of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99. Pin 30 of A20 , the actual starter motor, receives the voltage coming directly from the battery A1 . The direct current generated by alternator A10 (pin B+) is directed to battery A1 , passing through motor A20 . When the alternator is not turning and therefore not recharging the battery, an earth signal is sent from pin D+ to the rev counter module E15 , pin 7 of connector B. Module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 15 of connector A from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99; when this signal arrives, the "recharging" warning light comes on. When the engine has been started up this signal becomes 12 V and the warning light goes out.

Description The engine radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of one fan operated at two different speeds. the first speed is activated at a first coolant temperature level or at a certain air conditioner coolant pressure. the second speed cuts in at a higher temperature or pressure threshold. The operation of the fan is achieved by means of special relays located in the engine compartment, near the battery. The supply line for the fan is protected by a special maxifuse, whilst the circuit for energizing the relays is protected by the fuse which protects numerous other services controlled by the ignition. The fan therefore only comes on when the ignition is switched ON.

Functional description The supply for fan N11 arrives directly from the battery from the line for the VENT maxifuse of B6 up to 2/99 or FAN 1 of B99 from 2/99: the fan therefore works when it receives an earth command. The relays J30 and J31 , specific to the cooling system, receive a supply at their coils controlled by the ignition (15/54) protected by fuse B25 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. They are energized by an earth signal coming from the engine control unit M10 . If the engine coolant temperature reaches the first temperature stage, or the 4-stage pressure switch K10 (pin 3) signals to the control unit M10 that the first pressure stage has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends an earth signal to the 1st speed fan relay J30 which energizes the coil. The relay then sends an earth signal which, via the additional resistor O10 , operates the fan N11 which rotates at the first (slow) speed. If the engine coolant reaches a higher temperature level or the 4-stage pressure switch K10 (pin 6) signals to the control unit M10 that a higher pressure stage has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends an earth signal to the 2nd speed fan relay J31 which energizes the coil. Description The engine radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of two fans connected in parallel. They are operated together at two different speeds by the same software. the first speed is activated at a first coolant temperature level or at a certain air conditioner coolant pressure. the second speed cuts in at a higher temperature or pressure threshold. The fans are activated by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines for the fans are protected by special maxifuses, whilst the energizing circuit for the relays is protected by the fuse which protects numerous other services controlled by the ignition. The fans therefore only come on when the ignition is switched ON.

Functional description The supply for the two fans N11 and N12 arrives directly from the battery from the lines of the two maxifuses FAN1 and FAN2 of B99 :the fans operate when they receive an earth command. The relays J30 , J31 and J32 , specific to the cooling system, receive supply to their coils from the line controlled by the ignition (15/54) protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A . They are energized by an earth signal coming from the engine control unit M10 . If the engine coolant temperature reaches the first temperature stage, or the 4 stage pressure switch K10 (pin 3) signals to the control unit M10 that the first pressure stage has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends an earth signal to the 1st speed fan relay J30 which energizes the coil. The relay then sends an earth which, via the additional resistors O10 and O12 , operates both fans N11 and N12 which rotate at the first (slow) speed. If the engine coolant reaches a higher temperature level, or the 4 stage pressure switch K10 (pin 6) signals to the control unit M10 that a higher pressure level has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends an earth signal to the two 2nd speed fan relays J31 and J32 which energize the coils. The two relays then send an earth directly to the two fans N11 and N12 which rotate at maximum speed.

Description The engine radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of one fan operated at two different speeds: the first speed is activated at a first coolant temperature level or at a certain air conditioner coolant pressure. the second speed cuts in at a higher temperature or pressure threshold. The fan is operated by two specific relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply line for the fan is protected by a special maxifuse, whilst the circuit for energizing the relays is protected by the fuse which protects numerous other services controlled by the ignition. The fan therefore only comes on when the ignition is switched ON.

Functional description The supply for fan N11 arrives directly from the battery from the line for the maxifuse FAN 1 of B99 : the fan therefore works when it receives an earth command. The specific relays J30 and J31 for the cooling system have coils supplied by the direct line (EFI) protected by fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98A . They are energized by an earth signal coming from the engine control unit M10 . If the engine coolant temperature reaches the first temperature stage, or the 4 stage pressure switch K10 (pin 3) signals to the control unit M10 that the first pressure stage has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends an earth signal to the 1st speed fan relay J30 which energizes the coil. The relay then sends an earth signal which, via the additional resistance O10 , operates the fan N11 which rotates at the first (slow) speed. If the engine coolant reaches a higher temperature level or the 4-stage pressure switch K10 (pin 6) signals to the control unit M10 that a higher pressure stage has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends an earth signal to the 2nd speed fan relay J31 which energizes the coil. The relay then sends an earth signal directly to the fan N11 which rotates at the maximum speed.

Description The engine radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of two fans connected in parallel. They are operated together at two different speeds in accordance with the same logic. the first speed is activated at a first coolant temperature level or at a certain air conditioner coolant pressure. The second speed cuts in at a higher temperature or pressure threshold. The fans are activated by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. Functional description The supply for the two fans N11 and N12 arrives directly from the battery from the lines of the two maxifuses FAN1 and FAN2 of B99 : the fans operate when they receive an earth command. The two relays then send an earth directly to the two fans N11 and N12 which rotate at maximum speed.

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit that controls the twin spark ignition (static and lost spark), and the injection (phased). The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; exhaust with catalytic converter; fuel vapour recirculation. On this version, the engine is fitted with a throttle body controlled electronically by the control unit. Special software inside the control unit computes throttle opening. This system does away with a connection between accelerator and throttle body. For more details, . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other jumper fuses located next to the junction unit.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The direct supply for the control unit arrives from the battery, from the line for the EFI maxifuse of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99. at pin 4 of connector B of M10 through the line protected by the fuse B35 up to 2/99 or fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) arrives from the line protected by fuse B25 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99, and energizes the main relay J10 which consequently sends the supply: to pin 2 of connector A of control unit M10 ; to injectors N70 ; to coils A30 ; to the timing sensor K47 ; to the air flow meter K41 , through the line protected by fuse B40 up to 2/99 or fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99.; to the vapour recovery solenoid valve L10 , via the line protected by fuse B40 up to 2/99 or F3 of B98A from 2/99.; to Lambda probe heater K40, via the line protected by the fuse B40 up to 2/99 or F3 of B98A from 2/99. The ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) also supplies fuel pump J15 , which is excited by a control signal (earth) from pin 29 of connector C of control unit M10 . This supplies power to the fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of impact to prevent the danger of fuel flowing out. Pins 3, 7 and 8 of connector A of control unit M10 are earthed and used as references: the first two for the ignition and the third for the injectors. Pin 8 of connector F is also earthed. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine operating parameters. Rpm sensor K46 supplies information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pins 37 and 38 of connector E of control unit M10 . Timing sensor K47 receives a reference earth from pin 39 of connector E of control unit M10 and sends back a frequency signal corresponding to the timing at pin 40 of the same connector up to 2/99. The engine temperature sensor K45 receives a reference earth from pin 28 of connector E of the control unit M10 and provides a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant at pin 29 of the same connector from 2/99. Engine temperature sender unit K36 receives a reference earth from connector E of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the coolant temperature to pin 29 of control unit connector E. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light ( ). See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Hot Lambda probe K40 provides control unit M10 with information on the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture. The signal is sent to pin 32 of control unit, while pin 31 provides a reference earth signal. Probe K40 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. the resistor is supplied by the relay J10 and receives the heating signal from pin 5 of connector A of M10 . Knock sensors K50 and K51 provide information on knock status via frequency signals sent to pins 42 and 44 respectively of control unit connector E. An earth signal is sent from pins 41 and 43 of connector E of M10 respectively. Air flow meter K41 (supplied from relay J10 ) receives a reference voltage from pin 46 of control unit connector E and sends to pin 47 of the same connector a signal proportional to air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 48 of connector E of M10 , while pin 45 of connector E receives an air temperature signal. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 22 and 23 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 24 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 27 and 26 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 25 of connector C. Pin 14 of connector D of M10 receives the signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 , with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 ( ). See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS Pin 19 of connector D of M10 receives an earth signal from clutch pedal switch I31 . Injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from main relay J10 . The engine management unit sends commands to the injectors from pins 25, 13, 1, 26, 14 and 2 of the connector, for cylinders 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively. Control unit M10 also controls coils A30 via control signals for the coil primary windings, while the secondary winding sends a pulse to the spark plugs: pins 20, 6, 17, 13, 19 and 5 of connector F control ignition coils 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively. The coil A30 primary windings receive a signal to enable opening from main relay J10 . Throttle body actuator N75 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: they control throttle opening via a stepper motor. The motor receives information from pins 1 and 2 of connector F of M10 . Pin 33 of connector E sends a power supply to both potentiometers, pin 32 of connector E supplies an earth signal to the potentiometers, while pins 31 and 34 of the same connector receive signals from throttle body actuator N75 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. The valve L10 , supplied by the main relay J10 (through the fuse B40 up to 2/99 or F3 of B98A from 2/99), is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 21 of connector C of M10 . The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a specific serial line from pin 39 of connector C; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine does not start.( ). See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-test system that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : this receives indirect signals from control unit M10 via a serial line from control unit M20 described above. (pin 39 of connector C). The self-test system also generates the signal for the "injection failure" warning light in the instrument E15 , which comes from pin 21 of connector F of control unit M10 . The module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 15 of connector A from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or from fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99; when this earth signal arrives, the "fuel injection fault" warning light comes on. The speedometer signal (car speed) reaches pin 13 of connector D of control unit M10 ( ). See E4021 SPEEDOMETER The control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to the engine rpm ( ) from pin 38 of connector C. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 4 and 21 of connector E. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 6 of connector A, 3 of connector D and 15, 17 of connector E control activation of the relevant fan ( ). See E5020 ENGINE COOLING Some versions are fitted with supplementary connector R51 for connection to the control unit. This is located in the engine bay. This connection is used solely at the Production Plant and SHOULD UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES be used during servicing.

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit that controls the twin spark ignition (static and lost spark), and the injection (phased). The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: engine cooling system; exhaust with catalytic converter; fuel vapour recirculation. The control unit also controls the hydraulic variable valve timing - an exclusive system adopted on T. SPARK engines. For more details, see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other jumper fuses located next to the junction unit.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The direct supply for the system arrives from the battery from the line for the EFI maxifuse of B5 . An ignition-operated power supply (15/54) is received on a line protected by shunt fuse B25 . The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 18, via the line protected by fuse B35 . The supply controlled by the ignition, on the other hand, arrives at pin 27, via the line protected by fuse B25 . The main relay J10 controls the entire system: it is energized by an (earth) signal coming from pin 36 of control unit M10 and, as a result, sends a supply: to pin 37 of the control unit, via the line protected by fuse B41 ; to the petrol pump relay J15 ; to injectors N70 ; to coils A30 ; to air flow meter K41 , via a line protected by fuse B40 ; to the variable valve timing system J16 , via the line protected by fuse B40 ; to fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 , via a line protected by fuse B40 ; to the idle actuator N74 , via the line protected by fuse B40 ; The fuel pump relay J15 , supplied by the main relay J10 , is energized by an (earth) signal coming from pin 3 of control unit M10 . This supplies power to the fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of impact to prevent the danger of fuel flowing out. The relay J15 also provides a supply for the Lambda sensor heater K40 via the line protected by fuse B36 . Pins 2, 14, 19 and 24 of control unit M10 are earthed and act as a reference for the ignition, the injectors, the electronic screening and the final power stages, respectively. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine operating parameters. The rpm sensor K46 provides information, through a frequency signal sent to pins 48 and 49 of control unit M10 , concerning the engine speed: these two signals have an extremely low intensity and are therefore suitable screened. The timing sensor K47 receives a 5 V supply from pin 12 of the control unit and sends a signal where the frequency corresponds to the timing at pin 8 of the control unit.: the low intensity of the signals requires them to be screened. The butterfly position sensor K56 is supplied at 5 V from pin 12 and receives a reference earth from pin 30; it sends, through a potentiometer, a signal proportional to the degree of opening of the butterfly to pin 53 of M10 . The engine temperature sensor K45 , receives a reference earth from pin 30 of the control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant to pin 45 of the control unit. The intake air temperature sensor K42 receives a reference earth from pin 30 of the control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the temperature of the air entering to pin 54 of the control unit. The heated Lambda sensor K40 provides the control unit M10 with information concerning the correct composition of the air/fuel mixture: the signal is sent to pin 28 of the control unit, whilst pin 10 provides the reference earth: the intensity of these two signals is extremely low and therefore they are appropriately shielded. Probe K40 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. the resistor is supplied by the relay J15 . The knock sensor K50 provides information concerning detonation conditions by means of a frequency signal sent to pin 11 of the control unit and receives a reference earth from pin 30. These signals are of extremely low intensity and are therefore suitably shielded. The air flow meter K41 is supplied by the relay J10 , receives a reference earth from pin 30 of the control unit and sends a signal proportional to the air flow rate to pin 7. Control unit M10 controls the opening of the individual injectors N70 , via duty-cycle signals sent to pins 17 (cyl. 1), 34 (cyl. 2), 16 (cyl. 3) and 35 (cyl. 4). Injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from main relay J10 . The control unit M10 also controls the coils A30 by means of (earth) signals for the coil primary windings, whilst the secondary winding sends an impulse to the spark plugs: from pins 1 and 21 for the pair of cylinders 1-4 and from pins 20 and 38 for cylinders 2-3. The primary windings for coils A30 receive the supply for enabling the opening from the main relay J10 . The idle actuator N74 regulates the butterfly by-pass line. It consists of two windings: one operates the opening and the other the by-pass port: it is controlled by the control unit through duty-cycle type signals for pins 22 (closing) and 4 (opening) of M10 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. Valve L10 , supplied by main relay J10 , is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 5 of M10 . The timing variator N76 mechanically controls the inlet timing advance: it is operated by the relevant relay J16 . This, supplied by the main relay J10 , is energized by means of an earth command from the control unit, pin 52 and thereby supplies the timing variator N76 . Control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a specific serial line from pin 47; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine is not started. ( ). See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-test system which can be used by connecting the unit to the connector R10 : it receives signals from pin 55 from the control unit M10 through the special diagnostic line. The self-test system also produces the signal for the "injection failure" warning light, in the instrument E15 , which comes from pin 51 of the control unit M10 . Module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 15 of connector A from the line protected by fuse B11 : when the earth signal arrives, the "injection failure" warning light comes on. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 9 of control unit M10 ( ). See E4021 SPEEDOMETER The control unit M10 sends a signal from pin 6 proportional to the engine speed ( ). See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT The control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system through pins 32 and 40. This makes it possible to adjust the engine idle speed as the load increases each time the compressor is switched on or to switch off the compressor in the case of high engine speed or load conditions ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 25, 26, 43 and 44 control the engagement of the appropriate fan ( ). See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

The module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 15 of connector A from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or from fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99; when this earth signal arrives, the "fuel injection fault" warning light comes on. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 27 of connector A of control unit M10 ( ). See E4021 SPEEDOMETER The control unit M10 sends from pin 2 of connector A a signal proportional to the engine rpm ( ). See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 19 and 31 of connector A. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 4, 13, 34 and 35 of connector A control activation of the relevant fan ( ). See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit that controls the twin spark ignition (static and lost spark), and the injection (phased). The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; exhaust with catalytic converter; fuel vapour recirculation. On this version, the engine is fitted with a throttle body controlled electronically by the control unit. Special software inside the control unit computes throttle opening. This system does away with a connection between accelerator and throttle body. The control unit also controls the hydraulic variable valve timing - an exclusive system adopted on T. SPARK engines. This version is also characterized by the adoption of a variable geometry inlet system, managed by the fuel injection control unit in accordance with the engine's operating conditions. For more details, . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other jumper fuses located next to the junction unit.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The system is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by the maxifuse EFI located on the battery, connector B99 C . The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) arrives from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 15 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The supply controlled by the ignition reaches pin 47 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . Main injection relay J10 controls the entire system: this is excited by a control signal (earth) received from pin 31 of connector A of control unit M10 and then sends power: to pins 16, 32 and 48 of connector A of the control unit, through the line protected by fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98 A . to air flow meter K41 , to fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 , to variable geometry control solenoid L15 , to variable valve timing actuator N76 and lambda probe K40 ; (all these lines are protected by fuse F2 of B98 A ). to the fuel injectors N70 , via the line protected by the fuse F3 , located in the unit B98 A ; the fuel pump relay J15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition via fuse F4 , of the additional fuse box B98 A . It is excited by a control signal (earth) from pin 30 of connector A of control unit M10 and supplies power to fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of a crash and so prevents the dangerous spilling of fuel. It also supplies power to the ignition coils A30 . The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine operating parameters. Rpm sensor K46 provides information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pins 10 and 59 of connector B of control unit M10 . These two signals are very low intensity and are therefore shielded. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 51 of connector B of control unit M10 , receives a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B and sends a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing to pin 42 of control unit connector B. Engine temperature sender unit K36 riceives a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the coolant temperature to pin 25 of control unit connector B. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light ( ). See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Hot lambda probe K40 provides control unit M10 with information on the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture. The signal is sent to pin 23 of connector B of M10 , while pin 55 provides a reference earth signal. Probe K40 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. The resistor is supplied by relay J10 and receives an earth signal from pin 34 of connector B of control unit M10 . Knock sensor K50 provides information on knock status via a frequency signal sent to pin 22 of connector B of control unit M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 54 of connector B. The signals are very low intensity and are therefore shielded. Air flow meter K41 (supplied from relay J10 ) receives a reference voltage from pin 63 of connector A and sends pin 57 of connector A a signal proportional to air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 25 of connector A of M10 , while an air temperature signal is received by pin 54 of connector A. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 56 and 24 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 8 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 7 and 25 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 40 of connector A. Pin 274 of connector A of M10 receives the signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 , with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 ( ). See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS Control unit M10 controls the opening of individual injectors N70 via duty cycle signals produced by pins 19 (cyl. 1), 52 (cyl. 2), 35 (cyl. 3) and 3 (cyl. 4) of connector B of M10 . Injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from main relay J10 . Control unit M10 also controls coils A30 via control signals (earth) for the coil primary windings, while the secondary winding sends a pulse to the spark plugs: from pins 16 and 14 of connector B for cylinder pair 1-4 and from pins 30 and 31 of connector B of M10 for cylinders 2-3. The primary windings of the coils A30 receive a signal to enable opening from main relay J15 . Throttle body actuator N75 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: they control throttle opening via a stepper motor. The motor receives information from pins 17 - 49 and 1 - 33 of connector B of M10 . Pin 58 of connector B sends a power supply to both potentiometers, pin 26 supplies an earth signal to the potentiometers, while pins 24 and 41 of the same connector receive signals from the throttle body actuator N75 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. Valve L10 , supplied by main relay J10 , is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 5 of connector B of M10 . Variable geometry solenoid L15 is controlled from pin 4 of connector B of control unit M10 . Variable valve timing system N76 controls intake advance mechanically: it is controlled by pin 36 of control unit connector B. Control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit via a line from pin 3 of connector A ( ). See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-test system that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : this receives signals from pin 52 of connector A of control unit M10 through the tester line. The self-test system also produces the signal for the "injection failure" warning light in the instrument E15 , which comes from pin 46 of the control unit M10 . The module E15 receives an ignition-controlled supply (INT) at pin 15 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A ; when this earth signal is received, the "injection failure" warning light comes on. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 44 of connector A of the control unit M10 ( ). See E4021 SPEEDOMETER Control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to engine rpm ( ) from pin 35 of connector A. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 6 and 13 of connector A. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 9, 41, 50 and 62 of connector A control activation of the relevant fan ( ). See E5020 ENGINE COOLING Control unit M10 is connected to the gearbox control unit (SELESPEED) M54 via pins 12 and 29 of connector A ("CAN" lines). ( ) See E7050 AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION

The system is managed by a single control unit that controls the ignition (static and lost spark) and the fuel injection (phased). The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; exhaust with catalytic converter; fuel vapour recirculation. On this version, the engine is fitted with a throttle body controlled electronically by the control unit. Special software inside the control unit computes throttle opening. This system does away with a connection between accelerator and throttle body. For more details, . Characteristic of working principle 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The control unit is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by maxifuse EFI located on the battery (connector B99 C ), at pin 4 of connector B of M10 via the line protected by fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The ignition-operated power supply (15/54) is received on a line protected by the fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A, and energizes the main relay J10 which consequently sends the supply: to pin 2 of connector A of control unit M10 ; to injectors N70 ; to the coils A30 ; to the timing sensor K47 ; to the air flow meter K41 , via the line protected by the fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98 A . to the vapour recovery solenoid L10 , again via the line protected by fuse F3 ; to the heater of the Lambda probes K39 and K40 , again via the line protected by fuse F3 . The earth of the main relay J10 is protected by a jumper diode M11 . The ignition-operated power supply (15/54) also supplies - via fuse F4 of B98 A - the fuel pump relay J15 , which is excited by a control signal (earth) from pin 29 of connector C of control unit M10 . It supplies power to the fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of impact to prevent the danger of fuel flowing out. Pins 3, 7 and 8 of connector A of control unit M10 are earthed and used as references: the first two for the ignition and the third for the injectors. Pin 8 of connector F is also earthed. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. Rpm sensor K46 supplies information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pins 37 and 38 of connector E of control unit M10 . Timing sensor K47 receives a reference earth from pin 39 of connector E of control unit M10 and sends back a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 40 of the same connector. Engine temperature sender unit K36 receives a reference earth from pin 28 of connector E of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the coolant temperature to pin 29 of control unit connector E. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The (first) hot Lambda probe K40 provides control unit M10 with information on the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture in the three cylinders of one head. The signal is sent to pin 32 of control unit connector C, while pin 31 provides an earth signal. Probe K40 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold; the resistor is supplied by the relay J10 and receives the heating signal from pin 5 of connector A of M10 . Similarly, the second Lambda probe K39 provides control unit M10 with information on the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture in the three cylinders of the other head. The signal is sent to pin 33 of control unit connector C, while pin 34 provides a reference earth signal. Probe K39 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold; the resistor is supplied by the relay J10 and receives the heating signal from pin 1 of connector A of M10 . Knock sensors K50 and K51 provide information on knock status via frequency signals sent to pins 42 and 44 respectively of control unit connector E. An earth signal is sent from pins 41 and 43 of connector E of M10 respectively. Air flow meter K41 (supplied by relay J10 ) receives a reference voltage from pin 46 of connector E and sends to pin 47 of the same connector a signal proportional to air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 48 of connector E of M10 , while pin 45 of connector E receives an air temperature signal. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 22 and 23 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 24 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 27 and 26 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 25 of connector C. Pin 14 of connector D of M10 receives the signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 , with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS The injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from main relay J10 . The engine management unit sends commands to the injectors from pins 25, 13, 1, 26, 14 and 2 of the connector, for cylinders 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively. Control unit M10 also controls coils A30 via control signals for the coil primary windings, while the secondary winding sends a pulse to the spark plugs: pins 20, 6, 17, 13, 19 and 5 of connector F control ignition coils 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. The coil A30 main windings receive the go ahead supply for opening from the main relay J10 . Throttle body actuator N75 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: they control throttle opening via a stepper motor. The motor receives information from pins 1 and 2 of connector F of M10 . Pin 33 of connector E sends a power supply to both potentiometers, pin 32 of connector E supplies an earth signal to the potentiometers, while pins 31 and 34 of the same connector receive signals from throttle body actuator N75 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. Valve L10 , supplied by main relay J10 , is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 21 of connector C of M10 . The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a specific serial line from pin 39 of connector C ; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine is not started . See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-test system that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : this receives indirect signals from control unit M10 via a serial line from control unit M20 described above. (pin 39 of connector C). The self-test system also generates the signal for the 'injection failure' warning light in the instrument E15 , which comes from pin 21 of connector F of control unit M10 . The module E15 receives an ignition-controlled supply (INT) at pin 15 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A ; when this earth signal is received, the 'injection failure' warning light comes on. The speedometer signal (car speed) reaches pin 13 of connector D of control unit M10 . See E4021 SPEEDOMETER The control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to the engine rpm from pin 38 of connector C. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 4 and 21 of connector E. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pin 6 of connector A , 3 of connector D and 15, 17 of connector E control activation of the relevant fan . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING Control unit M10 is connected to the automatic transmission control unit M55 from pins 11 and 12 of connector D ('CAN' lines) . See E7050 AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION There is also a supplementary connector R51 for connection to the control unit, located in the engine bay (connected to pin 3 of connector B of M10 ). This connection is used solely at the Production Plant and SHOULD UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES be used during servicing.

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit which controls both the double ignition and the injection. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; exhaust with preconverters and catalytic converter controlled by three Lambda sensors; fuel vapour recirculation. The throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit; special software in the engine management control unit computes throttle opening; this dispenses with the need for a mechanical connection between the accelerator pedal and the throttle body. The control unit also controls the hydraulic variable valve timing, an exclusive device which allows the intake timing to be optimised. This version is also characterized by the adoption of a variable geometry inlet system, managed by the fuel injection control unit in accordance with the engine's operating conditions. Thanks to the electronic management described above, this engine conforms to the latest anti-pollution and continuous control regulations in accordance with the EOBD (European On Board Diagnosis) system; this system allows continuous diagnosis of the car components relating to emissions, and indicates to the user, by switching on the relevant warning light on the instrument panel, any deterioration in these components. For more details Characteristic of working principle 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other fuses, located alongside in the additional fusebox.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The system is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by the maxifuse EFI located on the battery, connector B99 C . The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) arrives from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 15 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The supply controlled by the ignition reaches pin 47 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A. Main injection relay J10 controls the entire system: this is excited by a control signal (earth) received from pin 31 of connector A of control unit M10 and then sends power: to pins 16, 32 and 48 of connector A of the control unit, through the line protected by fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98 A . the air flow meter K41 , fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 , variable geometry control solenoid L15 , variable valve timing actuator N76 and Lambda probes K15 , K15 and K17 ; (all these lines are protected by fuse F2 of B98 A ). to the injectors N70 and the coils A30 , via the line protected by fuse F3 , located in unit B98A . The fuel pump relay J15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition via fuse F4 , of the additional fuse box B98 A . It is energized by a control signal (earth) from pin 30 of connector A of control unit M10 and supplies power to fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of a crash and so prevents the dangerous spilling of fuel. On the control unit, the earth point C40 C is located, which connects to the engine earth C40 A . The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine operating conditions. Rpm sensor K46 provides information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pins 10 and 59 of connector B of control unit M10 . These two signals are very low intensity and are therefore shielded. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 51 of connector B of control unit M10 , receives a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B and sends a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing to pin 42 of control unit connector B. Engine temperature sender unit K36 riceives a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the coolant temperature to pin 25 of control unit connector B. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The three Lambda probes K15, K16 and K17 provide the control unit M10 information concerning the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture in three different positions of the exhaust: two are upstream of the precatalyzers, the third is upstream of the main catalyzer. The probe K15 , on the right precatalyzer, sends a signal to pin 23 of connector B of M10 , while pin 55 supplies the reference earth. Probe K15 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. The resistor is supplied by the main relay and receives an earth signal from pin 34 of connector B of control unit M10 . The probe K16 , on the left precatalyzer, sends the signal to pin 39 of connector B of M10 , while pin 7 supplies the reference earth. The probe K16 is heated with a resistor, supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 2 of connector B of control unit M10 . The probe K17 downstream of the main catalyzer sends the signal to pin 28 of connector B of M10 , while pin 60 supplies the reference earth. The probe K17 is heated with a resistor, supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 50 of connector B of control unit M10 . Knock sensor K50 provides information on knock status via a frequency signal sent to pin 22 of connector B of control unit M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 54 of connector B. The signals are very low intensity and are therefore shielded. Air flow meter K41 (supplied by the relay J10 ) receives a reference voltage from pin 63 of connector A of the control unit, and sends to pin 57 of connector A a signal proportional to the air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 25 of connector A of M10 , while an air temperature signal is received by pin 54 of connector A. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 56 and 24 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 8 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 7 and 25 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 40 of connector A. Pin 27 of connector A of M10 receives the 'pedal pressed' signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 , with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . Pin 26 of connector A of M10 receives the 'pedal pressed' signal coming from the other contact of the brake lights switch l30 , with the supply controlled by the igntion (15/54) from fuse F6 of the additional fusebox B98 A . Pin 59 of connector A of M10 receives the signal coming from the clutch switch I31 (manual gearbox versions only). The control unit M10 dialogues with the ABS control unit M50 via the CAN line - pins 12 and 29, of connector A: the latter signals any irregularities on the ground, distinguished via the speed sensors installed on the individual wheels. In this way, the engine management control unit can distinguish between variations in driving torque due to irregularities in the road surface and those due to misfiring in the combustion chambers. Via this CAN line, the control unit M10 also receives the speedometer signal (vehicle speed). Control unit M10 controls the opening of individual injectors N70, via duty cycle signals produced by pins 19 (cyl. 1), 52 (cyl. 2), 35 (cyl. 3) and 3 (cyl. 4) of connector B of M10 . The control unit M10 also controls the coils A30 by means of (earth) signals for the coil primary windings, whilst the secondary winding sends a pulse to the spark plugs: from pins 16, 31, 30 and 14 of connector B of M10 for cylinders 1,2, 3 and 4 respectively. Throttle body actuator N75 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: they control throttle opening via a stepper motor. The motor receives information from pins 17 - 49 and 1 - 33 of connector B of M10 . Pin 58 of connector B sends a power supply to both potentiometers, pin 26 supplies an earth signal to the potentiometers, while pins 24 and 41 of the same connector receive signals from the throttle body actuator N75 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. Valve L10 is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 5 of connector B of M10 . Variable geometry solenoid L15 is controlled from pin 4 of connector B of control unit M10 . Variable valve timing system N76 controls intake advance mechanically; it is controlled by pin 36 of control unit connector B. The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit via a line from pin 3 of connector A . See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic system that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : this receives signals from pin 53 of connector A from control unit M10 through the tester line. The self-test system also produces the signal for the 'EOBD' warning light in the instrument E15 , which comes from pin 46 of connector A of the control unit M10 . Control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to engine rpm from pin 35 of connector A. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT The minimum engine temperature signal is sent from 19 of connector A to the auxiliary instrument E20 ; pin 22 receives, from E20 , a 'fuel reserve' signal . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 6 and 13 of connector A. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 9, 41, 50 and 62 of connector A control activation of the relevant fan . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING Functional description Control unit M10 is connected to the gearbox control unit (SELESPEED) M54 via pins 12 and 29 of connector A via the CAN line . See E7050 AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
