Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit which controls both the double ignition and the injection. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; exhaust with preconverters and catalytic converter controlled by three Lambda sensors; fuel vapour recirculation. The throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit; special software in the engine management control unit computes throttle opening; this dispenses with the need for a mechanical connection between the accelerator pedal and the throttle body. The control unit also controls the hydraulic variable valve timing, an exclusive device which allows the intake timing to be optimised. This version is also characterized by the adoption of a variable geometry inlet system, managed by the fuel injection control unit in accordance with the engine's operating conditions. Thanks to the electronic management described above, this engine conforms to the latest anti-pollution and continuous control regulations in accordance with the EOBD (European On Board Diagnosis) system; this system allows continuous diagnosis of the car components relating to emissions, and indicates to the user, by switching on the relevant warning light on the instrument panel, any deterioration in these components. For more details Characteristic of working principle 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other fuses, located alongside in the additional fusebox.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The system is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by the maxifuse EFI located on the battery, connector B99 C . The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) arrives from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 15 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The supply controlled by the ignition reaches pin 47 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . Main injection relay J10 controls the entire system: this is excited by a control signal (earth) from pin 31 of connector A of control unit M10 and then sends a power supply to pins 16, 32 and 48 of connector A of the control unit via a line protected by fuse F3 of supplementary fuse box B98 A. to air flow meter K41, fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10, variable geometry contol solenoid L15, variable valve timing actuator N76 and lambda sensors K15, K16 and K17; (all these lines are protected by fuse F2 of B98 A ). to the injectors N70 and the coils A30 , via the line protected by fuse F3 , located in the unit B98 A . the fuel pump relay J15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition via fuse F4 , of the additional fuse box B98 A . It is energized by a control signal (earth) from pin 30 of connector A of control unit M10 and supplies power to fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of a crash and so prevents the dangerous spilling of fuel. On the control unit, the earth point C40 C is located, which connects to the engine earth C40 A . The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. Rpm sensor K46 provides information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pins 10 and 59 of connector B of control unit M10 . These two signals are very low intensity and are therefore shielded. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 51 of connector B of control unit M10 , receives a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B and sends a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing to pin 42 of control unit connector B. Engine temperature sender unit K36 riceives a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the coolant temperature to pin 25 of control unit connector B. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The three Lambda probes K15, K16 and K17 provide the control unit M10 information concerning the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture in three different positions of the exhaust: two are upstream of the precatalyzers, the third is upstream of the main catalyzer. The probe K15 , on the right precatalyzer, sends a signal to pin 23 of connector B of M10 , while pin 55 supplies the reference earth. Probe K15 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. The resistor is supplied by the main relay and receives an earth signal from pin 34 of connector B of control unit M10 . The probe K16 , on the left precatalyzer, sends the signal to pin 39 of connector B of M10 , while pin 7 supplies the reference earth. The probe K16 is heated with a resistor, supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 2 of connector B of control unit M10 . The probe K17 downstream of the main catalyzer sends the signal to pin 28 of connector B of M10 , while pin 60 supplies the reference earth. The probe K17 is heated with a resistor, supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 50 of connector B of control unit M10 . Knock sensor K50 provides information on knock status via a frequency signal sent to pin 22 of connector B of control unit M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 54 of connector B. The signals are very low intensity and are therefore shielded. Air flow meter K41 (supplied by the relay J10 ) receives a reference voltage from pin 63 of connector A of the control unit, and sends to pin 57 of connector A a signal proportional to the air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 25 of connector A of M10 , while an air temperature signal is received by pin 54 of connector A. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 56 and 24 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 8 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 7 and 25 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 40 of connector A. Pin 27 of connector A of M10 receives the 'pedal pressed' signal coming from the brake lights switch I30, with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 or, depending on the version, from fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B. Pin 59 of connector A of M10 receives the signal coming from the clutch switch I31. The control unit M10 converses with the ABS control unit M50 via the CAN line - pins 12 and 29 of connector A: the latter, on versions with VDC, signals any irregularities on the ground, distinguished via the speed sensors installed on the individual wheels via steering sensor K58 to ABS control unit M50. In this way the engine management control unit can distinguish between variations in engine torque due to irregularities on the road surface and those due to misfire in the combustion chambers. Via this CAN line, the control unit M10 also receives the speedometer signal (vehicle speed). Control unit M10 controls the opening of individual injectors N70, via duty cycle signals produced by pins 19 (cyl. 1), 52 (cyl. 2), 35 (cyl. 3) and 3 (cyl. 4) of connector B of M10 . The control unit M10 also controls the coils A30 by means of (earth) signals for the coil primary windings, whilst the secondary winding sends a pulse to the spark plugs: from pins 16, 31, 30 and 14 of connector B of M10 for cylinders 1,2, 3 and 4 respectively. Throttle body actuator N75 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: they control throttle opening via a stepper motor. The motor receives information from pins 17 - 49 and 1 - 33 of connector B of M10 . Pin 58 of connector B sends a power supply to both potentiometers, pin 26 supplies an earth signal to the potentiometers, while pins 24 and 41 of the same connector receive signals from the throttle body actuator N75 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. Valve L10 is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 5 of connector B of M10 . Variable geometry solenoid L15 is controlled from pin 4 of connector B of control unit M10 . Variable valve timing system N76 controls intake advance mechanically; it is controlled by pin 36 of control unit connector B. The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit via a line from pin 3 of connector A . See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic system that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : this receives signals from pin 53 of connector A from control unit M10 through the tester line. The self-test system also produces the signal for the 'EOBD' warning light in the instrument Control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to engine rpm from pin 35 of connector A. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT The minimum engine temperature signal is sent from pin 34 of connector A to the auxiliary instrument pin 22 receives, from E20, a 'fuel consumption' signal . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() A speedometer signal is sent to instrument E10 from pin 52 of connector A . See E4021 SPEEDOMETER Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 6 and 13 of connector A. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 9, 41, 50 and 62 of connector A control activation of the relevant fan . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

Description The 2.0 JTS engine fuel system is fitted with a high pressure pump for direct injection. An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single Bosch Motronic MED7.1.1 control unit with motorised throttle which controls both the ignition and the injection (sequential phased type). The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; control of high-pressure fuel pump; air supply: accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; exhaust with catalytic converters controlled by four lambda sensors; fuel vapour recirculation. The control unit of this JTS engine manages high pressure fuel pump operation by controlling an electric pressure regulator and pressure sensor. The throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit; special software in the engine management control unit computes throttle opening; this dispenses with the need for a mechanical connection between the accelerator pedal and the throttle body. The control unit also controls the hydraulic variable valve timing, an exclusive device which allows the intake timing to be optimised. The variable geometry intake system is also managed by the injection system on the basis of engine service conditions. Thanks to a specific sensor, the control unit also detects drops in the brake servo vacuum, and intervenes by reducing the load as appropriate so as to restore more efficient braking. Thanks to the electronic management described above, this engine conforms to the latest anti-pollution and continuous control regulations in accordance with the EOBD (European On Board Diagnosis) system. For more details . Characteristic of working principle 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other fuses, located alongside in the additional fusebox.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The system is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by the maxifuse EFI located on the battery, connector B99 C . The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) arrives from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 70 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The supply controlled by the ignition reaches pin 67 of connector A, via a line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 A . The main injection relay J10 controls the entire system: this is excited by a control signal (earth) received from pin 25 of connector A of control unit M10 and then sends power: to pins 3, 5 and 6 of control unit connector A; the air flow meter K41 , fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 , variable geometry control solenoid L15 , variable valve timing actuator N76 and Lambda sensors K15 , K16 K17 and K18 ; (all these lines are protected by fuse F2 of B98 A ). to the coils A30 , via the line protected by fuse F3 of B98 A ; to high pressure pump N77 , again via the line protected by fuse F3 of B98 A . the fuel pump relay J15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition via fuse F4 , of the additional fuse box B98 A . It is energized by a control signal (earth) from pin 28 of connector A of control unit M10 and supplies power to fuel pump N40 , which is earthed through the inertia switch I50 , which cuts off the circuit in the case of a crash and so prevents the dangerous spilling of fuel. Pins 1, 2 and 4 of connector A of M10 are earthed. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. Rpm sensor K46 supplies information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pins 40 and 55 of connector B of control unit M10 . Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 26 of connector B of control unit M10 , receives a reference earth from pin 21 of connector B and sends a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing to pin 41 of control unit connector B. Fuel pressure sensor K83 is supplied from pin 26 of connector B of control unit M10 , receives a reference earth from pin 21 of connector B and sends a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing to pin 24 of control unit connector B. Engine temperature sender unit K36 riceives a reference earth from pin 57 of connector B of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the coolant temperature to pin 9 of control unit connector B. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The four Lambda probes K15, K16, K17 and K18 provide the control unit M10 information concerning the correct composition of the air-fuel mixture in four different positions of the exhaust: two (linear) are upstream of the precatalyzers, and two (planar) are downstream of the catalyzers. Linear sensor K15 sends signals to pins 53, 52 and 74 of connector A of M10 , while pin 75 supplies the reference earth. Probe K15 is heated by a resistor in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. The coil is supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 73 of connector A of control unit M10 . Linear sensor K16 sends signals to pins 79, 58 and 80 of connector A of M10 , while pin 57 supplies the reference earth. Sensor K16 is heated by a heating coil in order to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. The coil is supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 29 of connector A of control unit M10 . Planar sensor K17 sends a signal to pin 77 of connector A of M10 , while pin 76 supplies the reference earth. The sensor K17 is heated by a heating coil supplied by the main relay and receives an earth signal from pin 49 of connector A of control unit M10 . Planar sensor K18 sends a signal to pin 55 of connector A of M10 , while pin 56 supplies the reference earth. Sensor K18 is heated with a heating coil, supplied by the main relay, and receives an earth signal from pin 94 of connector A of control unit M10 . The knock sensor K50 makes it possible, through a frequency signal sent to pin 44 of connector B of control unit M10 to have information concerning knock conditions: it receives a reference earth from pin 59 of connector B. Air flow meter K41 (supplied by the relay J10 ) receives a reference voltage from pin 17 of connector A of the control unit, and sends to pin 10 of connector A a signal proportional to the air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 16 of connector A of M10 , while an air temperature signal is received by pin 10 of connector A. The brake servo vacuum sensor K105 intervenes by reducing the load as appropriate so as to restore more efficient braking: the sensor is supplied from pin 26 of connector B of control unit M10 , it receives a reference earth from pin 21 of connector B and sends a signal of frequency corresponding to the vacuum to pin 42 of control unit connector B. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The former receives power and earth from pins 83 and 59 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 61 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 81 and 82 respectively of connector A of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 60 of the same connector. Pin 27 of connector A of M10 receives the 'pedal pressed' signal coming from the brake lights switch I30, with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 or, depending on the version, from fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98 B; it receives a pedal released signal from I30 at pin 20 of connector A. Pin 23 of connector A of M10 receives the signal coming from the clutch switch I31 . The control unit M10 dialogues with the ABS control unit M50 via the CAN line - pins 64 and 86 of connector A: this line, on versions with VDC, passes through steering sensor K58 to reach ABS control unit M50: the latter signals any irregularities on the ground, distinguished via the speed sensors installed on the individual wheels. In this way the engine management control unit can distinguish between variations in engine torque due to irregularities on the road surface and those due to misfire in the combustion chambers. Control unit M10 controls the opening of individual injectors N70, via appropriate signals produced by pins 1 and 33 (cyl. 1), 16 and 46 (cyl. 2), 31 and 18 (cyl. 3) and 48 and 2 (cyl. 4) of connector B of M10 . Fuel pressure regulator N77 is controlled by control unit M10 from pin 5 of connector B. The control unit M10 also controls the coils A30 by means of (earth) signals for the coil primary windings, whilst the secondary winding sends a pulse to the spark plugs: from pins 54, 37, 39 and 38 of connector B of M10 for cylinders 1,2, 3 and 4 respectively. Throttle body actuator N75 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: they control throttle opening via a stepper motor. The motor receives information from pins 15 and 30 of connector B of M10 . Pin 14 of connector B sends a power supply to both potentiometers, pin 29 supplies an earth signal to the potentiometers, while pins 13 and 28 of the same connector receive signals from the throttle body actuator N75 . Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows fuel vapours to pass through to the engine intake where they join the mixture entering the combustion chamber. Valve L10 is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load via a duty-cycle signal from pin 60 of connector B of M10 . Variable geometry solenoid L15 is controlled from pin 6 of connector B of control unit M10 . Variable valve timing system N76 controls intake advance mechanically; it is controlled by pin 36 of control unit connector B. The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit via a line from pin 72 of connector A . See E7010 CODE The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic system that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : this receives signals from pin 87 of connector A from control unit M10 through the tester line. The self-test system also produces the signal for the 'EOBD' warning light in the instrument E10 , which comes from pin 89 of the control unit M10 . Control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to engine rpm from pin 66 of connector A. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT The minimum engine temperature signal is sent from pin 71 of connector A to the auxiliary instrument E20 ; pin 8 receives, from E20, a 'fuel consumption' signal . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() A speedometer signal is sent to instrument E10 from pin 68 of connector A. See E4021 SPEEDOMETER Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pins 7 and 40 of connector A. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 45, 24, 69 and 93 of connector A of M10 to control the activation of the relevant fan . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING Cruise control management signals leave from pins 41, 43, 44, 21 and 91 of connector A of M10. See E5060 CRUISE CONTROL

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The Diesel engine is fitted with a COMMON RAIL UNIJET injection system. This uses high injection pressure controlled electronically. Fuel delivery, termed a pilot injection, is optimised by the electronic control unit via the injector and not managed by the pump. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: glow plug preheating; accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; fuel preheating. For more details, . Characteristic of working principle 1060 DIESEL FUEL INJECTION The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other jumper fuses located next to the junction unit. The heater plugs are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the battery.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic injection system. Engine control unit M10 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) at pin 13 of connector B from the line protected by fuse B25 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. The relay J10 controls the system supply: it is supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99, while the coil is supplied by the line protected by fuse B35 up to 2/99 or fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. Pin 46 of connector C of control unit M10 sends an enablement signal which energizes the relay J10 and sends a supply to the control unit, to pins 7, 8 and 1 of connector A (the line which from J10 goes to pin 1 is also protected by fuse B41 up to 2/99 or fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99). The relay J15 is also supplied by the battery from the line of maxifuse EFI of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99; pins 30 and 52 of connector C of control unit M10 send the signals which energize the relay J15 , which provides the supply to the fuel pump N40 , which is connected to earth via the inertia switch l50 . In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. From 2/99: a signal arrives from pin 52 of connector C of the control unit M10 which energizes the relay J15, which provides the supply for the electric fuel pump N40 which is earthed via the inertia switch I50 . In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. The diesel preheating relay J17 is supplied by the battery via the line protected by fuses B37 and B39 up to 2/99, or the GLOW maxifuse of B99 and the fuse F2 of the additional fusebox B98A from 2/99.; it receives an ignition-controlled supply (15/54) from the fuse B25 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99, and controls the operation of the diesel heating resistor O20 : the thermal contact (connector A of O20 ) deactivates the system when heating has taken place. Control unit M15 , responsible for controlling preheating of heater plugs A40 , is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by fuse B37 up to 2/99 or the GLOW maxifuse of B99 from 2/99. It receives controls from pins 38 and 51 of connector C of M10 and sends a feedback signal to pin 1 of connector B of the control unit. Pins 4, 5 and 6 of connector A of M10 are earthed. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. Rpm sensor K46 supplies information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pin 26 of connector D of control unit M10 . It receives an earth signal from pin 37 of control unit connector D. Both signals are weak and are therefore shielded. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 12 of connector D of control unit M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 2 of connector D of control unit M10 and sends it a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing of pin 3 of the same connector. Functional description Engine temperature sender unit K45 receives a reference earth from pin 27 of connector D of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to coolant temperature to pin 36 of the same connector. Functional description Engine temperature sender unit K36 receives a reference earth from pin 27 of connector D of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to coolant temperature to pin 36 of the same connector. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Functional description Air flow meter K41 receives a general power supply from pin 11 of control unit connector D and a reference voltage from pin 1. It sends pin 14 of connector D a signal proportional to air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 4 of connector D of M10 , while an air temperature signal is received by pin 23 of connector A. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 5 and 23 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 10 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 21 and 8 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 9 of connector C. Fuel temperature sensor K81 fitted on the return manifold measures the temperature of diesel leaving the injectors. It receives a reference earth from pin 1 of connector C of M10 and sends a fuel temperature signal to control unit pin 24. The turbocharging sensor K82 records turbo pressure. It is supplied from pin 8 of connector D of M10 and receives a reference earth from control unit pin 7. The signal is sent to pin 6 of control unit connector D. The fuel pressure sensor K83 is responsible for providing the injection control unit with a feedback signal for governing pressure and injection duration. It receives power and the reference earth from pins 13 and 34 respectively of connector D of M10 ; it then sends the pressure signal to pin 24 of the same connector. The fuel pressure regulator N77 has the task of keeping the value of the fuel pressure in the accumulator constant. Both control signals are produced by pins 31 and 21 of control unit connector D. The EGR solenoid L30 controls exhaust gas recirculation. It is supplied from pin 37 of connector C of M10 and sends a signal to control unit pin 50. Pin 8 of connector C of M10 receives a signal from brake light switch I30 , ignition-operated (INT) through a line protected by fuse F1 in junction unit B1 . Pin 2 of connector C of M10 receives a signal from the clutch pedal switch I31 , also ignition operated (INT) by fuse F1 of junction unit B1 . The injectors N70 receive the opening go ahead supply from pins 2 (cylinders 1 and 4) and 4 (cylinders 2 and 3) for connector E of M10 . The engine control unit sends commands to the injectors from pins 9, 7, 5 and 3 of connector E for cylinders 1, 2, 3 and 4, respectively. The rev counter module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99: when the earth signal reaches pin 48 of connector C, the 'injection failure' warning light comes on. The speedometer module E10 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99: when the earth signal reaches pin 43 of connector C, the 'heater plugs' warning light comes on. The coolant temperature signal is sent to the auxiliary instrument from pin 49 of connector C of M10 . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a line from pin 13 of connector C; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine is not started. The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic unit that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 via pin 28 of connector C. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 26 of connector C of the control unit M10 . See E4021 SPEEDOMETER Control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to engine rpm from pin 40 of connector C. See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pin 32 of connector D and pin 3 of connector B. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pin 23 of connector B, pin 15 of connector D and 20, 45 of connector C control activation of the relevant fans . Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The Diesel engine is fitted with a COMMON RAIL UNIJET injection system. This uses high injection pressure controlled electronically. Fuel delivery, termed a pilot injection, is optimised by the electronic control unit via the injector and not managed by the pump. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: glow plug preheating; accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; fuel preheating. For more details, . Characteristic of working principle 1060 DIESEL FUEL INJECTION The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and other jumper fuses located next to the junction unit. The heater plugs are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the battery.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic injection system. Engine control unit M10 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) at pin 13 of connector B from the line protected by fuse B25 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. The relay J10 controls the system supply: it is supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99, while the coil is supplied by the line protected by fuse B35 up to 2/99 or fuse F5 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99. Pin 46 of connector C of control unit M10 sends an enablement signal which energizes the relay J10 and sends a supply to the control unit, to pins 7, 8 and 1 of connector A (the line which goes from J10 goes to pin 1 is also protected by fuse B41 up to 2/99 or fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99). The relay J15 is also supplied by the battery from the line of maxifuse EFI of B5 up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99; up to 2/99: pins 30 and 52 of connector C of control unit M10 send the signals which energize the relay J15 , which provides the supply to the fuel pump N40 , which is connected to earth via the inertia switch l50. In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. from 2/99: a signal arrives from pin 52 of connector C of the control unit M10 which energizes the relay J15, which provides the supply for the electric fuel pump N40 which is earthed via the inertia switch I50 . In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. The diesel pre-heating relay J17 is supplied by the battery via the lline protected by fuses B37 and B39 up to 2/99 or the GLOW maxifuse of B99 and fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99.; it receives an ignition-controlled supply (15/54) from the fuse B25 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A from 2/99, and controls the operation of the diesel heating resistor O20 : the thermal contact (connector A of O20 ) deactivates the system when heating has taken place. Control unit M15 , responsible for controlling preheating of heater plugs A40 , is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by fuse B37 up to 2/99 or the GLOW maxifuse of B99 from 2/99. It receives controls from pins 38 and 51 of connector C of M10 and sends a feedback signal to pin 1 of connector B of the control unit. Pins 4, 5 and 6 of connector A of M10 are earthed. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. Rpm sensor K46 supplies information on engine speed via a frequency signal sent to pin 26 of connector D of control unit M10 . It receives an earth signal from pin 37 of control unit connector D. Both signals are weak and are therefore shielded. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 12 of connector D of control unit M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 2 of connector D of control unit M10 and sends it a signal of frequency corresponding to the timing of pin 3 of the same connector. Functional description Engine temperature sender unit K45 receives a reference earth from pin 27 of connector D of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to coolant temperature to pin 36 of the same connector. Functional description Engine temperature sender unit K36 receives a reference earth from pin 27 of connector D of control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to coolant temperature to pin 36 of the same connector. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Functional description Air flow meter K41 receives a general power supply from pin 11 of control unit connector D and a reference voltage from pin 1. It sends pin 14 of connector D a signal proportional to air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor: the sensor reference earth is supplied by pin 4 of connector D of M10 , while an air temperature signal is received by pin 23. Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 5 and 23 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 10 of the same connector. The second receives power and earth from pins 21 and 8 respectively of connector C of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 9 of connector C. Fuel temperature sensor K81 fitted on the return manifold measures the temperature of diesel leaving the injectors. It receives a reference earth from pin 1 of connector C of M10 and sends a fuel temperature signal to pin 24. The turbocharging sensor K82 records turbo pressure. It is supplied from pin 8 of connector D of M10 and receives a reference earth from control unit pin 7. The signal is sent to pin 6 of control unit connector D. The fuel pressure sensor K83 is responsible for providing the injection control unit with a feedback signal for governing pressure and injection duration. It receives power and a reference earth from pins 13 and 14 respectively of connector D of M10 ; it then sends the pressure signal to pin 24 of the same connector. The fuel pressure regulator N77 has the task of keeping the value of the fuel pressure in the accumulator constant. Both control signals are produced by pins 31 and 21 of control unit connector D. The EGR solenoid L30 controls exhaust gas recirculation. It is supplied from pin 37 of connector C of M10 and sends a signal to control unit pin 50. Pin 8 of connector C of M10 receives a signal from brake light switch I30 , ignition-operated (INT) through a line protected by fuse F1 in junction unit B1 . Pin 2 of connector C of M10 receives a signal from the clutch pedal switch I31 , also ignition operated (INT) by fuse F1 of junction unit B1 . The injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from pins 1 (cylinders 1, 3 and 4) and 4 (cylinders 2 and 5) of connector E of M10 . The engine management unit sends commands to the injectors from pins 5, 9, 8, 7 and 3 of connector E, for cylinders 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 respectively. The rev counter module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99: when the earth signal reaches pin 48 of connector C, the 'injection failure' warning light comes on. The speedometer module E10 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99: when the earth signal reaches pin 43 of connector C, the 'heater plugs' warning light comes on. The coolant temperature signal is sent to the auxiliary instrument from pin 49 of connector C of M10 . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a line from pin 13 of connector C; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine is not started. The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic unit that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 via pin 28 of connector C. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 26 of connector C of the control unit M10 . See E4021 SPEEDOMETER Control unit M10 sends out a signal proportional to engine rpm from pin 40 of connector C.). See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT Control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system via pin 32 of connector D and pin 3 of connector B. This allows engine idling speed to be adjusted to increased engine load whenever the compressor is activated, or to turn off the compressor in the case of high speeds or high engine loads . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pin 23 of connector B, pin 15 of connector D and 20, 45 of connector C control activation of the relevant fans . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

The Diesel engine is fitted with a COMMON RAIL UNIJET injection system. - This uses high injection pressure controlled electronically. Fuel delivery, termed a pilot injection, is optimised by the electronic control unit via the injector and not managed by the pump. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: glow plug preheating; accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; fuel preheating. For more details, . Characteristic of working principle 1060 DIESEL FUEL INJECTION The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic injection system. The supply for the engine control unit M10 is controlled by the ignition (15/54) at pin 58 by the line protected by fuse F21 of the additional fuse box B98A . The relay J10 controls the system supply: it is supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B99 ; pin 13 of control unit M10 sends the enablement signal which excites relay J10 and sends power to the control unit, directly to pin 5 and, via the line of fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98A , to pin 4. The relay J15 is also supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B99 ; pin 24 of control unit M10 sends the signal which energize the relay J15 , which provides the supply to the fuel pump N40 , which is connected to earth through the inertia switch I50 . In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. Pins 1, 2 and 3 of M10 are earthed. The diesel preheating relay J17 is supplied by the battery via the line protected by the GLOW maxifuse of B99 or fuse B39 , and controls the operation of the diesel heating resistor 020 ; a signal from the control unit M10 (from pin 111) deactives the system after heating has taken place. Control unit M15 , responsible for controlling preheating of heater plugs A40 , is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by the GLOW maxifuse of B99 . It is supplied - connector C - from the line of fuse F2 of the additional fusebox B98A , and exchanges the command and control signals with pins 22 and 62 of M10 which controls the time lag. Connector B is connected to the heater plugs A40. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. The rpm sensor K46 provides information concerning the engine speed through a frequency signal sent to pin 100 of the control unit M10 . It receives an earth signal from pin 99 of the control unit. Both signals are weak and are therefore suitably shielded by pin 101. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 102 of M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 104 of control unit M10 and sends it a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 103. The engine temperature sensor K36 , receives a reference earth from pin 85 of the control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant to pin 84. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() Air flow meter K41 receives a general power supply from the line of fuse F2 of the additional fusebox B98A ; it receives a reference voltage from pin 88 of M10 . It is supplied by the control unit from pin 97 of M10 , and sends a signal proportional to the air flow to pin 89. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor which sends an air temperature signal to pin 86 of M10 . Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 78 and 76 respectively of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 77. The second receives power and earth from pins 81 and 79 respectively of M10 and sends the signal to pin 80. Fuel temperature sensor K81 fitted on the return manifold measures the temperature of diesel leaving the injectors. It receives a reference earth from pin 83 of M10 and sends a fuel temperature signal to control unit pin 82. The turbocharging sensor K82 records turbo pressure. It is supplied from pin 93 of M10 and receives a reference earth from pin 95. The signal is sent to pin 94 of the control unit. The fuel pressure sensor K83 is responsible for providing the injection control unit with a feedback signal for governing injection pressure and duration. It receives the power and reference earth from pins 90 and 92 respectively of M10 ; it then sends the pressure signal to pin 91. The fuel pressure regulator N77 has the task of keeping the value of the fuel pressure in the accumulator constant. The two control signals come from pins 108 and 109 of the control unit M10 . The EGR solenoid L30 controls exhaust gas recirculation. It is supplied by the line of fuse F2 of the additional fusebox B98A and is controlled by a signal from pin 16 of M10 . The turbine variable geometry control solenoid L36 regulates the turbine's operation in accordance with engine load: it is supplied by the line of fuse F2 of the additional fusebox B98A and is controlled by a signal from pin 17 of M10 . The solenoid on the throttle body L62 chokes and closes the butterfly, for example when the engine is turned off; it is supplied by the line of fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A and is controlled by a signal of pin 15 of M10 . Pin 59 of M10 receives the signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 , with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS Pin 62 of M10 receives an earth signal coming from the clutch pedal switch l31 . The injectors N70 receive the opening go ahead supply from pins 117 (cylinders 1 and 2) and 118 (cylinders 3 and 4) of M10 . The engine control unit sends commands to the injectors N70 from pins 119, 120, 121 and 114 for cylinders 1, 2, 3 and 4, respectively. The rev counter module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B ; when the earth signal reaches pin 21 of M10 , the 'injection failure' warning light comes on. The speedometer module E10 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B : when the earth signal reaches pin 14 of M10 , the 'heater plugs' warning light comes on. The coolant temperature signal is sent to the auxiliary instrument from pin 110 of M10 . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a specific serial line from pin 11; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine is not started. The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic unit that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 via pin 28. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 49 of control unit M10 . See E4021 SPEEDOMETER The control unit M10 sends a signal from pin 47 proportional to the engine speed . See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT The control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system through pins 18 and 60. This makes it possible to adjust the engine idle speed as the load increases each time the compressor is switched on or to switch off the compressor in the case of high engine speed or load conditions . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 19, 20 51 and 52 control the engagement of the relevant fans . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The Diesel engine is fitted with a COMMON RAIL UNIJET injection system. - This uses high injection pressure controlled electronically. Fuel delivery, termed a pilot injection, is optimised by the electronic control unit via the injector and not managed by the pump. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply: glow plug preheating; accelerator pedal; engine cooling system; fuel preheating. For more details, . Characteristic of working principle 1060 DIESEL FUEL INJECTION The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and by other jumper fuses, located in the additional fuse box. The heater plugs are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the battery.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic injection system. The supply for the engine control unit M10 is controlled by the ignition (15/54) at pin 58 by the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A . The relay J10 controls the system supply: it is supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B99 ; pin 13 of the control unit M10 sends the enablement signal which excites relay J10 and sends power to the control unit, directly to pin 5 and, fia the line of fuse F3 of the additional fuse box B98A , to pin 4. The relay J15 is also supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B99 ; pin 24 of control unit M10 sends the signals which energize the relay J15 , which provides the supply to the fuel pump N40 , which is connected to earth through the inertia switch I50 . In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. Pins 1, 2 and 3 of M10 are earthed. The diesel preheating relay J17 is supplied by the battery via th eline protected by the GLOW maxifuse of B99 or fuse B39 , and controls the operation of the diesel heating resistor O20 ; a signal of the control unit M10 (from pin 111) deactivates the system once heating has taken place. Control unit M15 , responsible for controlling preheating of heater plugs A40 , is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by the GLOW maxifuse of B99 . It is supplied - connector C - by the line of fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A , and exchanges the command and control signals with pins 22 and 62 of M10 which controls the time lag. Connector B is connected to the heater plugs A40. The engine control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service conditions. The rpm sensor K46 provides information concerning the engine speed through a frequency signal sent to pin 100 of the control unit M10 . It receives an earth signal from pin 99 of the control unit. Both signals are weak and are therefore suitably shielded by pin 101. Timing sensor K47 is supplied from pin 102 of control unit M10 . It receives a reference earth from pin 104 of control unit M10 and sends it a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 103. The engine temperature sensor K36 , receives a reference earth from pin 85 of the control unit M10 and supplies a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant to pin 84. The same sender unit also supplies information to the temperature gauge and warning light . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The air flow meter K41 receives a general power supply from the line of fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A ; it receives a reference voltage from pin 88 of M10 . It is supplied by the control unit from pin 97 of M10 , and sends to pin 89 a signal proportional to the air flow. K41 also contains an air temperature sensor which sends an air temperature signal to pin 86 of M10 . Accelerator pedal K55 is fitted with two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety back-up). The first receives power and earth from pins 78 and 76 respectively of M10 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 77. The second receives power and earth from pins 81 and 79 respectively of M10 and sends a signal to pin 80. Fuel temperature sensor K81 fitted on the return manifold measures the temperature of diesel leaving the injectors. It receives a reference earth from pin 83 of M10 and sends a fuel temperature signal to control unit pin 82. The turbocharging sensor K82 records turbo pressure. It is supplied by pin 93 of M10 and receives a reference earth from pin 95. The signal is sent to pin 94 of the control unit. The fuel pressure sensor K83 is responsible for providing the injection control unit with a feedback signal for governing pressure and injection duration. It receives the power and reference earth from pins 90 and 92 of M10 ; it then sends the pressure signal to pin 91. The fuel pressure regulator N77 has the task of keeping the value of the fuel pressure in the accumulator constant. The two control signals come from pins 108 and 109 of the control unit M10 . The EGR solenoid L30 controls exhaust gas recirculation. It is supplied from the line of fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A and is controlled by a signal of pin 16 of M10 . The turbine variable geometry control solenoid L36 governs the operation of the turbine in accordance with engine load; it is supplied by the line of fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A and is controlled by a signal from pin 17 of M10 . The solenoid on the throttle body L62 chokes and closes the butterfly, for example when the engine is turned off; it is supplied by the line of fuse F2 of the additional fuse box B98A and is controlled by a signal of pin 15 of M10 . Pin 59 of M10 receives the signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 , with the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS Pin 62 of M10 receives an earth signal coming from the clutch pedal switch l31 . The injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from pins 117 and 118 of M10 . The engine management control unit sends commands to the injectors N70 from pins 119, 120, 121, 114 and 115 respectively for cylinders 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. The rev counter module E15 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B ; when the earth signal arrives from pin 21 of M10 , the 'injection failure' warning light comes on. The speedometer module E10 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B ; when the earth signal arrives from pin 14 of M10 , the 'heater plugs' warning light comes on. The coolant temperature signal is sent to the auxiliary instrument from pin 110 of M10 . See E4023 DASHBOARD CENTRE AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT() The control unit M10 is connected to the ALFA ROMEO CODE control unit M20 via a specific line from pin 11; in this way if the ALFA ROMEO CODE unit does not detect a correct code, it does not issue enablement and the engine is not started. The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic unit that may be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 via pin 48. The speedometer signal (vehicle speed) reaches pin 49 of control unit M10 . See E4021 SPEEDOMETER The control unit M10 sends a signal from pin 47 proportional to the engine speed . See E4020 REV COUNTER INSTRUMENT The control unit M10 is connected to the air conditioning system through pins 18 and 60. This makes it possible to adjust the engine idle speed as the load increases each time the compressor is switched on or to switch off the compressor in the case of high engine speed or load conditions . See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins 19, 20, 51 and 52 control the engagement of the relevant fans . See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

Description An electronic management system supervises and governs all engine parameters. It optimises performance and fuel consumption by responding in real time to different service conditions. The Diesel engine is fitted with a COMMON RAIL UNIJET injection system. This features the use of high, electronically-controlled injection pressure. Fuel delivery, termed a pilot injection, is optimised by the electronic control unit via the injector and not managed by the pump. The common rail injection system on this version with 4 valves per cylinder uses MULTIJET technology: i.e. during each engine cycle it carries out more than the usual two injections: it carries out two pre-injections (before the piston is at TDC), one main injection and two post-injections. This solution improves consumption, emissions, quietness and performance because it allows better control of the temperature in the combustion chamber, lowering the maximum value and extending the optimum combustion zone. The system uses signals received from numerous sensors to control actuators. It is connected to the following systems: fuel supply; air supply system; heater plugs; accelerator pedal; engine cooling; fuel preheating. For greater detail, see . Characteristic of working principle 1060 DIESEL FUEL INJECTION Starting from September 2003 Thanks to the electronic management described above, this engine conforms to the latest anti-pollution and continuous control regulations in accordance with the EOBD system (European On Board Diagnosis); The EOBD (European On Board Diagnosis) system carries out continuous diagnosis of the car's petrol fuel system components relating to emissions and indicates any deterioration of these components by the warning light in the instrument panel coming on. The aim of the system is: keeping the efficiency of the system under control; signalling an increase in emissions due to a vehicle malfunction; signalling the need to replace components which have deteriorated. The system is also controlled by means of special relays located in the engine compartment near the battery. The supply lines to the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a specific maxifuse and by other jumper fuses, located in the additional fuse box. The heater plugs are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the battery.

Functional description The engine control unit M10 monitors and controls the entire electronic injection system. The supply for the engine control unit M10 is controlled by the ignition (15/54) at pin 28 by the line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98A. The relay J15 is also supplied by the battery, from the line for maxifuse EFI of B99; pin 91 of control unit M10 sends the signals which energize the relay, which provides the supply to the fuel pump N40, which is connected to earth through the inertia switch I50. In case of impact, this cuts off the circuit to prevent the danger of fuel delivery. Pins 2, 4 and 6 of connector A of M10 are earthed. This makes it possible to adjust the engine idle speed as the load increases each time the compressor is switched on or to switch off the compressor in the case of high engine speed or load conditions . Description The Cruise Control function allows the vehicle to always be driven at a constant speed without pressing the accelerator pedal. The function is managed by the engine control unit which receives a command from the special Cruise Control lever on the left of the steering wheel, under the steering column switch unit. When the function is switched ON, the LED in the lever comes on. When a speed is set (SET +, SET -) it remains memorized and can be recalled at any time (RCL). The function is automatically switched off: by pressing the brake pedal; by pressing the clutch pedal; by placing the lever in N (automatic transmission). When the function is switched OFF, the speed memorized is lost. A warning light on the instrument panel (check module) indicates system activation. For more details, Characteristic of working principle 5580A cruise control system The Cruise Control system has a supply line protected by a fuse in the junction unit which also protects other supplies controlled by the ignition.

Functional description The Cruise Control function is controlled by engine management unit M10 upon a command from the Cruise Control switch H7 located to the left of the steering wheel. The switch H7 is supplied when the ignition is switched on (INT) - pin 3 - from the line protected by the fuse F1 for the junction unit B1. Control H7 is connected to management unit M10: to pin 10 of connector A, with the ON/OFF signal to pin 42 of connector A, with the RES signal to pin 43 of connector A, with the SET + signal to pin 58 of connector A, with the SET - signal The 'pedal released' signal for double switch I30, on the other hand, is sent to the engine management control unit M10 - pin 26 of connector A. For the management of the Cruise Control function the control unit also uses the signal at pin 59 of connector A of M10 coming from the clutch pedal switch I31 and the accelerator pedal potentiometer K55 signals. See E5030 PETROL ENGINE ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT To turn on the Cruise Control warning light, engine management unit M10 sends a signal - pin 1 of connector A - to check module E30 which is supplied by a line protected by fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B.

Description The climate control system with heater unit is controlled by means of three knobs in the control panel in the centre of the dashboard: the left knob mechanically controls the mixture flap between hot air (red) and cold air (blue); the right knob, mechanically operated via a cable, controls the opening of the flaps which regulate the distribution of air flows; the centre knob electrically controls the ventilation of the air at four different speeds: 1, 2, 3 and 4. In position 0, the fan is turned off but air still enters due to the dynamic effect of the car's motion.; when pressed, the left button activates the air recirculation function by an electrical command; when the button is pressed, the relevant LED comes on. If the button is released, "dynamic" air flows in from the outside the right button switches on the heated rear window; when the button is pressed, the relevant LED comes on. ( ). See E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING The control switches have ideograms which are lit up when the side lights are on. For more details, see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5020 HEATER The system is controlled by means of a special relay located in the distributor duct unit. The fan supply lines are protected by a special maxifuse and by the fuse which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition. The fan only operates when the ignition is switched ON.

Functional description The relay J35 controls the heater fan circuit. The supply at the relay contact comes from the battery through the line for the A/C maxifuse up to 2/99 or of B99 from 2/99, while the coil energizing is controlled by the ignition (INT/A) from the line protected by fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. The relay J35 supplies the control knob H81 : this controls the fan at the different speeds through the regulator O30 . The voltage control system varies according to the position of the knob and passes or does not pass through the resistors of the regulator O30 determining the four different voltage signals for the fan N85 which sends outside or recirculation air to the duct/distributor unit at 4 different speeds. The regulator O30 has a thermal contact which protects against dangerous overvoltages. The intake of outside air is controlled by the motor N82 which operates the flap between the two extreme positions of "dynamic air" and "recirculation". The activation of the motor is controlled by the button located in the controls H80 : this switch receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) from the line protected by the fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. and is connected to earth: when the supply and earth are reversed, the motor's direction of rotation is reversed. With the recirculation switched on, the LED in the button for H80 also comes on. The controls unit H80 has ideograms which are lit up when the side lights are on by means of the line coming from the steering column switch unit H5 protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99.

Description The climate control via the heater unit is insufficient when the engine is cold, especially in Diesel engines which are slow to warm up. These engines may optionally be fitted with a supplementary heater system. This remains active from the moment when the engine is turned on until a certain temperature is reached. The system consists of an additional heating device, located on the engine coolant supply pipe to the heater unit. This device contains three spark plugs (similar to those used to preheat the combustion chamber). The operation of the heater plugs is controlled by a special control unit which operates either one, two or three of them giving 200W, 400W or 600W. This control logic depends on: the temperature of the engine coolant; the electrical power available (the battery voltage is checked) the engine speed (which should be above a pre-set value) The supply of one, two or three heater plugs is controlled by two relays: 1. Level: activated by the first relay; 2. Level: activated by the second relay; 3. Level: activated by both relays. There is also a third relay/safety switch which interrupts the heater plugs supply if the contact to earth is not correct: the metal device containing the heater plugs is connected to the engine earth by means of a special loom. For more details, . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5020L additional heater The control unit supply lines are protected by a fuse in the junction unit and by the fuse which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition. The safety relay supply line is protected by a fuse located in the junction unit, whilst the one supplying the resistors is protected by a special maxifuse.

Functional description The additional heater control unit M75 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) at pins 15 and U from the line protected by the fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. The direct supply arrives from the battery (maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99) at pin TL through fuse F10 of junction unit B1 : this signal allows the battery voltage to be checked, i.e. the level of electrical power available. Pin 31 of M75 is earthed. Pin N of M75 receives the engine rpm signal coming from the engine management control unit M10 . Pin TW, on the other hand, is connected to the special temperature sensor K80 which measures the temperature of the coolant near the additional heater. Relays J36 and J37 control the engagement of the resistors O25 . The supply at the contact of the relays arrives from the battery from the line of the specific maxifuse B38 up to 2/99 or from the HEAT maxifuse, located directly on the battery A1 - connector D from 2/99, while the coils are energized by the control unit M75 , which operates only relay J36 to switch on plug O35 A , only relay J37 to switch on plugs O35 B and C, and both relays for all three plugs O35 . The safety relay J38 interrupts the supply of the two above mentioned relays and consequently the heater plugs if the contact to earth is not correct: the coil for J38 is connected on one side to earth and on the other to the metal frame for the device containing the heater plugs: this is connected to the engine earth C1 by means of a special earth loom C41 : if this connection is broken, relay J38 is energized and immediately stops the current supply to the heater plugs.

These engines may optionally be fitted with a supplementary heater system. This remains active from the moment when the engine is turned on until a certain temperature is reached. The system consists of an additional heater, located on the coolant delivery pipe to the heater unit. This device contains three spark plugs (similar to those used to preheat the combustion chamber). The operation of the heater plugs is controlled by a specific control unit which operates either one, two or three of them, thus providing heating of 200 W, 400 W or 600 W. This control logic depends on: the temperature of the engine coolant; the electrical power available (in effect, the battery voltage is checked) the engine speed (which should be above a pre-set value) The supply of one, two or three heater plugs is controlled by two relays: 1. Level: activated by the first relay; 2. Level: activated by the second relay; 3. Level: activated by both relays. There is also a third relay/safety switch which cuts off the heater plugs supply if the contact to earth is not correct: the metal device containing the heater plugs is connected to the engine earth by means of a special loom. For more details, . Characteristic of working principle 5020L additional heater The control unit supply lines are protected by a fuse in the junction unit and by the fuse which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition. The safety relay supply line is protected by a fuse located in the junction unit, whilst the one supplying the resistors is protected by a special maxifuse.

Functional description The additional heater control unit M75 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) at pins 15 and U from the line protected by the fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B . The direct supply arrives from the battery (maxifuse J/B1 of B99 ) at pin TL through fuse F10 of junction unit B1 : this signal allows the battery voltage to be checked, i.e. the level of electrical power available. Pin 31 of M75 is earthed. Pin N of M75 receives the engine rpm signal coming from the engine management control unit M10 . Pin TW, on the other hand, is connected to the special temperature sensor K80 which measures the temperature of the coolant near the additional heater. Relays J36 and J37 control the engagement of the resistors O25 . The supply at the contact of the relays arrives from the battery from the line of the specific HEAT maxifuse, located directly on the battery A1 - connector D, while the coils - supplied by the line protected by F10 of the junction unit B1 - are energized by the control unit M75 , which operates only relay J36 to switch on plug O35 A , only relay J37 to switch on plugs O35 B and C, and both relays for all three plugs O35 . The safety relay J38 cuts off the supply to the two above-mentioned relays and consequently the heater plugs if the contact to earth is not correct. The coil of J38 is connected on one side to earth and on the other side to the metal frame of the device containing the heater plugs: this is connected to the engine earth C1 by means of a special earth loom C41 . If this connection is broken, relay J38 is energized and immediately stops the current supply to the heater plugs.

Description An automatic system manages passenger compartment climate control, i.e. temperature and ventilation with recirculation and air flow orientation. A dedicated control unit manages system operation by controlling: air temperature at outlets; fan speed; compressor activation (air cooling circuit); air recirculation activation; "rapid demisting" function; The control unit sets the above parameters in order to adjust passenger compartment temperature to the required level. The system controls are located outside the control unit housing. The control unit supplies information on interior and exterior temperature via special sensors. After processing the information, it adjusts passenger compartment air intake speed by means of the fan motor and air temperature by means of a mixer actuator. It also controls interior air recirculation via a dedicated actuator. When required, the ECU automatically activates the cooling circuit and dehumidifies the air by operating the air conditioner compressor. ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT For more details, . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The control unit supply lines are protected by a fuse in the junction unit and by the fuse which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition. The fan supply lines are protected by a special maxifuse. The system will only operate when the ignition is turned ON.

Functional description The climate control unit M70 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) at pin 5 of connector B from the line protected by fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99.; the same line also supplies all the actuators of the system. The direct supply arrives from the battery (maxifuse J/B1 of B5 up to 2/99 or B99 from 2/99) at pin 10 of connector B through fuse F10 of junction unit B1 . The supply for illuminating the controls with the side lights on reaches pin 2 of connector B from the line coming from the switch for the steering column switch unit H5 protected by fuse B11 up to 2/99 or fuse F4 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99. Pin 14 of connector A of M70 is earthed. Pin 7 of connector B of M70 receives the speedometer signal coming from instrument E10 , whilst the outside temperature value is signalled from pin 1 of connector A also at instrument E10 . The sensor which measures the outside temperature is located on the right external rear view mirror P61 : the sensor receives a 5 V supply from pin 13 of connector A of M70 and sends the signal to pin 10 of connector A. Control unit M70 is also connected to sensors K87 (lower treated air), K88 (upper treated air) and K89 (passenger compartment air), which receive a 5 V supply from pin 13 of the connector and send signals to pins 11, 10, 9 respectively of connector A of M70 . Sensor K89 is fitted with a fan motor controlled by the ignition so that the temperature reading is not affected by the motionless and thus warmer air inside the dashboard. Functional description The frost sensor K86 receives a 5 V supply from pin 13 of connector A of M70 and sends a signal to pin 5 of connector A, preventing the switching on of the air conditioning if the evaporator temperature is too low. Functional description The air conditioning system is equipped with three activators for recirculation ( N82 ), air mixing ( N81 ) and air distribution ( N80 ). The recirculation actuator N82 is controlled by the control unit M70 from pin 11 of connector B, and there is a current feedback at pin 3 of connector A of M70 . The mixing actuator N81 is controlled by the control unit M70 from pin 6 of connector B, receiving a supply for controlling the potentiometer from pin 2 of connector A and sending a feedback signal to pin 12 of connector B. The distribution actuator N80 is controlled by the control unit M70 from pin 16 of connector A, receiving a supply for controlling the potentiometer from pin 2 of connector A and sending a feedback signal to pin 9 of connector B. The electronic governor M72 operates the fan at different speeds: it receives an input signal from the control unit (from pin 3 of connector B) and transforms it into a variable voltage signal that controls the fan. This voltage control is also stabilized, i.e. it is independent of the battery voltage variations. The governor supply is controlled by the ignition (INT/A) from fuse B10 up to 2/99 or fuse F6 of the additional fuse box B98B from 2/99, is connected to earth and also sends the temperature control signal to pin 4 of connector A of M70 . The fan N85 is supplied directly from the battery through the A/C maxifuse line of B6 , whilst it is controlled at the different speeds for the voltage signal coming from the electronic governor M72 . The control unit M70 is equipped with a self-test system which can be used by connecting the unit to connector R10 : it receives signals from pin 8 of connector B through the diagnostic line. The commands for switching on the heated rear windscreen, the LED and the "rapid demist" function are transmitted to the integrated services control unit M40 by pin 1 of connector B and pins 6 and 8 of connector A, respectively. It should be remembered that the climate control control unit only "houses" the control button and the LED, but does not in any way affect the heated rear windscreen activation logic. ( .) See E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING Pin 7 of connector A controls the activation of the compressor ( ). See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT
